primary_reviews.rationale: Both edges of this row survive inspection of the pointed text. MT 1:6 runs inside the narrative wayyiqtol chain (וַיַּעַל֩ שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה ... וַיַּ֧עַל עָלָ֛יו עֹל֖וֹת אָֽלֶף), and MT 1:7 does not continue that chain: it fronts the adverbial בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא ahead of the qatal נִרְאָ֥ה, an X-qatal construction whose whole function is to step out of the sequence. The row's word 'disjunction' is therefore demonstrable morphology rather than an impression, and it belongs to the tier-1 time-frame class. Its three Hebrew quotes (MT 1:1, 1:6, 1:7) collate byte-exact and each has a matching oshb ref in the array. Every English parenthetical here that carries an inline web: ref reproduces the WEB witness verbatim, which I checked string by string. The span lies wholly outside offset zone A, which opens only at WEB 2:1 = MT 1:18, so the single-number oshb refs are the right form. The one mark nearby, a SAMEKH after MT 1:10 (single-witness), falls inside the next row and is tier-3 in Writings either way; its non-citation here is correct handling, not an omission.

The accession formula וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֛ק שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בֶן דָּוִ֖יד עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ does open oshb:2Chr.1.1 exactly as quoted, and the sacrifice-count close וַיַּ֧עַל עָלָ֛יו עֹל֖וֹת אָֽלֶף does end oshb:2Chr.1.6 exactly as quoted; I sliced both lines from 2Chr_oshb.txt and they match byte for byte. The pivot into בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא at 1.7 is a real time-frame disjunction (device-matrix tier-1), and nothing in WEB 1.2-1.6 interrupts the single cultic-assembly action the row describes, so the six-verse span reads as one coherent opening notice rather than an arbitrary chapter-following slice.

primary_reviews.rationale: The close itself is safe. MT 1:13's וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל collates byte-exact, the return notice moves the scene bodily from the Gibeon high place to Jerusalem, and the mark cite is accurate: pmarks_2Chr.json carries '2Chr.1.13': 'PE' (single-witness), sitting at the span's last verse in MT numbering. The SAMEKH after MT 1:10 lies uncited inside the span, which is the right call, since in Writings it could neither drive an internal split nor count against one. What does not survive a sweep is the envelope reasoning. עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ is unique to MT 1:1 across the book, but v.13 does not repeat that phrase; the only shared element is the mlk root, and the malkut noun itself reappears immediately past the claimed bracket. So the seam holds while the argument offered for it does not carry the weight the row assigns.

challenges.claim: The row holds that MT 1:13's וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל 'answers the opening עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ of web:2Chr.1.1/oshb:2Chr.1.1, bracketing the whole Gibeon episode with the same kingship root'. A book-wide sweep of 2Chr_oshb.txt shows the repetend does not stop at the claimed bracket: the malkut noun recurs at oshb:2Chr.1.18 (לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ, = web:2Chr.2.1) and again at oshb:2Chr.3.2 (לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ), i.e. in each of the two units that follow. The exact phrase עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ occurs once only (oshb:2Chr.1.1) and is not the phrase v.13 uses. Tier-1 inclusio needs a repetend that marks the edges; a root that runs straight on through the next two pericopes cannot demarcate the one it supposedly closes.
challenges.suggested_action: Demote the mlk-root envelope to a passing observation and let the v.13 close rest on the tier-1 return notice (Gibeon high place to Jerusalem) the row already supplies. If the envelope is kept, state the oshb:2Chr.1.18 and oshb:2Chr.3.2 recurrences in the rationale and mirror them into boundary_evidence_refs so the claim is bounded by its own counter-instances.

primary_reviews.rationale: The dialogue is genuinely self-contained: invitation (1.7), petition (1.8-1.10), grant (1.11-1.12), and the return-and-reign notice at 1.13 that the row reads as answering 1.1's kingship language. I checked the claimed relationship carefully — 1.1 has the noun מַלְכוּת֑וֹ and 1.13 has the verb וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ, and the row is careful to call this a shared root rather than a repeated phrase, which is the accurate description; overclaiming a verbatim echo here would have been the wrong move, and the row avoids it.

The cure lands, and my own sweep leaves the row's conclusion safer than it claims: consonantal מלכות stands in 22 verses of 2Chr — 1:1, 1:18, 2:11, 3:2 and eighteen more running out to 36:22-23 — while the wayyiqtol of the same root recurs in 21, so a repetend of that density could never demarcate 1:1-1:13, and the row is right to let no inclusio rest on it. One in-block instance it does not name, וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ at web:2Chr.2.12 = oshb:2Chr.2.11 (MT), sits inside the Solomon correspondence itself. Both edges are textually secure: the nocturnal-theophany opening of 1:7 and the return-and-reign clause וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל collate byte-exact, and 1:14's וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ turns to an unrelated inventory. Two residual problems remain, both small. The noun is called a root, and the samekh standing after MT 1:10 falls inside this span at the hinge between petition and answer (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֣ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֡ה) without any disclosure, even though the pe after v.13 is cited as corroboration for the close — the same one-directional use of the mark apparatus that was filed and repaired at rows 011 and 012 of this cluster. Noted without filing: the précis cites web:2Chr.1.8-1.10 for a petition of wisdom 'over riches, honor, or long life', but those three items are enumerated only in God's reply at 1:11.

challenges.claim: The rewritten sentence begins 'The מלכות root of v.13's closing clause, וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, shares its root with v.1's עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ'. מלכות is not a root: it is an abstract noun in -ut built on the triliteral מלך, and v.13's verb is a qal wayyiqtol of that root. primary_reviews.rationale: The repetition this row leans on is real and, importantly, its hedge is honest. Laid side by side, MT 2:1 and MT 2:17 share the three figures and most of the wording but are not identical: MT 2:1 spells the second number plene (וּשְׁמוֹנִ֥ים) where MT 2:17 is defective (וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים), and MT 2:1 has אִ֣ישׁ סַבָּ֔ל and אִ֖ישׁ חֹצֵ֣ב where MT 2:17 has bare סַבָּ֔ל and חֹצֵ֣ב. 'Almost verbatim' is thus the accurate description and not an overstatement. The verb echo is exact lexically and correctly quoted at both accentual variants, וַיִּסְפֹּ֨ר at MT 2:1 against וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר at MT 2:16, both qal wayyiqtol 3ms of the spr root. The row is also careful where slipping would be easy: it marks oshb:2Chr.3.1 as lying outside the offset zone, which is right, since zone A terminates at WEB 2:18 = MT 2:17 and chapter 3 is numbered alike in both witnesses. No mark is claimed after MT 2:17 and pmarks records none there — correct restraint rather than an oversight.

Two independent signals converge at this close: the near-verbatim repetition of the 70,000/80,000/3,600 figures from the opening census, and the shared verb form וַיִּסְפֹּר that opens both the census (2.2 WEB) and this row's bridge verse (2.17 WEB) — I confirmed both forms are the same Qal wayyiqtol of ספר, differing only in cantillation, which the row correctly calls the same verb rather than merely a similar one. The pivot to וַיָּ֣חֶל at 3.1 is a genuinely different act-verb and closes the pericope cleanly.

primary_reviews.rationale: I re-ran the row's programmatic claim rather than take it on trust, and it holds exactly: searching the consonantal skeleton of וַיָּ֣חֶל across the forty verses MT 3:1-5:1 returns oshb:2Chr.3.1 (וַיָּ֣חֶל) and oshb:2Chr.3.2 (וַ֠יָּחֶל) and nothing else. Book-wide the same skeleton also surfaces at oshb:2Chr.16.12 (וַיֶּחֱלֶ֣א, a different root) and oshb:2Chr.29.17 (וַ֠יָּחֵלּוּ, the same hll hiphil but plural), each outside the range the row scopes, so the claim as worded is exact and the two accentual variants are properly not conflated. The list-header reading of MT 3:3 is sound in form too: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ opening a measurement series is a register formula, categorically unlike the narrative inceptive before it, which is enough to seat the boundary between v.2 and v.3. The defect lies in the gloss, not the seam.

challenges.claim: MT 3:3's וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת בֵּ֣ית is glossed 'and these [are what] Solomon founded for building the house of...', which renders הוּסַ֣ד as an active verb governing Solomon as agent. הוּסַ֣ד is a Hophal perfect 3ms of the ysd root, a passive form ('was founded/laid'); it is not active, and treating שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה as its agentive subject is precisely the crux of the clause rather than a reading that can be assumed. That WEB at web:2Chr.3.3 has to reorganise the syntax to render it ('Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid') is itself evidence of the difficulty, not a licence to state the active.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword the gloss so it does not silently convert the Hophal to an active — for instance 'and these are [the foundations] laid for Solomon's building of the house of God' — or flag the clause's voice as contested. No repair is needed to the boundary, which rests on the וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ list-opening formula and is untouched by the voice question.

primary_reviews.rationale: I re-ran the row's own programmatic claim rather than taking it on faith: scanning every oshb line from 2Chr.3.1 through 2Chr.5.1, the inceptive verb וַיָּחֶל/וַ֠יָּחֶל appears only at 3.1 and 3.2, nowhere else in that range (5.1 opens instead on וַתִּשְׁלַם, the completion formula for a different, later boundary). That confirms the doubled-inception frame the row describes is real and not an artifact of selective quoting. The pivot to the list-header וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד at 3.3 is a distinct formula type from the narrative inceptive, and the row's rejected alternative honestly grants that grouping 3.1-3.3 is at least plausible before explaining why the genre shift still wins.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative answers only the maximal merge and leaves the panel's formally strongest internal rival untouched: a cleavage at 6:23/6:24 (tier-1 form evidence). The oath case is individual and judicial -- protasis אִם יֶחֱטָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ, apodosis וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ וְשָׁפַטְתָּ֣ אֶת עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ לְהָשִׁ֣יב לְרָשָׁ֔ע לָתֵ֥ת דַּרְכּ֖וֹ בְּרֹאשׁ֑וֹ וּלְהַצְדִּ֣יק צַדִּ֔יק -- and grants no forgiveness, whereas the three petitions that follow are national and share tissue the oath case entirely lacks: 6:24 and 6:26 each carry a sin-clause that is byte-identical between them down to the accents, כִּ֣י יֶֽחֶטְאוּ לָ֑ךְ, and 6:25, 6:27, 6:30 resolve with the forgiveness verb. A panel of 6:24-31 is thus held together by shared formulae that stop at 6:23, which is a stronger rival than treating 6:22-39 as one undifferentiated catalog.

primary_reviews.rationale: Four citations, four exact matches; three are verse-initial and the closing forgiveness clause is verse-final in 6:39 (119-165 of 165), so the panel's stated edges are textually where the row places them. The pivot at 6:32 and the register change at 6:40 both hold, and I do not contest the span. Two supporting assertions inside the rationale do not survive checking, however. One is an exclusivity claim about the climactic case's embedded generalization, which a read of the first panel refutes. The other is a comparative-length claim that measurement contradicts. Neither is a marker question -- pmarks_2Chr.json records nothing at 6:39 and the row rightly claims nothing there -- and neither involves the offset zones, which lie well outside chapter 6. I flag them separately because they call for different repairs.

challenges.claim: 'the only one carrying its own universalizing parenthetical' is false on the Hebrew (tier-1). The famine-and-siege case in the first panel already carries one: 6:30 ends with כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ לְבַדְּךָ֣ יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת לְבַ֖ב בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם, a subordinate clause generalizing about the heart of all mankind, and it is formally the twin of the clause the row calls unique at 6:36, כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין אָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא יֶחֱטָ֔א. Both are introduced by the same subordinator, both interrupt a petition to state a truth about people in general, and both hinge on the same noun for humanity. 6:29 widens the same case to all mankind a verse earlier still. The captivity petition's parenthetical is therefore the second of its kind in the prayer, not the only one.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the exclusivity wording, or restate it as the only universalizing clause that sits inside a case's own protasis. Register oshb:2Chr.6.29 and oshb:2Chr.6.30 as refs so this comparandum stops being invisible.

challenges.claim: 'markedly longer than the earlier cases' is not borne out by measurement. Counting consonantal characters in 2Chr_oshb.txt with cantillation and spaces removed, the seven cases run: oath 6:22-23 = 126, defeat 6:24-25 = 138, drought 6:26-27 = 167, famine and siege 6:28-31 = 299, foreigner 6:32-33 = 211, battle 6:34-35 = 119, captivity 6:36-39 = 304. The captivity case exceeds four of the six but sits within two percent of the famine-and-siege case that precedes it, so comparative length cannot carry the climactic weight the row assigns it.
challenges.suggested_action: Rest the climactic reading on what is genuinely distinctive, namely the exile-and-return sequence at 6:37-38 that no other case has, and either retire the length premise or record oshb:2Chr.6.28 as a ref so a downstream checker can redo the count.

primary_reviews.rationale: The three-case progression (foreigner, battle-abroad, captivity) is accurately described, and the claim that v36's 'for there is no man who doesn't sin' is the series' only universalizing parenthetical holds up -- none of the other cases in either this panel or the preceding one carries a comparable general maxim. The v40 register shift to direct second-person plea, picking up v20's 'eyes...open' language, is a legitimate closing signal for the whole series rather than an eighth case. Unlike the previous panel, there is no internal mark evidence here to weigh either for or against finer splitting, which is itself consistent with treating 32-39 as one continuous build toward the exile climax rather than a marked sequence of discrete units.

Both objections are met, and the arithmetic that survives is sound: my own count of the two cases returns the same two numbers the row prints, and the difference is indeed under two percent. The parenthetical exclusivity is properly abandoned with the competing clause quoted. In place of the two retired warrants, though, the row installs a third exclusivity claim, and this one is refuted from inside its own span -- the battle petition at v34 already sends the people to pray directionally toward the chosen city and the built house, in wording that ends identically to v38's, and the turning-and-restoration half is already carried by the defeat case in the previous panel. Separately, the plea quoted from v40 is not what WEB prints, and what was removed is the particle the register argument depends on.

challenges.claim: The third exclusivity claim fares no better than the two withdrawn ones. "The exile-and-return sequence unique to it, vv37-38's turning of heart in the land of captivity and prayer toward their land, the city, and the house -- the only such sequence the prayer's petition series carries" is contradicted from within this row's own span: 6:34 reads וְהִתְפַּֽלְל֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתָּ בָּ֔הּ וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֥יתִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ against 6:38's וְהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֗וּ דֶּ֤רֶךְ אַרְצָם֙ ... וְהָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֔רְתָּ וְלַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֥יתִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ, the closing three words byte-identical and the city clause differing only by a demonstrative and a resumptive pronoun. The turning-and-restoration element is likewise not new here: the defeat case pairs 6:24's וְשָׁ֨בוּ֙ with 6:25's וַהֲשֵׁיבוֹתָם֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה (WEB: "bring them again to the land which you gave to them").

primary_reviews.rationale: Quote fidelity and mark accuracy are both fine here. The four citations match byte for byte; 6:40 is quoted in full, the 6:42 clause is verse-final (52-92 of 92), and the 7:1 temporal clause opens its verse. pmarks_2Chr.json confirms SAMEKH at 2Chr.6.40 and PE at 2Chr.6.42, both cited with the single-witness label, and the row is right in principle that a Writings mark cannot drive an edge. The problem is that the tier-1 argument offered in the mark's place points the other way once the particle is checked against its own environment. Verse-initial usage of the linking adverb in this prayer is a pivot device, not a binding one, and the two verses the row wants to attach differ from 6:40 in divine appellation and in verbal mood. That makes the rejected alternative better founded than the row allows, and it is not a marker-only objection, so it is not disqualified as insufficient_evidence. The medium_low grade at least registers the difficulty, and the strategy's own list of shaky regions names this seam.

challenges.claim: The row's sole tier-1 counterweight to the SAMEKH is the adverbial chain from 6:40 into 6:41, but the prayer's own usage inverts that reading. A book-wide pass over 2Chr_oshb.txt counting where the linking adverb stands first in its verse yields fifteen addresses, three inside this prayer: 6:16 (וְעַתָּ֞ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁ֠מֹר לְעַבְדְּךָ֨ דָוִ֤יד אָבִי֙), 6:17 (וְעַתָּ֕ה יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יֵֽאָמֵן֙ דְּבָ֣רְךָ֔) and 6:41 (וְעַתָּ֗ה קוּמָ֞ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְֽנוּחֶ֔ךָ). At 6:16 and 6:17 it pivots away from the historical recital into a fresh petition -- precisely the dynastic movement that M8-2Chr-021 identifies as a distinct beat -- so in this prayer the particle opens appeals rather than binding a verse to what precedes it. Two further shifts, independent of any mark, reinforce a seam at 6:40/6:41: the divine address changes from the first-person-suffixed form at 6:40 (אֱלֹהַ֗י) to the compound name at 6:41 and 6:42 (יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙), and the mood changes from jussive with the particle of entreaty (יִֽהְיוּ נָ֤א) to a run of imperatives (קוּמָ֞ה, אַל תָּשֵׁ֖ב, זָכְרָ֕ה). That is the same register distinction M8-2Chr-023 invokes to stop panel two at 6:39.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-argue the 6:40/6:41 seam on the appellation and mood evidence rather than framing the rival as mark-following: either separate 6:40 from 6:41-42 or state why the register shift is subordinate to the adverbial link. Enter oshb:2Chr.6.16 and oshb:2Chr.6.17 in the refs array, since those are the in-prayer comparanda for the particle.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row does the discipline right: it names the samekh after v40 as a live counter-signal and then argues past it with a specific tier-1 observation -- the עַתָּה/וְעַתָּה adverbial chain linking v40's plea to v41's invocation -- rather than quietly ignoring the mark or leaning on it. That is exactly how tier-3 evidence should be handled per the evidence rules: disclosed, weighed, and subordinated to the textual argument. The medium_low confidence is honest given that a scribal tradition did see fit to break at v40, even though the syntax argues otherwise. 7:1's completion clause 'when Solomon had finished praying' is an unambiguous scene-closing formula for the right edge.

Two repaired observations survive independent testing. Sweeping 2Chr_oshb.txt for the temporal particle across 6:14-42 returns exactly four tokens, every one of them verse-initial, at 6:16, 6:17, 6:40 and 6:41, with nothing mid-verse anywhere in the prayer; so the row's contrast between the bare form at 6:40 and the conjunctive form elsewhere in the prayer is exhaustive, not cherry-picked. The appellation pair also checks out byte-for-byte, עַתָּ֣ה carrying the first-person suffix at 6:40 against the compound divine name at 6:41 and 6:42, as does the shift from jussive-plus-entreaty into a bare imperative run. The trouble lies underneath those observations. The repair advertised a book-wide sweep it never reports, and it leaned the same point on what a sibling row does with 6:16-17; and it installed 7:1 as the row's anchor without noticing that the same frame is silent about the 6:39|6:40 edge on which this span opens.

The remaining twelve stand at MT 2:6 (= WEB 2:7), MT 2:12 (= WEB 2:13), MT 2:14 (= WEB 2:15), 7:16 (וְעַתָּ֗ה), 10:11, 13:8, 18:22, 19:7 (וְעַתָּ֕ה), 20:10, 28:10, 28:11 and 32:15, and none is named. primary_reviews.rationale: The revised row is now honest about the strength of its own rival: it concedes the appellation/mood shift at 6:41 is 'the genuinely stronger rival' rather than dismissing it as mark-following, and declines the split only because 7:1's retrospective 'finished praying' frame never distinguishes an entreaty phase from an imperative phase. That is a real argument, not airtight, but the medium_low grade matches its own admitted weakness. No fresh defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This is the cluster's clearest primary-versus-primary disagreement, and OL's evidence wins it. LF's review praises the row's handling of the SAMEKH after 6:40 as textbook tier-3 discipline -- disclosed, then argued past by a tier-1 chain -- without testing whether that chain actually holds, and on inspection it does not hold as stated. Rerunning OL's book-wide sweep for verse-initial וְעַתָּה (the vav-prefixed form, distinct from the bare עַתָּה that opens v40 itself) gives the identical count: fifteen occurrences total, three inside this prayer at 6:16, 6:17, and 6:41. At 6:16 and 6:17 the particle demonstrably pivots away from the preceding recital into a fresh petition, the same dynastic request the row's own text labels a separate component earlier in this cluster -- which means its usage elsewhere in this very prayer argues that 6:41's וְעַתָּה opens a new appeal rather than binding backward to 6:40's plea. Two further, mark-independent shifts corroborate a seam at 6:40/6:41: the divine address changes from the first-person-suffixed אֱלֹהַ֗י at 6:40 to the compound יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ at 6:41-42, and the mood shifts from jussive-plus-entreaty (יִֽהְיוּ נָ֤א) to a run of bare imperatives (קוּמָ֞ה, אַל תָּשֵׁ֖ב, זָכְרָ֕ה). None of this rests on the mark itself -- it is built entirely from appellation, mood, and the particle's own distribution -- so it clears the bar against marker-only grounds and gives the SAMEKH's rival reading real tier-1 support that the row's counter-argument doesn't actually supply. The medium_low confidence already registers real difficulty here; whether the 6.40-6.42 span itself should be revisited is for the author/boss round.

challenge_responses.response: Accepted. The adverbial-chain counter-argument is withdrawn: the same vav-prefixed וְעַתָּ֞ה form pivots to fresh petitions at 6:16-17 rather than reliably binding backward, so it cannot by itself refute the SAMEKH's rival reading. The rationale is rebuilt around the appellation shift (אֱלֹהַ֗י to יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙) and mood shift (jussive-entreaty to imperative) as a genuine intensification, and rests the case for keeping 40-42 together on 7:1's own retrospective frame, which treats the whole prayer (6:14-42) as one undifferentiated act without distinguishing an entreaty phase from an imperative phase. Confidence stays at medium_low, matching book_strategy_draft.md §6's own listing of '6:40-42→7:1' among the campaign's expected low-confidence regions; the boss round should treat the 6:40/6:41 seam as a live, evidence-backed rival, not a settled question.

primary_reviews.rationale: Four Hebrew runs sit in this row and all four reproduce their source consonants, points and accents without deviation: the 7:1 string running from the temporal frame down to “הָעֹלָ֖ה”, the 7:2 priests-clause, “וְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל” at the head of 7:3, and the 7:3 doxology. The row's one universal claim is the interesting part, and it survives. Reducing all 821 MT lines to consonants and searching for the full refrain (“כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ”) returns exactly two addresses in this book, 5:13 and 7:3, while the truncated form lacking “כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב” turns up additionally at 7:6 and 20:21. So “the second and only other instance of the full refrain” is demonstrated rather than asserted, and the 5:13/7:3 pairing that §4 licenses as in-book evidence is real. Numbering holds no trap here: MT and WEB both run 42 verses in chapter 6 and 22 in chapter 7, so this row sits wholly outside the two dual-cite zones and its single-numbered refs are correct. One evidence-hygiene note aimed at the mesh rather than the writer — the English refrain the row quotes does not appear in 2Chr_web_clean.txt, which drops WEB's poetic lines; it is in 2Chr_web.usfm as \q1/\q2 at 5:13 and again at 7:3. That is tier-4 markup and I leaned on none of it; the Hebrew carries the refrain unaided. Where I part company with the row is the closing edge, which rests entirely on v4 turning “to a new subject and action.” The Hebrew will not bear that weight.

challenges.claim: Tier 1 (syntax and participant tracking). Verse 4 is “וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֑ם זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה” — waw plus a fronted compound subject plus the masculine-plural participle “זֹבְחִ֥ים”. That is a circumstantial or summarising clause, the weakest available form of narrative onset; the first wayyiqtol actually advancing the sacrificial action is v5's “וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֮”. Nor do the participants change: v3's “וְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל” and v4's “וְכָל הָעָ֑ם” are one congregation with the king added, not a new cast. The closing warrant therefore rests on a clause type that ordinarily continues a scene rather than opening one, while the row is graded high over a three-verse span inside the dedication complex that book_strategy_draft.md §5 says “must not be over-split” and against a §7 target near six or seven verses per decision.
challenges.suggested_action: Rebuild the v3/v4 argument on a signal the Hebrew actually supplies — the closed doxology answering 5:13, which this row has already verified book-wide — instead of a claimed subject-and-action change at v4, or lower the grade to medium. Should the mesh prefer to price a rival span, the one worth testing is 7:1-5, where the participial v4 heads the sacrifice report that v5's wayyiqtol specifies.

primary_reviews.rationale: The 7:1 opening stands on a genuine completion-formula hinge -- וּכְכַלּוֹת שְׁלֹמֹה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל belongs to the same וּכְ + infinitive-of-כלה family the strategy already verifies at 31:1, so treating it as a fresh scene-opener rather than a bare continuation of chapter 6's prayer is textually grounded, not merely asserted. The v1-v2 doubled glory notice and the v3 refrain both quote byte-true from 2Chr_oshb.txt, and the v3/v4 handoff to 'the king and all the people' offering sacrifice is a clean subject-and-verb-form change. The claim that 7:3 and 5:13 are the only two instances of the full doxology in the book held up under an independent sweep of every טוֹב occurrence and every לעולם חסדו occurrence in 2Chr_oshb.txt (5 and 3 hits respectively); only 5:13 and 7:3 carry both clauses together, while 7:6 and 20:21 each preserve the lovingkindness half alone, without כי טוב.

challenges.claim: The rationale asserts the full-refrain uniqueness claim is 'per the book-wide check run above,' but no such check or its residue (e.g. the near-miss partial forms at 7:6 and 20:21 that a real sweep would have to rule out) appears anywhere in this row's boundary_evidence_refs, so the claim is not verifiable from the frozen row alone.
challenges.suggested_action: Either mirror the disambiguating near-miss refs (web/oshb 2Chr.7.6, 2Chr.20.21) into boundary_evidence_refs, or drop the 'check run above' phrasing and state the sweep's scope and result inline.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every quantitative claim the repair introduced holds under independent consonantal sweep of 2Chr_oshb.txt. The two-clause refrain occurs at 5:13 and 7:3 and at no third address; the truncated form lacking the first clause adds exactly 7:6 and 20:21; and the opening clause on its own is confined to the same two full-refrain verses, so "neither a third instance of the full pair" is accurate in both directions. The morphological concession about v4 is likewise right: the verse fronts a compound subject before a masculine-plural participle, and the wayyiqtol that moves the sacrifice forward is v5's. With the boundary now carried by a closing signal that is verifiable book-wide rather than by an asserted change of cast, the high grade is earned. One observation I record without filing: WEB sets the doxology as verse at both 5:13 and 7:3, reading it with an initial capital and a terminal exclamation, where the row lowercases and drops the final mark -- the wording is otherwise identical at the two verses, so the bracket itself is genuine.

Both cures are clean. The row now states plainly that the v3/v4 edge rests on the 5:13/7:3 doxology bracket, 'not any change of subject at v4,' demoting the participial-clause description to background rather than a boundary warrant, and the refrain-uniqueness claim now carries its own disambiguating refs. No new defect found in the revised argument.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both challenges verify independently. LF-025-1's refs-gap point is confirmed by my own consonantal sweep of every line in 2Chr_oshb.txt: the full doxology (וְהוֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ) lands only at 5:13 and 7:3, while the truncated form lacking כי טוב surfaces additionally at 7:6 and 20:21 -- exactly the near-miss pair the row's 'check run above' phrase gestures at without citing; neither verse sits in boundary_evidence_refs, so the uniqueness claim is true but unverifiable from the frozen row alone, matching LF's point precisely. OL-025-1's grammatical challenge also checks out: v4 (וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֑ם זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה) is a waw-plus-fronted-subject participial clause -- background/circumstantial in Biblical Hebrew narrative grammar, the participle זֹבְחִ֥ים continuing rather than advancing the scene -- not the wayyiqtol that actually moves the sacrifice forward (v5's וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֮); and v3's 'וְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל' plus v4's 'וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֑ם' name one congregation with the king added, not a new cast. The row's 'new subject and action' warrant is overstated as OL says. Neither correction disturbs the v3/v4 seam itself, which the row's stronger, independently-verified evidence (the 5:13/7:3 refrain bracket closing exactly at v3) already secures without leaning on the disputed v4 language -- but the stated rationale needs rebuilding around that bracket, and whether 'high' confidence survives once the shaky warrant is removed is a live question for the author/boss round, not something I can adjudicate here.

challenge_responses.response: Accepted. The disambiguating near-miss verses (7:6, 20:21, both truncated forms lacking 'for he is good') are now stated inline with the sweep's method and result, and mirrored into boundary_evidence_refs, so the uniqueness claim is verifiable from the frozen row alone.

Accepted. v4 is a circumstantial waw-plus-participle clause, not the advancing wayyiqtol (that is v5's וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח), and its cast (king added to v3's assembly) is not new; the v3/v4 warrant is rebuilt to rest on the independently-verified 5:13/7:3 refrain bracket alone. primary_reviews.rationale: Six Hebrew strings appear here and each matched its verse exactly under byte comparison. The closing device is genuine rather than a workaday verb: reduced to consonants, this completion verb stands in only two places in the entire book, 4:11 (“וַיְכַ֣ל חירם חוּרָ֗ם”, of Huram) and 7:11 (“וַיְכַ֧ל”, of Solomon), both of them closing notices, so resting the end of the unit on v11 is lexically well grounded. The next unit's opening is equally firm, since “וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה” changes verb-type, agent and time-of-day in a single clause. On the paragraph witness I read pmarks_2Chr.json as giving PE after 7:11, which is the type the row states, and the row rightly treats it as one small vote rather than a driver. WEB agrees with the glosses at vv10-11, and MT and WEB run in step across both chapters, so no dual-cite obligation arises. One observation I deliberately do not raise to a challenge: the row's flat verdict “not a spoken cry” is firmer than the syntax warrants, because “לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ בְּהַלֵּ֥ל דָּוִ֖יד בְּיָדָ֑ם” sets the short doxology between the purpose infinitive “לְהֹד֤וֹת” and “בְּהַלֵּ֥ל דָּוִ֖יד בְּיָדָ֑ם”, and WEB reads it as direct speech — but the refrain contrast the row is drawing survives either construal, since v6 lacks “כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב” whichever way the clause is parsed. Two smaller defects do warrant challenges.

challenges.claim: Refs gap measured against book_strategy_draft.md §7, which requires every argued comparandum to be mirrored into boundary_evidence_refs. The rationale quotes Hebrew out of 7:6 — “לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ בְּהַלֵּ֥ל דָּוִ֖יד בְּיָדָ֑ם” — and argues it as the foil to the full 5:13 and 7:3 refrain, yet boundary_evidence_refs holds neither oshb:2Chr.7.6 nor web:2Chr.7.6. An original-language claim is being made from a verse the row never cites.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Chr.7.6 and web:2Chr.7.6 to boundary_evidence_refs.

The row cites the paragraph break after v11 as “one more small vote,” but its span quietly encloses two further single-witness marks that the mark file records inside it, a SAMEKH after 7:4 and a SAMEKH after 7:6, neither disclosed. primary_reviews.rationale: Each of the four evidentiary anchors here checks out: the v4 subject-verb pairing genuinely breaks from v3's congregational doxology, the v6 instrument description quotes the short single-clause echo (לְהֹדוֹת לַיהוָה כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ) accurately and rightly distinguishes it from the fuller v3/5:13 refrain rather than conflating the two, the v10 dismissal date and v11 completion formula both match 2Chr_oshb.txt verbatim, and the v11 PE mark is correctly labeled single-witness and correctly kept from doing any of the row's actual boundary work. The v12 'appeared ... by night' opening is a strong, independent scene-changing formula, so the rejected alternative (folding v12 in as a capstone) is a real rival fairly stated and fairly beaten.

The disclosure repair worked and the closing edge is well made: the completion formula at 7:11 answers building language that runs back through the whole complex, and 7:12's night-theophany formula changes time, mode and initiative, so the seam stands without any help from the mark file -- which is what the row itself says. Two smaller defects rode in with the repair. The festival arithmetic in the middle of the span is folded into a shape 7:9 does not have, and the newly written disclosure sentence sorts the 7:11 PE in with the two genuinely span-internal marks, collapsing the very internal-versus-edge distinction the original challenge was raised to establish. Neither moves the boundary; both would propagate downstream as stated.

challenges.claim: "the seven-plus-seven day feast (vv8-9)" welds together two observances the Hebrew keeps apart, and the row cites neither verse. 7:8 gives the festival by itself seven days -- וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אֶת הֶ֠חָג בָּעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ -- and 7:9 supplies the second seven as the altar dedication rather than a second festival week: כִּ֣י חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ עָשׂוּ֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וְהֶחָ֖ג שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים. The same verse opens on the eighth-day assembly, וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֛וּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י עֲצָ֑רֶת, which the summary omits altogether even though that assembly is what bridges the two weeks to the dismissal on the twenty-third day in v10. Nothing in boundary_evidence_refs covers 7:8 or 7:9, so span content the rationale argues is uncited on both witnesses.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast as a dedication week plus a festival week closed by the eighth-day assembly, and mirror oshb:2Chr.7.8, web:2Chr.7.8, oshb:2Chr.7.9 and web:2Chr.7.9 into boundary_evidence_refs.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every one of the six Hebrew runs in this row is faithful to its source line. The row's best piece of evidence is one it does not fully cash: 7:18's “לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל” picks up 6:16's “לֹא יִכָּרֵ֨ת לְךָ֥ אִישׁ֙ מִלְּפָנַ֔י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל”, and stripped of pointing the two share the string behind “לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ” verbatim, so the claim that the oracle answers Solomon's dynastic plea is checkable, in-book, and admissible under §4. There is no offset to negotiate, MT and WEB both counting 22 verses in chapter 7, and the paragraph file records nothing between the PE at 7:11 and the PE at 7:22 (both single-witness), so not one mark falls inside this span and no tier-3 question touches it either way. The opening at v12 stands on its own terms. What I cannot confirm is the row's account of what binds the span and what divides it from the next: the claimed mirror at v17 and v19 is not a mirror in the Hebrew, and four verses in the middle are never argued at all.

challenges.claim: Two argued comparanda are absent from boundary_evidence_refs although §7 requires them mirrored: the Gibeon theophany the row invokes (2Chr 1:7) and the dynastic plea it says the oracle answers (2Chr 6:16). The Gibeon comparison is additionally overstated as “the same appeared formula”. 1:7 reads “בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה” — niphal perfect, subject “אֱלֹהִ֖ים”, addressee marked by lamed — whereas 7:12 reads “וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה” — niphal wayyiqtol, subject “יְהוָ֛ה”, addressee marked by “אֶל”. Shared root and stem, three differing slots: that is a shared lexeme, not a shared formula.
challenges.suggested_action: Mirror oshb:2Chr.1.7 and oshb:2Chr.6.16 with their WEB counterparts into boundary_evidence_refs, and downgrade the Gibeon wording from a shared formula to a shared niphal of the root r-'-h with the differences named. The 6:16 link is strong enough to carry what the 1:7 link is being asked to bear.

challenges.claim: Tier 1 (verbal morphology). The seam is made to turn on v19 mirroring v17, “a deliberate contrast to v17's ‘if you will walk’.” Yet v17 is second masculine singular start to finish (תֵּלֵ֣ךְ / צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ / תִּשְׁמֽוֹר), spoken to Solomon, while v19 is second masculine plural (תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם / וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙ / וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם) and its apodosis in v20 turns third plural (“וּנְתַשְׁתִּ֗ים מֵעַ֤ל”, “I will uproot them”). The two conditionals do not share an addressee, so they are not antithetical twins; v19 swings from the king to the nation. The seam may well be better supported than the row claims, but not for the reason given, and a frozen rationale that misstates the morphology propagates downstream.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the v18/v19 argument as an addressee shift — a singular royal conditional giving way to a plural national conditional with third-plural consequences — quoting the verbal forms, rather than as a positive-negative mirror addressed to one hearer.

challenges.claim: Unargued internal tier-1 material. The rationale leaps from v12 to v17 and leaves vv13-16 undiscussed, though they hold a complete protasis-apodosis — the brief's own tier-1 device class — running from “הֵ֣ן אֶֽעֱצֹ֤ר הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙”, extended by “וְהֵן” and “וְאִם”, into “וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י”, with deictic pivots at “עַתָּ֗ה” in v15 and “וְעַתָּ֗ה” in v16. Those verses also speak to the plural nation, aligning them with v19 rather than v17, so the span as drawn welds two addressee registers together without saying so.
challenges.suggested_action: Argue vv13-16 explicitly, either as a national conditional held inside the ratification frame or as a candidate internal seam, and use rejected_alternative to say why the plural block at 13-14 stays joined to the singular block at 17-18.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening and both named echoes are real: וַיֵּרָא יְהוָה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹה בַּלָּיְלָה does share its ראה-niphal-plus-night pattern with the Gibeon notice at 1:7 (נִרְאָה אֱלֹהִים לִשְׁלֹמֹה ... בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא), and v18's לֹא יִכָּרֵת לְךָ אִישׁ ... בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל does answer 6:16's petition in nearly identical words -- confirmed by pulling both cited verses directly from 2Chr_oshb.txt. Neither comparandum, though, is mirrored into this row's boundary_evidence_refs, which is exactly the omission the strategy's granularity section warns against.

challenges.claim: The span treats vv12-18 as a single 'positive panel,' but v13 opens its own protasis-apodosis (הֵן אֶעֱצֹר הַשָּׁמַיִם ... וְהֵן ... וְאִם) addressing national calamity-and-repentance, textually distinct in topic and addressee from v17's personal וְאַתָּה אִם pivot to Solomon's dynasty; this candidate internal seam is never raised or rebutted in strongest_rejected_alternative, which argues only against treating the whole 12-22 oracle as unbroken.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three of the four repairs are solid, and the morphological one is exactly right: across 7:17 the address is second masculine singular (וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם תֵּלֵ֣ךְ with the suffixed and prefixed forms following), 7:19 turns second masculine plural (וְאִם תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙), and 7:20's consequences go third plural. The Gibeon downgrade is also correctly executed, and a sweep for the niphal of the seeing root confirms 1:7 and 7:12 are the book's only appearances to Solomon (the third niphal, at 3:1, reports an appearance to David). What remains open is where the internal seam is handled and how the block at 13-16 is characterised. The rejected-alternative field was never updated, so the sharper of the two rivals is argued nowhere in the field reserved for it; and the description of vv13-16 as addressed to the people is contradicted by the verses themselves, which contain no second-person form at all.

challenges.claim: Uncured original defect, LF-M8-2Chr-027-2. Its operative sentence -- that the 13-16 against 17-18 candidate seam "is never raised or rebutted in strongest_rejected_alternative, which argues only against treating the whole 12-22 oracle as unbroken" -- is still true word for word of the revised row. Curing OL-M8-2Chr-027-3 in boundary_rationale did not touch the field the LF item named, and the revision arguably worsens the position: the row now states in its own voice that vv13-16 "hold their own complete protasis-apodosis" in a register distinct from the second-singular conditional at v17, which on the row's own analysis makes the 13-16|17-18 division a better claimant to strongest rival than the 12-22 merge the field still nominates.
challenges.suggested_action: Move the join argument into strongest_rejected_alternative in one sentence -- why the national conditional at 13-16 stays welded to the royal conditional at 17-18 -- and demote or drop the 12-22 merge, which the row already answers adequately in the rationale.

challenges.claim: The new sentence calls vv13-16 "addressed throughout in the third person to 'my people' rather than to Solomon directly". The morphology gives no addressee change there at all. Across 7:13, 7:14, 7:15 and 7:16 there is not one second-person form of either number: the pronominal suffixes are first person (עַמִּ֜י, שְׁמִ֣י, פָנַ֔י, עֵינַי֙, וְלִבִּ֛י) and third plural (עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם, מִדַּרְכֵיהֶ֣ם, לְחַטָּאתָ֔ם, אַרְצָֽם). The addressee was fixed by the frame at v12, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ ... אֶת תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ, second masculine singular to Solomon, and nothing in 13-16 revokes it; those verses speak about the nation, not to it. The register run the row is really describing is second-singular at v12, no second person through v16, second-singular again at 17-18, second-plural at v19 -- a different shape from the two-addressee picture asserted, and the seam argument is built on that picture.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate vv13-16 as third-person reference to the nation inside an oracle whose addressee never leaves Solomon, opened by הֵ֣ן אֶֽעֱצֹ֤ר הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙, and let the hinge at v18|v19 rest on the second-singular to second-plural turn the row already quotes accurately.

primary_reviews.rationale: This was the heaviest-challenged row in the cluster and the revision earns it. The Gibeon comparison is correctly walked back from 'shared formula' to 'shared lexeme...not a repeated formula' with the three differing slots (subject, tense, addressee marker) named; the v17/v19 seam is recast as an addressee-broadening shift (2ms to 2mp, apodosis to 3mp) rather than a false positive/negative mirror, quoting the actual verbal forms; and vv13-16 are no longer silently skipped -- they are now argued as the national mechanism that vv17-18 personalizes onto the dynasty. That last argument sits in the main boundary_rationale rather than literally inside strongest_rejected_alternative, but it is present and substantive, which is what the challenge asked for.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Five challenges land on this row and all five verify; two pairs converge and reconcile to single remedies, plus one further correction. LF-027-1 and OL-027-1 converge on the same gap: 1:7 (Gibeon) and 6:16 (dynastic plea) are argued as comparanda in the rationale but neither appears in boundary_evidence_refs -- confirmed by inspecting the frozen refs array, which runs straight through 7:12/17/18/19 with no 1:x or 6:x entries. One remedy covers both: mirror the pairs in. OL additionally corrects the row's characterization of the Gibeon link as 'the same appeared formula' -- collating both verses directly, 1:7's נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה is a niphal perfect with אֱלֹהִ֖ים as subject and the ל- prefix marking the addressee, while 7:12's וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה is a niphal wayyiqtol with יְהוָ֛ה as subject and אֶל marking the addressee -- one shared root and binyan across three differing slots, a shared lexeme rather than a shared formula exactly as OL states; I confirm this reading directly from both cited verses. Independently, OL-027-2's addressee-morphology point also checks out verbatim on collation: v17 (וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם תֵּלֵ֣ךְ...) runs second-masculine-singular start to finish (תֵּלֵ֣ךְ … צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ … תִּשְׁמֽוֹר) addressed to Solomon, while v19 (וְאִם תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם...) shifts to second-masculine-plural (וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙ … וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙) with v20's apodosis turning third-masculine-plural (וּנְתַשְׁתִּ֗ים, 'I will uproot THEM') -- the row's 'deliberate contrast'/'mirror' language claims a shared-addressee antithesis the grammar does not deliver; the v18/19 seam may still stand, but on an addressee-shift ground, not the one stated. Finally, LF-027-2 and OL-027-3 converge on the same unargued interior: vv13-16 hold a complete protasis-apodosis (הֵ֣ן אֶֽעֱצֹ֤ר הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֣ה...) addressed in the plural to 'עַמִּ֜י' with its own deictic pivots at עַתָּ֗ה (v15) and וְעַתָּ֗ה (v16); rejected_alternative tests only the coarsest rival (the whole 12-22 oracle unsplit) and never engages this candidate seam, which by addressee register actually aligns with v19's plural warning rather than v17's singular promise. One remedy covers this pair too: argue vv13-16 explicitly and say why the plural block stays bracketed inside a span framed around v17's singular promise. None of the five findings moves the frozen span or the 7:18/19 outer seam, but together they show the row's stated warrant needs rebuilding around addressee-register rather than a positive/negative mirror, and its medium confidence looks earned rather than generous given how much interior material goes unargued.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three Hebrew runs, all clean on collation. Both of the row's load-bearing original-language claims hold up. The opening first: v19's plural protasis is exactly as quoted, and the swing to plural addressees at that point is morphology rather than impression. Then the outer edge, where I swept the book for the time-frame noun and found it a hapax, present at 8:1 and nowhere else in 2Chr. So the row is not loosely pattern-matching a common connective: “וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה” is this book's single instance of the device, and it heads a clause left syntactically incomplete until v2 supplies its resumption, “בָּנָ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֹתָ֑ם” — the shape of a section frame, not of a continuation. Turning to the paragraph witness, the mark file gives PE after 7:22, which is the type cited, and the row weights it as “thin additional weight,” which is all a Writings mark may ever be. The causal summary “עַל כֵּן֙” is quoted accurately out of v22, WEB's “a proverb and a byword among all peoples” is v20 word for word, and with MT and WEB agreeing at 22 verses for chapter 7 and 18 for chapter 8 the row's single-numbered refs are right. I did probe the obvious rival, that this four-verse panel should be folded back into the night oracle; the morphological evidence I developed under M8-2Chr-027 tells against that merge rather than for it, so I bring no challenge here even though the row's stated alternative looks forward into chapter 8 rather than backward.

v19's marked antithesis to v17 is real and the row states it accurately, and the outer edge at 7:22/8:1 is about as clean a tier-1 seam as this cluster gets -- מִקֵּץ עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה is one of the strategy's own verified time-frame specimens, so the rejected alternative (reading 19-22 as a bridge into ch.8) is fairly weighed against real, cited textual competition rather than a straw man.

challenges.claim: The repaired rationale rests its concession on a rule Hebrew does not have: "Hebrew narrative requires the queen's name to be restated here simply because v2 handed the subject slot to Solomon." וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ at 9:3 is third feminine singular, and the queen is the only feminine participant in the scene, so the verb by itself resolves the reference; re-nomination is the unmarked option, not an obligation. 2Chr 9:12 settles it inside the same chapter with the same two participants: after וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן, third masculine singular, the subject reverts to the queen with no name at all -- וַֽתַּהֲפֹ֛ךְ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ -- carried by verbal morphology alone, with הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ appended only after the second verb. primary_reviews.rationale: Two quoted runs, both byte-perfect. Mark verification: pmarks_2Chr.json carries PE at oshb:2Chr.9.16 and PE at oshb:2Chr.9.21, matching the types reported; each rests on WLC alone, and neither verse belongs to the pair that takes two marks, so nothing further needs disclosing. The row is also correct in principle that one witness cannot by itself relocate a boundary. Where it fails is in describing what the intervening Hebrew actually looks like, and that description carries its entire case against subdividing; the challenge below sets out the falsification. I record separately that the outcome here still looks defensible to me even though the argument for it is not: sweeping 2Chr for the opener at issue returns four instances, three of them packed inside this chapter and one far away in Rehoboam's reign, a distribution that reads as item-marking within catalogs rather than unit-marking, which is a sound basis for keeping register material coarse. The row never makes that argument.

challenges.claim: This span's only stated warrant for refusing subdivision is contradicted by the text it describes. The rationale calls the material chained by "plain we-continuations and 'besides' connectors without any new formula-opener breaking the sequence", and the rejected alternative turns on the assertion that "none of these items opens with its own new subject or formula". Listing the actual openers refutes both: v15 begins וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה and v17 begins וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ, each a wayyiqtol governing an explicit nominal subject. That is heavier than the subjectless וַיְהִי֙ accepted at v13 as this unit's own start, so one standard is applied at the outer edge and a laxer one within. Particle- and noun-led continuations are certainly present — לְבַ֞ד at v14, then vv18-21 — but they do not cover v15 or v17. Tier-3 aggravates rather than relieves this: the PE at oshb:2Chr.9.16 (WLC only; 9:16 is not one of the twice-marked verses) sits at exactly the join those two openers bracket, so mark and clause structure agree instead of the mark being the lone, dismissible signal the rationale portrays. A high grade cannot rest on a premise the Hebrew refutes.
challenges.suggested_action: Rebuild the rejected alternative on accurate footing — the defensible warrant is that ויעש המלך behaves as a catalog item-opener rather than a unit-opener, attested at 9:11 and 9:15 and 9:17 inside this chapter plus 12:10 in Rehoboam's reign, which makes it list-internal here — or else divide at 9:16|9:17, where opener and mark converge. In either case the grade should fall below high until the edge argument matches the Hebrew, and oshb:2Chr.9.15 with oshb:2Chr.9.17 should be mirrored into boundary_evidence_refs.

primary_reviews.rationale: Keeping the shields-and-throne sequence as one register rather than splitting on item boundaries is the right call under this campaign's catalog handling: none of vv15-19 opens with its own subject or formula, so treating them as successive we-clauses inside one inventory that opens at v13 is textually accurate, not merely a coarseness preference. The mid-span PE at 9:16 is correctly treated as incapable of relocating anything on its own, and the row closes precisely where the Tarshish-fleet cargo list ends.

I tested the rebuilt warrant book-wide instead of accepting it. Sweeping OSHB for a verse-initial wayyiqtol plus the article-bearing noun for king returns exactly four places in 2Chr -- 9:11, 9:15, 9:17 and 12:10 -- and the same string occurs nowhere else in the book in any position, so the two comparanda the row cites are the complete set outside this span. Checking the campaign's own span list, no row begins at any of the four, which makes the assertion that the construction is never treated as a row-opener here true as stated rather than merely plausible. The continuation inventory also checks out: v18 opens with a conjunctive noun, v19 and v20 likewise, and v21 with a particle, so nothing in vv18-21 matches the v15/v17 shape. Both mark positions are correct under the follows-the-verse convention -- the PE keyed to 9:16 lands immediately before v17's opener, the PE keyed to 9:21 at the 9:21/9:22 edge -- and both are disclosed single-witness. This is a strong repair; what it leaves behind is one verse argued from but not cited, and one parenthetical that overshoots its quote.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This is the row my brief flagged for independent Hebrew verification, and OL-M8-2Chr-037-1 checks out against the primary text rather than against either reviewer's paraphrase. Slicing 9:11, 9:13-9:22, and 12:10 directly: v13 opens with the subjectless-of-agent וַיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב (subject is "the weight," not "the king"); v14 opens with the particle לְבַ֞ד; v16, v18, v19, v20 all open with bare wə-noun continuations (וּשְׁלֹשׁ, וְשֵׁ֣שׁ, וּשְׁנֵ֧ים, וְ֠כֹל) and v21 opens with the particle כִּֽי -- all consistent with the row's "plain continuation" description. But v15 opens וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה and v17 opens וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ, each a fresh wayyiqtol governing an explicit nominal subject -- exactly the construction the rejected alternative denies exists anywhere in vv15-19 ("none of these items opens with its own new subject or formula"). The same construction recurs at 9:11 (algum aside) and at 12:10 in Rehoboam's reign (וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ רְחַבְעָם֙), confirming this is a real, repeatable item-opener in this book's catalog style, not a one-off. Tier-3 does not rescue the row either: pmarks_2Chr.json places the PE at the end of 9:16, i.e. immediately before v17's own fresh opener, so mark and clause-shape converge on the same seam instead of the mark standing alone as the row's rationale portrays. Notably, LF's own verification of this row repeats the same premise it endorses ("none of vv15-19 opens with its own subject or formula") rather than catching the exception, so this is not a case of the primaries disagreeing so much as OL finding what LF's supporting check missed. The challenge does not by itself dictate a different span -- OL's own suggested_action allows that ויעש המלך may function as a catalog item-opener rather than a unit-opener, which could still support keeping the row coarse on a corrected rationale -- but the row's stated warrant for its high grade is factually wrong as written, and that is a confidence question for the author/boss round to resolve, not one I can settle here.

The register contrast the row draws is visible in the Hebrew rather than merely asserted: 9:22-24 runs on universalising subjects and predicates (וְכֹל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ at v23) and terminates on the distributive דְּבַר שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה, against the counted quantities that fill 13-21. The comparanda at 1:14-16 are mirrored into the refs in both witnesses, and since offset zone A does not begin until MT 1:18, those chapter-1 refs need no dual-cite.

The pivot from itemized catalog to universalizing rhetoric at v22 is a genuine register change, not a manufactured seam, and the recurring 'year in year' formula at the close of v24 gives the row a clean closing device distinct from 9:25's own fresh list opener. The PE at 9:24 lines up with that same edge and is treated appropriately as corroboration only, never as the reason for the seam.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row advances the most exacting original-language claim in the cluster, and one half of it survives byte-level scrutiny outright. The 9:25/1:14 comparison is precisely correct: the two closing clauses diverge by a single character, the meteg U+05BD carried by 1:14's בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָֽם and absent from 9:25's בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם, so "identical but for a single pointing mark" is literally true. All six runs in the row collate exact. Two problems remain, and they are of different weight. The lesser is that the parallel claim about 9:27 and 1:15 does not meet the standard the row set one sentence earlier. The graver is that the opening count of four echoing verses does not survive a lexical check of v26, which the row's own walk through 25, 27 and 28 passes over without comment.

challenges.claim: The row opens by calling these "Four verses that verbally echo 1:14-17", but 9:26 has no counterpart there. Comparing the consonantal word-set of 9:26 against the whole of 1:14-17 yields exactly one shared token, the generic connective ויהי; every content word of 9:26 (מושל, בכל, המלכים, מן, הנהר, ועד, ארץ, פלשתים, גבול, מצרים) is absent from 1:14-17, and territorial dominion has no topic-counterpart anywhere in that wealth notice. The row walks 25, 27 and 28 in detail and never mentions 26. Compounding this, 9:26 opens with the verse-initial וַיְהִ֥י מוֹשֵׁ֖ל — the very clause type this draft treats as seam-marking at 9:25 in its own rejected alternative — so an unargued internal opener of the row's preferred class sits inside a span graded high.
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the claim to the three verses that actually echo (25, 27, 28) and argue v26's attachment on its own terms, either as a dominion notice absorbed into the recapitulation or as a candidate internal seam; if it is absorbed on thematic grounds alone, bring the confidence down from high, since the row's inclusio warrant does not reach a quarter of its own span.

challenges.claim: The row states that 9:27 differs from 1:15 "only by 1:15's added" וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֛ב. A byte diff finds two further divergences, both accentual: 9:27's הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ against 1:15's הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ (U+05A7 -> U+059C), and 9:27's הַכֶּ֛סֶף against 1:15's הַכֶּ֧סֶף (U+059B -> U+05A7). The clauses are identical once cantillation is stripped but are not identical as pointed text. The re-accentuation is a mechanical consequence of the inserted phrase, so the literary point is untouched; the precision claim is not, and the row had just held itself to a byte-level standard at 9:25/1:14, where the claim does hold.
challenges.suggested_action: Qualify the 9:27/1:15 sentence as consonantal-and-vocalic identity with the accentuation redistributed around the insertion, so that the row's two parallel claims are measured on one scale.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the strongest row in the cluster. The claim that 9:25's closing clause differs from 1:14's only by a single pointing mark is not an assertion -- it collates exactly, meteg and all -- and the 1:15/9:27 comparison correctly identifies 1:15's added 'and the gold' as the sole difference rather than overstating a verbatim match. Citing this pairing as the in-book inclusio the strategy itself names, and expressly declining any Kings-Vorlage comparison, is exactly the synoptic discipline this campaign requires.

Both cures land, and I re-derived their arithmetic rather than take it on report. Removing "וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֛ב" from 1:15 and stripping the te'amim yields a string identical to 9:27; the surviving differences are two single codepoints, U+05A7 against U+059C on the word for the king and U+059B against U+05A7 on the word for the silver, which is what the revised sentence says and nothing more. The 9:25 claim is likewise exact at byte level: the two closing clauses differ by one U+05BD inside 1:14's spelling of Jerusalem and are consonantally identical, so "a single pointing mark" is the correct description. What the repair introduced is a fresh exclusivity claim about v26 that a token sweep does not support, and a rewritten rejected-alternative field that no longer weighs any rival span at all, which in turn strands a ref the prose has stopped using.

challenges.claim: The new sentence says v26 "shares only the toponym Egypt with 1:16-17's horse-trade notices". Tokenising both without points, 9:26 and 1:16-17 share no identical token whatever: 9:26 has the absolute "מִצְרָֽיִם" in construct after "גְּב֥וּל", while 1:16 and 1:17 both carry the prefixed form. The overlap is therefore lemma-level, and at lemma level Egypt is not the only one -- 9:26's "בְּכָל הַמְּלָכִ֑ים" and 1:17's "לְכָל מַלְכֵ֧י" plus "וּמַלְכֵ֥י" share the king lemma and the quantifier collocation alike. On strict token identity the sentence's premise that Egypt is shared fails; on the looser matching that makes Egypt count, the word "only" fails. Strategy §7 requires exclusivity claims to be swept at writing time, and this one was added by the repair to carry the argument that v26's contact with 1:14-17 is coincidental.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate as: 9:26 shares no exact token with 1:16-17, and its only lemma-level contacts are the toponym for Egypt and the common king-plus-quantifier collocation, neither of which is a topical parallel, since 9:26 marks a dominion border while 1:16-17 name a trade source. That preserves the argument and drops an exclusivity the sweep does not license.

challenges.claim: The frozen strongest_rejected_alternative weighed a rival span -- 9:22-28 read as one undivided recapitulation -- and argued the v24/v25 seam from the point where the wording turns near-verbatim rather than merely thematic. The revised field replaces that with a rival characterisation, whether all four verses are equally weighted echoes, and explicitly "keeps the row's edges as drawn". The row now tests no alternative boundary at all, which leaves a medium-graded span with no rival segmentation on the record. The substitution also strands web:2Chr.9.24, which survives in boundary_evidence_refs although nothing in the revised prose argues from v24 any longer; in the frozen text it was carried by the 22-24 comparison the repair deleted.
challenges.suggested_action: Keep the weighting correction but restore a rival span beside it -- 9:22-28 or 9:24-28 as one undivided recapitulation is the natural candidate and was already refuted in the frozen text -- and then either re-engage v24 in the prose or drop web:2Chr.9.24 from the refs so the array continues to mirror the argument.

primary_reviews.rationale: Narrowing the inclusio claim to vv.25/27/28 and giving v.26 a topical rather than lexical home is the right repair; the row no longer implies a uniform four-verse echo it can't support from the text. The accentuation qualifier is precise rather than hand-waved, naming the exact word pairs whose cantillation shifted around the inserted phrase.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Two challenges here land differently. OL-M8-2Chr-039-2 is confirmed outright at the codepoint level: diffing 9:27 against 1:15 word-for-word shows הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ (9:27, accent DARGA U+05A7) against הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ (1:15, accent GERESH U+059C), and הַכֶּ֛סֶף (9:27, accent TEVIR U+059B) against הַכֶּ֧סֶף (1:15, accent DARGA U+05A7) -- precisely the two divergences OL names, both mechanical consequences of 1:15's inserted וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֛ב reshuffling the disjunctive accents downstream, with the underlying consonants and vowels otherwise identical. OL-M8-2Chr-039-1 is right in substance but overstated in one particular, so I am ruling it supported_with_correction rather than outright supported: v26 (וַיְהִ֥י מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל הַמְּלָכִ֑ים מִן הַנָּהָר֙ וְעַד אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם) genuinely shares no topical content with 1:14-17's horses-silver-cedar-trade notice, and it does open with its own verse-initial וַיְהִ֥י clause of the very shape 038's rejected_alternative treats as seam-marking at 9:25 -- both points check out and neither reviewer had flagged them. But the claim that "every content word of 9:26...is absent from 1:14-17" is not quite true: the toponym מצרים (Egypt), which 9:26 itself closes on as מִצְרָֽיִם, recurs as the same lexeme in both 1:16 (מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם) and 1:17 (מִמִּצְרַ֤יִם), so the word-list is one toponym too strong. This does not rescue 9:26's inclusion in the inclusio claim, since Egypt marks a dominion-border terminus in 9:26 and a horse-trade source in 1:16-17 -- a shared geographic name doing unrelated topical work, not a shared content parallel -- so OL's underlying point about v26 survives the correction even though its literal word count does not.

challenges.claim: The row makes 10:15 the close of a unit opened at 10:12, but the Hebrew marks 10:14/10:15 as the stronger clause-level seam. Verses 12-14 run as consecutive wayyiqtol -- וַיָּבֹ֨א, then וַיַּעֲנֵ֥ם, then וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר -- and v.15 breaks that chain with וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע, waw plus negative plus qatal, a non-consecutive form; it then heads a run of three successive non-consecutive openings at 10:15, 10:16 (וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל) and 10:17 (וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִ֖ים). This is the same criterion decision M8-2Chr-047 elevates to a tier-1 driver at 11:13, and applied consistently it locates the seam before v.15, not after it. peer_crosscheck.assessment: Independently tracing the verb forms across vv.12-15, I confirm the challenge's grammatical premise: וַיָּבֹ֨א, וַיַּעֲנֵ֥ם and וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר run as an unbroken wayyiqtol chain through v.14, and v.15 opens וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע -- waw, negative, qatal -- genuinely departing from that chain, with v.16's וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל and v.17's וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל continuing the non-consecutive run. Where I would sharpen the challenge: these three verses are not one grammatical phenomenon. V.16 and v.17 front a bare subject noun phrase before their finite verb (matching the construction M8-2Chr-047 credits as tier-1 at 11:13), while v.15's clause is verb-first -- waw+lo+qatal with the verb (שָׁמַ֥ע) preceding its subject (הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ) -- a negated-comment type rather than the subject-fronted casus-pendens type of 11:13 (וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם...). Calling this 'the same criterion' as 047's driver overstates the grammatical identity even though the broader point (a real, unaddressed run of non-mainline clauses spanning 15-17) holds up. primary_reviews.rationale: Both Hebrew strings in this row are whole-verse slices and both collate byte-exact against 2Chr_oshb.txt (MT 13:23 and MT 14:1). Every dual-cite is arithmetically right: web 14:1 lands on MT 13:23 and web 14:2 on MT 14:1, while the 13:22 refs correctly carry no dual number because the offset zone has not yet begun there. The PE keyed to MT 13:23 is present in pmarks_2Chr.json, so the mark type is accurately reported (single-witness). The left-edge claim checks out lexically: MT 13:22 heads with וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה, which my book-wide sweep shows is the Chronicler's dominant reign-closing opener in 2Chr (10 occurrences of the yeter-divre shape against three one-off variants). The form distinction the row asserts is visible in the clause economy rather than merely stipulated: MT 13:23 runs a three-link succession chain, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב ... וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ ... וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ, and then closes with a fronted temporal clause, בְּיָמָ֛יו שָׁקְטָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ; MT 14:1 by contrast is a lone evaluative wayyiqtol, וַיַּ֤עַשׂ, governing the paired object הַטּ֣וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁ֔ר. Two different clause types, so the row's 'distinct forms' language is earned. I also quantified the rival the row concedes rather than taking it on trust: the root shin-qoph-tet occurs five times in 2Chr (MT 13:23, 14:4, 14:5, 20:30, 23:21), and the exact collocation of verb plus ha-arets occurs exactly twice, at MT 13:23 and at MT 14:5 (שָׁקְטָ֣ה הָאָ֗רֶץ), with MT 14:4 (וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה) a third member of the chain. So the 'quiet' link straddling this boundary is a verbatim repetition, not a loose motif. That is a genuinely strong rival, but the row names it, does not overstate its own footing, and prices the whole row at medium, which is the honest grade for a one-verse unit sitting on both a reign transition and the numbering seam. No challenge.

The single-verse span correctly isolates a death-succession-and-quiet-land formula (וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו בְּיָמָ֛יו שָׁקְטָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים) that belongs to neither the source-citation close before it (13:22, 'וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה...') nor the evaluation-formula opening after it (14:1 MT / 14:2 WEB, וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אָסָא֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁ֔ר בְּעֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו); three distinct formula classes stack in three consecutive verses, and isolating the middle one is defensible on tier-1 grounds alone. But the confidence explanation folds in something it should not: it grades the row medium partly 'because the verse sits directly on the reign transition and the numbering offset at once,' treating the WEB/MT versification hinge as a factor pulling confidence down. The evidence rules classify chapter/verse numbering as tier-4 metadata, 'NEVER evidence' -- that should bar it from confidence calibration in either direction, not just from driving the boundary itself.

challenges.suggested_action: Either split the row at the convocation, giving 15:8-9 as the reform response and 15:10-15 as the dated assembly and covenant oath, or keep 15:8-15 whole but argue the 15:9/15:10 seam explicitly and quote 15:10 to its end, including לִשְׁנַ֥ת חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא, so the strongest internal counter-signal is on the record rather than cut off at the atnach. primary_reviews.rationale: The response-formula opening and the movement through reform to assembly and covenant oath is well-anchored, and grading the v15-to-v16 seam as medium because the Maacah notice arrives as a plain topic change rather than a marked formula is an honest call on its own terms. But the row undersells its own strongest asset on the right edge: 'וַיָּ֧נַח יְהוָ֛ה לָהֶ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב' is not a generic rest-notice, it is a near-verbatim repeat of Asa's own words at 14:7 WEB / 14:6 MT, 'וַיָּ֥נַֽח לָ֖נוּ מִסָּבִ֑יב' -- a root-and-preposition match that a book-wide sweep shows occurring only four times total in 2Chr (14:6 MT, 15:15, 20:30, 32:22), with these two the only pair that brackets one continuous narrative arc. challenges.claim: The row's closing clause, 'וַיָּ֧נַח יְהוָ֛ה לָהֶ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב' ('Then Yahweh gave them rest all around', 15:15), verbatim-echoes Asa's own words at 14:7 WEB / 14:6 MT, 'וַיָּ֥נַֽח לָ֖נוּ מִסָּבִ֑יב' ('he has given us rest on every side'). primary_reviews.rationale: The right-edge repair holds up under sweep. מסביב occurs at four loci in the book (MT 14:6, 15:15, 20:30, 32:22) and pairs with וינח at three of them (14:6, 15:15, 20:30), so the diction the row calls closural genuinely is closural, and the 14:6/15:15 pairing does span the reform-battle-covenant material. That it recurs at 20:30 makes it a recurrent regnal-rest formula more than a bespoke bracket, which is a nuance rather than a fault, since either reading gives 15:15 independent closing warrant. What did not survive scrutiny is the newly written defence of the row's left interior. The seam at 15:9/15:10 carries three convergent signals — a PE, a qal-to-niphal voice change that hands the verb over to the people, and a month-plus-regnal-year date — and the row answers all three with one appeal to the campaign's device matrix. That appeal misreads the matrix and rests on a document that disclaims authority; I file it below. Byte collation of the row's six Hebrew strings is clean.

challenges.claim: The repair supplies the missing argument at 15:9/15:10, but grounds it in the wrong kind of authority and reads that authority backwards. The rationale's only reason for refusing the seam is that "the book's own device matrix already catalogs 15:9-10 together as a single assembly-summons instance, not as an unmarked participant-change seam." Three things tell against this. (i) The matrix entry sits under the heading "Boundary-driving devices (tier-1, in rough order of frequency)" in book_strategy_draft.md §1, and ASSEMBLY-SUMMONS frames are listed there because they OPEN units; cataloguing a locus under a boundary-driving class is therefore, if anything, a reason to expect an opening at 15:10, not evidence that 15:9 and 15:10 cohere. (ii) The matrix names קהל-family openings, and a consonantal sweep of the whole of 2Chr 15 returns no קהל form at all; 15:9 has וַיִּקְבֹּץ and 15:10 וַיִּקָּבְצוּ, both קבץ, so the entry the row invokes is not keyed to these verses' morphology — a mismatch the original item had already flagged and the revision does not disclose. (iii) The document self-describes at line 3 as a "Non-authorizing campaign working draft," so it cannot carry argumentative weight that tier-1 text signals are supposed to carry. Set against that single appeal are a PE after 15:9 (tier-3, weak, correctly not a driver), a qal-to-niphal alternation that changes the grammatical subject from Asa to the assembled people, and the full dating formula לִשְׁנַת חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה לְמַלְכוּת אָסָא that the row now quotes but never weighs. The formula class is not idle in this neighbourhood: למלכות dates Asa at only three places in the book (15:10, 15:19, 16:1), and the latter two are treated as boundary-grade at the 15:19/16:1 seam. Confidence was raised to high on the strength of the right edge while this interior counter-signal is left answered only by the draft's own catalogue.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the device-matrix appeal with a text-internal reason for reading 15:9-10 as summons-then-compliance — the obvious candidate is that 15:10's niphal has no independent subject expression and reads as the executed result of 15:9's qal, with the date attaching to the compliance rather than opening a new scene. If no such text-internal reason can be sustained against the PE, the voice change and the dating formula together, grade the row back to medium rather than high, or split at the convocation as the original item proposed. Either way, disclose that the matrix entry names קהל while 15:9-10 use קבץ.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both original defects are addressed in the same stretch of prose rather than patched separately: the missaviv refrain is quoted and named as a closural device, and the 15:9/15:10 seam is argued on its own terms with the full v.10 clause restored and the PE disclosed. Confidence moving to high is explained, not merely asserted, and the strongest_rejected_alternative's point about the assembly material's own rest-notice close survives the added discussion intact.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Two challenges reach this row from different directions and land differently. LF's inclusio point checks out on an independent sweep: stripping niqqud from מסביב across all of 2Chr returns exactly four hits, 14:6 (MT)/14:7 (WEB), 15:15, 20:30, and 32:22, and the נוח+מסביב 'rest all around' phrasing specifically brackets 14:6 and 15:15, the reform-to-covenant complex rows 058-061 traverse. OL's challenge, probing a different seam, is right about a real gap but overreaches on what it implies. The row's quotation of 15:10 does stop at the atnach and drops לִשְׁנַ֥ת חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָ֑א, and MT 15:9's qal וַיִּקְבֹּ֗ץ (Asa as agent) does give way to 15:10's niphal וַיִּקָּבְצ֥וּ (the people as subject) with a PE standing between them.
