primary_reviews.rationale: All four quotes match 2Chr_oshb.txt exactly (opening slices of 15:16 and 15:17, whole 15:19, opening slice of 16:1), no dual-cites are due outside the zone and none are offered, and the SAMEKH the refs key to 15:19 is in pmarks with that type. The year-pair claim survives a sweep rather than resting on impression: le-malkut appears nine times in the book, three of them dating Asa's reign, and 15:19 and 16:1 are adjacent members sharing everything but the ordinal - שְׁנַת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא against בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ לְמַלְכ֣וּת, differing only at וְחָמֵ֖שׁ versus וָשֵׁשׁ֙. 'Almost word for word' is therefore accurate rather than rhetorical. Clause syntax reinforces both sides of that seam: 15:19 is a fronted-subject negated qatal, וּמִלְחָמָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָיָ֑תָה, the disjunctive shape typical of a summarising close, while 16:1 fronts a temporal prepositional phrase before its qatal אָסָ֔א, the standard new-episode opening. The left edge is correctly graded as the weaker one: we-gam plus a fronted subject is an additive connective, not a formula, and medium confidence matches that asymmetry. One nuance where the Hebrew is sharper than the row's gloss, offered as verification rather than objection: the row reads 15:17 as a caveat on the reform's completeness, but MT 14:4 says וַיָּ֨סַר֙ מִכָּל עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אֶת הַבָּמ֖וֹת in the hiphil and of Judah's cities, whereas וְהַ֨בָּמ֔וֹת לֹא סָ֖רוּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל is qal and of Israel - a different stem and a different territory, so the two notices need not conflict. That is a glossing nuance internal to the span and does not bear on either boundary, so no challenge follows from it. No undisclosed mark falls inside 15:16-19.

Anchoring the row's strong edge on the paired year-counts (thirty-fifth year at 15:19, וּמִלְחָמָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָיָ֑תָה עַ֛ד שְׁנַת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא, answered by thirty-sixth year at 16:1, 'בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ לְמַלְכ֣וּת אָסָ֔א עָלָ֞ה בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה') is the right move; that is a genuine chronological hinge answered almost word for word, not mere numbering coincidence. Conceding that the 'also Maacah' opening is a softer connective than a marked formula, rather than dressing it up as something stronger, is honest bookkeeping given the medium grade assigned.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Also unchallenged, and the spot-check holds without qualification. primary_reviews.rationale: The four quotes collate byte-exact and the SAMEKH keyed to 16:6 is correctly typed in pmarks. Both edges hold up on inspection. The opening year notice does answer 15:19 as the row says, and the closing edge is clean because 16:7 opens on the time marker וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא with a fresh participant, בָּ֚א introducing Hanani. I also checked the internal SAMEKH after 16:5 and the fronted-subject clause that opens 16:6, וְאָסָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לָקַח֙: that clause is disjunctive in form, but it disposes of the Ramah materials Baasha abandoned in the previous verse, so it resolves the same episode rather than starting a new one, and I do not press a seam there. What I do contest is the genre label applied to the inset. The row calls 16:2-3 an embedded letter twice over, but a sweep of the book's letter lexemes finds none of them in either verse: 2Chr uses miktav at 21:12, 35:4 and 36:22 and iggerot at 30:1 and 30:6, and the two insets the strategy actually classes as letters are introduced by exactly those nouns - וַיָּבֹ֤א אֵלָיו֙ מִכְתָּ֔ב מֵֽאֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר at 21:12 and וְגַֽם אִגְּרוֹת֙ כָּתַב֙ at 30:1. 16:2 instead ends with the ordinary messenger frame, וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח governing לֵאמֹֽר. challenges.claim: The rationale classes 16:2-3 as a 'two-verse embedded letter', but no letter lexeme occurs in either verse. Book-wide sweep of 2Chr: miktav at 21:12, 35:4, 36:22; iggerot at 30:1, 30:6 - and the two insets the device matrix lists as letters carry those nouns explicitly, וַיָּבֹ֤א אֵלָיו֙ מִכְתָּ֔ב מֵֽאֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר at 21:12 and וְגַֽם אִגְּרוֹת֙ כָּתַב֙ at 30:1. 16:2 closes instead with the standard messenger frame וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח plus לֵאמֹֽר, so the inset is a messenger speech. primary_reviews.rationale: The crisis notice answering 15:19's peace count, and the building notice at v6 giving way to Hanani's time-marked entrance at v7 ('וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא בָּ֚א חֲנָ֣נִי הָרֹאֶ֔ה אֶל אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה'), are both solid tier-1 edges, and folding Asa's message to Ben-hadad inside the unit under the inset rule is correct since nothing resumes or reframes it afterward. primary_reviews.rationale: Three quotes, all byte-exact; worth noting that the long 16:9 string is contiguous in the MT, so the ellipsis in the row's English is a compression of the gloss and not of the Hebrew. No mark falls anywhere in MT 16:7-10, and the row correctly claims none. I checked the echo the row draws to 15:1-2: the function matches but the lexemes differ, since 15:2 has the prophet going out before the king (וַיֵּצֵא֮ לִפְנֵ֣י אָסָא֒) while 16:7 has the seer coming to him (בָּ֚א governing a preposition), so 'arrival' is fair as a scene description but is not a shared formula. Against that, the row missed a signal that positively supports its own span: the phrase ba-'et ha-hi occurs eight times in 2Chr (7:8, 13:18, 16:7, 16:10, 21:10, 28:16, 30:3, 35:17) and two of those eight are the first words of MT 16:7 (וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא) and the last words of MT 16:10 (בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא) - a temporal inclusio bracketing exactly this span, which is in-book tier-1 evidence for folding the reprisal into the rebuke and answers the rejected alternative better than the brevity argument the row actually gives. The challenge concerns the closing edge's description, not its location.

challenges.claim: The rationale calls 16:11 'the fixed source-citation formula' and equates it with the closer at 13:22, but 16:11 is the book's single lexical outlier in that class. Sweep of 2Chr reign-closers: the yeter-divre opener occurs ten times (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8), against וּשְׁאָר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה at 9:29, וְדִבְרֵ֣י רְחַבְעָ֗ם at 12:15, and וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א at 16:11 - one occurrence each. 13:22 heads with וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה, so the two verses the row equates do not share an opener, and וְהִנֵּה֙ occurs in this construction nowhere else in the book. The register class is genuinely shared - 16:11 carries the divre plus first-and-last plus 'written in the book' shape common to 20:34 and 25:26 - so the seam itself is not in doubt; the word 'fixed' and the claimed identity with 13:22 are.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword to say that 16:11 opens the reign-closing source-citation class in its one book-unique variant, quoting וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א against the ten-fold yeter-divre norm, rather than describing it as the fixed formula already seen at 13:22. Span unchanged. Optionally add the ba-'et ha-hi inclusio between 16:7 and 16:10 to the rationale and refs, since it strengthens the row's own folding of 16:10 into the unit.

primary_reviews.rationale: Hanani's arrival deliberately echoes Azariah's at 15:1-2 while inverting its message from exhortation to rebuke, and the row is self-aware about why it does not mirror the chapter-15 oracle/response split: Asa's one-verse reaction here (v10) never grows into its own reform report the way the assembly-and-oath material did after 15:7, so keeping rebuke and reaction in one row instead of two is a proportionate call rather than an inconsistency. The close on the fixed source-citation formula at 16:11 ('וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א...') is the same register-class Abijah's reign used at 13:22 ('וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י...'), correctly identified by the shared dibrei...kethuvim template.

Every count the repair asserts is right where I could test it. Consonantal sweeps return ויתר דברי at exactly ten verses (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8), ושאר דברי once at 9:29, and והנה דברי once, at 16:11; the only other verse-initial ודברי hit is 35:27, which is וּדְבָרָיו continuing 35:26's own yeter-closer, not a rival opener, so "a bare וְדִבְרֵי at 12:15" survives. The temporal bracket is real too: וּבָעֵת הַהִיא opens 16:7 and בָּעֵת הַהִיא ends 16:10, which is a stronger warrant for folding the reprisal in than the brevity argument it supplements. My one reservation is with the contrast set the sentence builds around those counts, which presents three openers as if they exhausted the book's reign-closers when the campaign's own strategy names a fourth locus that fits none of them.

challenges.claim: The contrast set enumerating the book's reign-closers is incomplete, and the omitted member is the one most relevant to the row's own argument. The rationale states that 16:11's hinneh-presentative is "found nowhere else among the book's reign-closers, which instead run וְיֶתֶר דִּבְרֵי ten times (13:22 among them), וּשְׁאָר דִּבְרֵי once at 9:29, or a bare וְדִבְרֵי at 12:15" — an enumeration that accounts for thirteen loci. book_strategy_draft.md §1 lists a fourteenth in the same class, 24:27, and the text bears that out: Joash's reign closes וּבָנָיו ... הִנָּם כְתוּבִים עַל מִדְרַשׁ סֵפֶר הַמְּלָכִים, which opens with none of the three forms named. So the book has two morphologically deviant reign-closers, not one, and the rhetorical force of calling 16:11 the lone outlier is overstated. A second, connected imprecision: the presentative element itself is not rare — הנם כתובים occurs at eleven verses (16:11, 20:34, 24:27, 25:26, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:19, 35:25, 35:27, 36:8) — so what is genuinely unique at 16:11 is the fronting of וְהִנֵּה into the incipit, not the presentative as such. The seam at 16:10/16:11 is not in question; the count is verified and the row's core uniqueness claim stands, since 24:27 does not open presentatively either.
challenges.suggested_action: Either mark the enumeration as partial ("which otherwise run ...") or add 24:27 as the class's second deviant opener, and sharpen the uniqueness claim to the fronted וְהִנֵּה incipit rather than to presentative diction generally, since הִנָּם כְתוּבִים is the class norm. List oshb:2Chr.24.27 among the row's refs. Span unchanged.

primary_reviews.rationale: The row no longer claims 16:11 repeats 13:22's opener. peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's challenge survives an independent sweep of the book's reign-closing openers. Of the 2Chr formulas built on the divre root, ten share the וְיֶתֶר construction (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8), 9:29 uses וּשְׁאָר, 12:15 uses a bare וְדִבְרֵי, and 16:11's וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א is this construction's only instance in the entire book. Calling it 'the fixed source-citation formula...already seen closing Abijah's reign at 13:22' overstates a shared register, divre plus rishonim/aharonim plus kethuvim, as though it were a shared opener, when 13:22 and 16:11 in fact open differently. The seam location is not in question, only the wording equating the two openers. OL also surfaces a genuine reinforcement the row missed: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא opens MT 16:7 and closes MT 16:10, and a book-wide sweep finds eight total occurrences of that phrase with only this pair adjacent, a temporal inclusio bracketing exactly this span that argues for folding the reprisal into the rebuke more directly than the brevity argument the row currently leans on.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation is clean: all five Hebrew strings here (16:11, 16:12, two from 16:14, and the succession clause at 17:1) reproduce the OSHB bytes exactly, and pmarks confirms the mark keyed to 2Chr.16.14 is PE, single-witness, correctly typed. The span itself I do not dispute — v.11 carries genuine tier-1 source-citation material and the closing edge holds against 17:1 — but two of the row's claims about the Hebrew fail on inspection. The formula at 16:11 is not "the same source-citation form" as 13:22: Abijah's notice opens וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה while Asa's opens וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א, and a consonantal sweep of the book puts the וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י incipit in ten verses against exactly one for וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י — 16:11 itself. Separately, the alleged contrast in sequence does not exist in the text. Both challenges are recorded below.

challenges.claim: The row identifies 16:11 as "the same source-citation form that closed Abijah's reign at 13:22" (tier-1, source-citation formula). The Hebrew shows two different incipits: 13:22 reads וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה, 16:11 reads וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א. A book-wide consonantal sweep of 2Chr returns the וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י incipit at ten verses (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8) and the וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י incipit at one (16:11). 16:11 is the book's sole presentative variant of the formula, not an instance of the 13:22 form.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate the relation at the level the Hebrew supports — same functional class (construct וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י-type heading plus a written-source clause), demonstrably different and in fact unique incipit. The hapax status strengthens rather than weakens the opening-signal argument, so the correction costs the row nothing and the span need not move.

challenges.claim: "[H]ere it precedes rather than follows the remaining biographical notices" asserts a contrast with 13:22 that the text does not bear out: MT 13:23 (= WEB 14:1) opens וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙, so at Abijah the citation formula likewise stands before the death-and-burial material. The rejected alternative then invokes "the pattern already seen at 13:22/13:23" as warrant for keeping formula and notices together, but under the strategy's own block map (§5, ASA = WEB 14:1-16:14) that precedent is a case where the formula and the notice following it were assigned to different blocks — the opposite of the cohesion it is cited for.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the false contrast and re-cast the argument on the real asymmetry: 13:23 fuses death, burial and succession in a single verse (וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו), whereas Asa's succession waits until 17:1, leaving 16:12-14 with no successor notice to cut against. That is what actually licenses holding 16:11-14 together.

primary_reviews.rationale: The unit's edges genuinely hold: the source-citation formula at 16:11 does precede rather than follow the biographical notices, an inversion of the more familiar Abijah pattern at 13:22-23, and the row is right to name that inversion instead of smoothing it over. But the rationale folds v.13 into a loose label, "death and burial," and quotes only the burial half (v.14); v.13 itself carries the exact regnal-death formula the book strategy's device matrix names as its own class (parallel to 21:1), and that formula never reaches boundary_evidence_refs at all.

challenges.claim: 2Chr.16.13, "וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אָסָ֖א עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיָּ֕מָת בִּשְׁנַ֛ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת לְמָלְכֽוֹ" ("Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign"), belongs to the same closing-formula class the strategy's matrix flags at 21:1, sits inside this decision's own span, and is invoked only generically as half of "death and burial" in the rationale; it is never quoted and never appears in boundary_evidence_refs, leaving the span's strongest available formulaic warrant undemonstrated.
challenges.suggested_action: Cite web:2Chr.16.13 / oshb:2Chr.16.13 in boundary_evidence_refs and quote the death notice next to the burial text already drawn from v.14.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the most thoroughly repaired row in the cluster and it survives re-testing on every point. The withdrawn contrast is genuinely withdrawn: MT 13:23 does open וַיִּשְׁכַּב אֲבִיָּה עִם אֲבֹתָיו וַיִּקְבְּרוּ אֹתוֹ immediately after 13:22, so sequence never distinguished the two cases; and the substituted completeness argument is textually exact, since 13:23 carries וַיִּמְלֹך אָסָא בְנוֹ תַּחְתָּיו within the same verse while nothing between 16:12 and 16:14 names a successor — 17:1 supplies him, past this part's edge. The subsidiary facts hold too: PE follows 16:14 in WLC; book_strategy_draft.md §5 assigns p06 as 13:1-16:14, so "this part's assigned last verse" is accurate; and 21:1's וַיִּשְׁכַּב יְהוֹשָׁפָט עִם אֲבֹתָיו matches the incipit on which §1 keys the death-and-succession class, so 16:13's membership is claimed on the criterion the matrix itself uses even though Asa's succession clause is deferred. The offset dual-cite web:2Chr.14.1 = oshb:2Chr.13.23 is correct. Ten-fold ויתר דברי and singleton והנה דברי both reconfirmed by sweep. I file nothing.

All three original defects are cured in a single reworked paragraph rather than three isolated patches: v.13 is quoted and cited, the 16:11/13:22 relation is corrected to shared-class-plus-unique-incipit, and the sequence-based contrast with 13:22/13:23 is replaced by the completeness argument the digest itself proposed. The four-verse span's closural warrant is now fully evidenced rather than resting on generic 'death and burial' language.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: All three challenges on this row converge on one weakness: the opening sentence over-claims formulaic identity and a false sequence-contrast between 16:11 and 13:22/13:23, while the row also passes over the tier-1 death formula sitting inside its own span at 16:13. My own consonantal sweep of 2Chr_oshb.txt returns וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י at exactly one verse, 16:11, against ten hits for וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8) -- confirming OL's correction that 16:11 is the book's sole presentative variant, not an instance of 13:22's own form. Slicing MT 13:23 (= web:2Chr.14.1 = oshb:2Chr.13.23 (MT)) also confirms OL's second point: it opens וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙, so Abijah's own citation formula (13:22) likewise precedes his death-and-burial notice; the row's claimed contrast in ordering does not exist in either account. LF's gap is confirmed too, and carries more weight than stated: 16:13's וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אָסָ֖א עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו is not generic "death and burial" language but a direct instance of the strategy's own named REGNAL DEATH-AND-SUCCESSION class (book_strategy_draft.md §1, verified specimen 21:1), and that verse never reaches boundary_evidence_refs at all. None of this moves the closing edge -- the PE at 16:14 (single-witness) and the 17:1 succession formula hold on every reviewer's own admission -- but a "high"-confidence row carrying three independently confirmed argumentative errors is worth the author round's attention.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every Hebrew form quoted in this row checks out byte for byte — the succession clause at 17:1, both halves of the seek/not-seek antithesis at 17:3 and 17:4, the high-places notice at 17:6, the dating clause at 17:7 — and pmarks types the 17:6 marker as PE (single-witness), which is what the row cites. The seam the row actually rests on survives my sweep and is strengthened by it: clause-initial וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת occurs in only three verses of 2Chr (17:7, 34:8, 36:22) and each one launches a fresh royal initiative, so the dated clause at v.7 does the work assigned to it. Two smaller matters. The "causal 'therefore' of v.5" is the WEB rendering of a bare wayyiqtol, וַיָּ֨כֶן; no causal particle stands in the Hebrew, though nothing in the boundary depends on it. challenges.claim: The rejected alternative turns on a universal — the v.7 regnal-year dating clause "which the Chronicler otherwise uses to open, not continue, an episode." A book-wide sweep of the dating lexeme in 2Chr returns eight verses (3:2, 13:1, 16:1, 16:12, 16:13, 17:7, 34:8, 36:22), and in three of them the dated phrase continues a clause instead of opening one: 3:2 (בִּשְׁנַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֖ע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ), and — inside this same cluster — 16:12 (וַיֶּחֱלֶ֣א אָסָ֡א בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים וָתֵ֤שַׁע לְמַלְכוּתוֹ֙) and 16:13 (וַיָּ֕מָת בִּשְׁנַ֛ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת לְמָלְכֽוֹ), both of which M8-2Chr-065 correctly keeps unit-internal. As stated the universal is contradicted by the cluster's own neighbouring row.
challenges.suggested_action: Restrict the universal to clause-initial position, where it is exceptionless: וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת heads only 17:7, 34:8 and 36:22 and opens an episode in all three. So restricted the claim is stronger than the one made, and the span is untouched.

The restriction it chose, however, is not the restriction that makes the claim true, and I could falsify the sentence as written from the same sweep that motivated the original item. The defect is confined to the scope word.

challenges.claim: The rebuilt universal is falsified as worded, and by verses this cluster itself handles. The rationale says of the v.7 dating clause that "restricted to this clause-initial form, the construction is exceptionless across the book — it opens only 17:7, 34:8, and 36:22," and the rejected alternative repeats that "narrowed to its clause-initial form, the construction opens only three episodes book-wide." My sweep of בשנת across 2Chr returns the same eight verses the original item found (3:2, 13:1, 16:1, 16:12, 16:13, 17:7, 34:8, 36:22). Partitioned by position rather than by prefix, five of those eight are clause-initial: וּבִשְׁנַת heads 17:7, 34:8 and 36:22, and בִּשְׁנַת heads 13:1 (בִּשְׁנַת שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לַמֶּלֶךְ יָרָבְעָם) and 16:1 (בִּשְׁנַת שְׁלֹשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ לְמַלְכוּת אָסָא). Both open episodes, and 16:1 is the opening verse of M8-2Chr-063 four rows back in this very cluster. So "clause-initial" does not isolate the three-member set; the conjunctive vav does. The original item was upheld precisely because a universal was contradicted by a neighbouring row in the same cluster, and the replacement wording reproduces that shape in a new key. The repair is also weaker than the truth available to it: on the position criterion the generalisation is in fact exceptionless in the row's favour, since all five clause-initial instances (13:1, 16:1, 17:7, 34:8, 36:22) launch an episode while all three non-initial ones (3:2, 16:12, 16:13) continue a clause already underway.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate on the criterion that actually holds. Either narrow to the prefix — "verse-initial וּבִשְׁנַת heads only 17:7, 34:8 and 36:22" — or, preferably, keep the position criterion and state the stronger true form: clause-initial dating opens an episode at all five loci (13:1, 16:1, 17:7, 34:8, 36:22), whereas 3:2, 16:12 and 16:13 carry the phrase inside a clause already begun. Drop "only" from the three-verse list, and carry oshb:2Chr.13.1 in the refs beside the existing 16:1 entry. The v.6/v.7 seam is untouched either way.

The teach/taught bracket the row builds its closing edge on is firmer than the row itself claims. The row's claim that v.10 carries no verbal link back is therefore exactly right, and it is right for a reason stronger than stated. Chapter 17 lies outside both offset zones, so the single-numbered refs are correct; no mark falls inside 17:7-9 (pmarks' nearest are PE at 17:6 and PE at 17:11, both single-witness), so no tier-3 material was mis-typed or quietly suppressed. Nothing here needs adjudication.

The teach/taught bracket is real and precisely quoted at both ends, and v.10's shift to a wholly new grammatical subject is legitimate grounds for not running the circuit report forward. challenges.claim: The closural bracket is miscounted, and the pairing chosen is not the tightest one available. The rationale says the officials' task is "stated twice, bracket-fashion: לְלַמֵּד בְעָרֵי יְהוּדָה (v.7) and וַיְלַמְּדוּ בָּעָם (v.9)." The piel of למד in fact occurs three times across 17:7-9, not twice: לְלַמֵּד at the end of v.7, then וַיְלַמְּדוּ twice within v.9 — וַיְלַמְּדוּ בִיהוּדָה opening the verse and וַיְלַמְּדוּ בָּעָם closing it. This matters twice over. The count is simply wrong as stated, and the nearest lexical partner to v.7's לְלַמֵּד בְעָרֵי יְהוּדָה is the verse-opening וַיְלַמְּדוּ בִיהוּדָה, which shares the Judah complement, rather than the verse-final phrase the row pairs it with; so the repetition is distributed through v.9 rather than anchored at the row's right edge, and "closes the circuit report cleanly" claims more edge-precision than the distribution supports. The v.10 pivot argument is unaffected, so the right edge itself is not in dispute.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the count to three occurrences and re-describe the figure as a resumptive repetition running from v.7's purpose infinitive into v.9's doubled finite verbs, rather than as a two-member bracket; if the inclusio reading is retained, say explicitly that the outer pair is selected and why the medial וַיְלַמְּדוּ בִיהוּדָה does not disturb it. No span change.

challenges.claim: The exclusivity claim — "the 'fear of Yahweh' clause-type recurs only twice more in 2Chr (14:13, 19:7)" — holds for the two-word string but not for the clause-type it is asserted about. Sweeping the clause opening וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד returns 17:10 and 20:29, and 20:29 (וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת) matches 17:10 (וַיְהִ֣י פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֗ה עַ֚ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָֽאֲרָצ֔וֹת) consonantally in six of its first seven words, diverging only in the divine name — far closer than either verse cited, where the noun sits in different syntax (MT 14:13 כִּי הָיָ֥ה פַֽחַד יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם; 19:7 וְעַתָּ֕ה יְהִ֥י פַֽחַד יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם). The omission is not neutral: 20:29 stands between the victory-return at 20:27-28 and the rest notice at 20:30, functioning as an aftermath clause attached to the episode before it — which is precisely the result-clause reading of 17:10-11 that this row rejects. The strongest in-book analogue therefore tells for the rejected alternative, not for the seam.
challenges.suggested_action: Cite 20:29 and rebut it — the available rebuttal is that 17:10's continuation names the kingdoms surrounding Judah as an ongoing state rather than a reaction to one battle — or accept that the nearest analogue cuts the other way and drop confidence below medium.

challenges.claim: The sweep result is reported in the rationale as "(14:13, 19:7)" with no numbering system named. The row's refs array dual-cites it correctly as "web:2Chr.14.14 = oshb:2Chr.14.13 (MT)", so prose and refs disagree in form and a downstream reader taking the prose at face value lands one verse off.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation is clean and the two book-wide sweeps this row leans on both replicate: פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֗ה stands at MT 14:13, 17:10 and 19:7 and nowhere else, while the clause opening וַיְהִ֣י פַּ֣חַד occurs at 17:10 and 20:29 only, the latter agreeing with 17:10 in six of its first seven words with just the divine name substituted. The prose arithmetic is right as well; the catalog next door really does run eight verses. What the repair has produced, though, is a rationale whose every evidentiary sentence now runs against its own boundary: the opening device is described as one the book does not treat as reliably boundary-driving, the nearest in-book analogue is said to cut against rather than for the seam, the rival at 17:12 is granted, and the mark is said to settle nothing either way. Honest grading is not the same thing as warrant, and after this rewrite the two-verse span has no affirmative evidence behind it at all. The account of the mark evidence is also short by one, in a way that bears on the contested edge.

Tier-3 material cannot drive a seam and absence of a mark is never counterevidence, but the row's summary of what the marks supply is factually short by one, and the omitted material does not sit neutrally: the witness's own division groups vv.10-11 with the teaching-circuit verses from which this row separates them.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This is the cluster's most heavily challenged row and every item on it holds up. LF's granularity complaint is confirmed: 17:10 opens וַיְהִ֣י פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֗ה... and 17:12 opens וַיְהִ֧י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֵ֖ל..., both new-subject vayehi clauses of the very type this row treats as its own seam-warrant, yet the device produces a standalone two-verse unit here and is absorbed without comment into an eight-verse catalog next door in decision 069. OL's closer-analogue challenge reinforces the same worry from the far side: a sweep of the clause וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד across 2Chr returns only 17:10 and 20:29, and 20:29's וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת matches 17:10 consonantally across six of its first seven words -- far closer than either verse this row actually cites (14:13, 19:7). Checked against WEB, 20:29 sits between the victory procession (20:27-28, "they returned... to Jerusalem with joy") and the rest notice (20:30) as a direct causal aftermath of the preceding battle ("when they heard that Yahweh fought"), which is exactly the teaching-mission-fruit reading this row's strongest_rejected_alternative calls merely "plausible" without ever defeating. I read LF-068-1 and OL-068-1 as one diagnosis rather than two: 17:10-11's isolation from what precedes AND from what follows is under-argued on both flanks at once, and the row's own self-capped medium confidence already senses this -- these challenges specify why that cap is earned rather than raising a new problem. The two narrower gaps are independently confirmed: pmarks_2Chr.json keys a PE to 2Chr.17.11 (single-witness) that this row alone in the cluster omits, where 065, 066, 069, and 072 all disclose theirs; and the prose gives the fear-of-Yahweh comparanda as a bare "(14:13, 19:7)" although 14:13 is MT numbering inside offset zone B (WEB 14:2-15 = MT 14:1-14), undisclosed in prose even though the refs array itself dual-cites it correctly as web:2Chr.14.14 = oshb:2Chr.14.13 (MT). None of the four items forces the span to move by itself, but together they leave this boundary the least independently anchored in the cluster -- a granularity question for the author/boss round, not mine to settle.

challenges.claim: 17:14 opens with וְאֵ֥לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֖ם, a list/register formula — tier-1 in the contract's own device list — and one of only four clause-initial openers of its kind in 2Chr (3:3, 8:10, 17:14, 24:26). primary_reviews.rationale: The two Hebrew strings quoted (18:1 and 18:3) are byte-exact, and read strictly the exclusivity claim survives: the collocation עֹֽשֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹֽב, matched on its consonantal skeleton, occurs in exactly two verses of 2Chr, 17:5 and 18:1. Two things still need correcting. The comparandum at 17:5 is asserted and never sliced, and the two forms are not the same string — 17:5 closes וַֽיְהִי ל֥וֹ עֹֽשֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹֽב against 18:1's וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב, differing in the beneficiary and in the accentuation of two words, so the longest pointed substring they share runs nineteen characters and begins mid-word. The frame around the collocation is also stock rather than bespoke. And the row's flat assertion that no formula break stands at v.2 passes over a lexeme the contract classes as tier-1.

challenges.claim: "V.1 reuses the phrase closing 17:5" is argued without ever quoting 17:5, and the two forms are not identical: 17:5 ends וַֽיְהִי ל֥וֹ עֹֽשֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹֽב, 18:1 opens וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב. They differ in the beneficiary (pronoun versus proper name) and in the accents on two of the three shared words; what the two hold in common is the collocation עֹֽשֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹֽב at the consonantal level only. The surrounding construction is moreover a recurring Chronistic royal-prosperity frame, not a bespoke echo — 32:27 opens וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד, the same existential-plus-beneficiary frame with a different quantifier, and the noun pair also appears at 1:11 and 1:12.
challenges.suggested_action: Slice 17:5's form into the rationale alongside 18:1's and state the reuse at the level it holds — a consonantal collocation inside a frame the book reuses — citing 32:27 so the resumptive echo is not overstated. The row's conclusion (echo relaunching the narrative, not an inclusio bracketing 17:1-18:1) is unaffected and in fact better supported once the frame is shown to be stock.

challenges.claim: The row states there is "no formula break at v.2," but 18:2 opens וַיֵּרֶד֩ לְקֵ֨ץ שָׁנִ֤ים, carrying the temporal lexeme the contract lists as a tier-1 time-frame transition and the strategy anchors at 8:1 (וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה). Across all of 2Chr that lexeme appears in only three verses — 8:1, 18:2 and 21:19, the last a fixed idiom for a term expiring — so 18:2 holds one of the book's two live temporal-transition tokens, and the row dismisses it without naming it. Since a break at v.2 would leave 18:1 stranded alone, this bears directly on the span, not merely on the prose.
challenges.suggested_action: Argue the point rather than assert it. The distinction available is positional: 8:1 has the phrase clause-initially in a full temporal frame, whereas 18:2 has it as an adjunct to a fronted verb of motion, which subordinates the time reference to an action already under way from v.1.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both of OL's challenges check out against the file. 17:5 closes וַֽיְהִי ל֥וֹ עֹֽשֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹֽב while 18:1 opens וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב -- the row asserts the reuse without ever slicing 17:5's own form into the rationale, and the two strings differ in beneficiary (bound pronoun versus proper name) exactly as claimed. 32:27's construction, וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד, confirms the "existential-plus-beneficiary" royal-prosperity frame recurs elsewhere with a different quantifier, so presenting the echo as a bespoke construction rather than a stock frame carrying one genuinely unique collocation overstates the case; the row's own conclusion is unaffected by this fix, and reads more solidly once restated at the level the Hebrew supports. The second challenge is equally confirmed: a bare consonantal sweep for קץ across all of 2Chr returns exactly three verses -- 8:1, 18:2, 21:19 -- so 18:2's לְקֵ֨ץ שָׁנִ֤ים does carry one of the book's few live temporal-transition tokens, and the row dismisses a possible break at v.2 with a flat "no formula break" rather than engaging that token by name. A positional distinction is available and preserves the span: 8:1's מִקֵּ֣ץ opens a full clause-initial temporal frame of its own, while 18:2's לְקֵ֨ץ is an adjunct subordinate to the already-fronted motion verb וַיֵּ֨רֶד, continuing the subject already established in v.1 rather than launching a new temporal frame. The row should argue this rather than assert its conclusion; neither correction disturbs the span.

The internal seam disposed of in the rejected alternative is likewise handled correctly on the syntax — v.9 opens וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֡ה יוֹשְׁבִים֩, a participial circumstantial clause setting the scene for action already in motion, not a new initiative. No mark falls anywhere in 18:1-16 (the chapter's first is SAMEKH keyed to 18:17, single-witness), so there is no tier-3 evidence this row could have cited or mistyped, and since neither dual-cite zone reaches chapter 18, its single-numbered refs stand as given. I find nothing here to adjudicate.

The opening quote and the verbatim-repetition claim both hold up: the four-hundred-prophets question occurs exactly twice in 2Chr, at 18:5 and 18:14, nowhere else. But the book strategy's own block map names this whole stretch, 18:4-27, as a scene to keep coherent, and the row's chosen rejected alternative, a hypothetical split at v.9, sidesteps the more obvious rival the strategy itself raises: not splitting 18:4-27 at all. A question asked verbatim twice, once of the crowd and once of the true prophet, is at least as readable as evidence of one doublet-structured scene bound together by repetition as it is evidence of a seam between two scenes, and the row never confronts that reading of its own best piece of evidence.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three quoted forms, all byte-identical to 20:1-3. The grammatical claim carrying the closing edge is verifiable and correct. In v.2 the king is a prepositional object under an unnamed plural subject (וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָט֙); v.3 makes him subject for the first time in the unit, with וַיִּרָ֕א taking an implicit third-person subject and וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט naming him; then v.4's subject is the collective in וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ יְהוּדָ֔ה. One descriptive refinement, not an objection: v.31's regnal data uses the בְּמָלְכ֗וֹ pattern attested at eighteen sites in 2Chr, and here it stands after the reign narrative rather than before it, as it also does at 21:20 — so 'accession notice' names the formula type accurately but not its position, which leaves the boundary function the row assigns it untouched. pmarks records no mark between 20:30 and 21:3.

Recognizing that the source-citation formula closes only this evaluative sub-block rather than the whole reign (correctly deferred to 21:1's actual death notice) shows real structural discipline, and the identification of Jehu ben Hanani as both the reign's opening prophetic voice and its closing historian is a genuine, textually demonstrated inclusio rather than an asserted one.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation is clean: the five Hebrew runs in this row (the 20:35 opener, the Tarshish infinitive phrase of 20:36, both 20:37 clauses, and the 21:1 death clause) reproduce their source verses byte for byte and each sits in the verse the row names. The unit's real anchorage is at its edges of content rather than in the marker it foregrounds: 20:34 carries the source-citation closer (וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֔ט ...), and 21:1 opens with וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו and ends with וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, so the death-plus-succession pairing the row invokes is literally present in one verse. Two original-language claims, however, are asserted at a precision the Hebrew does not bear. 20:1 and 20:35 are not the same formula — one is headed by a wayyiqtol of היה, the other by a plain conjunctive waw — and 16:13, offered as a specimen of the death-and-succession class, contains no succession clause at all. Neither defect touches the span itself, which the closing evidence holds independently, but both belong in the record. No dual-cite is owed anywhere here: chs 20-21 carry 37 and 20 verses in both witnesses, so MT and WEB numbering coincide.

challenges.claim: The opening is argued as “the same formula that opened the Moabite crisis at 20:1”, but the two forms differ in the Hebrew (tier-1 time-frame transition is the class at issue): 20:1 reads וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן — a wayyiqtol of היה heading the temporal phrase — while 20:35 reads וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן, a conjunctive waw with the adverbial fronted and no verb of occurrence. oshb:2Chr.20.1 sits in the refs array but its form is never sliced, so the identity is asserted rather than demonstrated. A book-wide sweep of אחרי כן in 2Chr returns five instances: the wayyiqtol-headed type at 20:1 and 24:4 (וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ן), the bare-waw type at 20:35 and 33:14, and a verse-final adverbial מֵאַֽחֲרֵי כֵֽן at 32:23. The one other bare-waw instance, וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּנָ֣ה חוֹמָ֣ה חִֽיצוֹנָ֣ה at 33:14, stands inside Manasseh's reign account after his restoration, so that lighter form is not an attested major-unit opener in this book.
challenges.suggested_action: Slice 20:1 byte-exact and restate the relation as a shared adverbial (אחרי כן) rather than a shared formula; carry the opening edge primarily on 20:34's source-citation closure and the participant/register change, both of which the row already possesses.

challenges.claim: Three verses are named as specimens of the death-and-succession notice. Two of them qualify: 9:31 ends וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ רְחַבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו and 12:16 ends וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲבִיָּ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו. The third does not — 16:13 in full reads וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אָסָ֖א עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיָּ֕מָת בִּשְׁנַ֛ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת לְמָלְכֽוֹ, a bare death notice with no succession member anywhere in the verse (Asa's successor is not named until 17:1). None of the three comparanda is mirrored into boundary_evidence_refs, which strategy §7 requires of every argued comparandum.
challenges.suggested_action: Swap 16:13 for a genuine two-member specimen — 27:9 reads וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹתָם֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו and is outside both offset zones — or relabel 16:13 explicitly as a death-formula-only instance; then mirror each retained comparandum into boundary_evidence_refs.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both edges hold up under inspection: the reopening אַחֲרֵי כֵן idiom, the Tarshish-ships notice, Eliezer's oracle, and its immediate wreck-fulfillment are correctly quoted and sequenced, and 21:1's death formula is a genuinely recurring reign-closer (confirmed independently at 9:31, 12:16, and 16:13), so the outward seam is sound. The one weak spot is a device-identification overreach: the row calls 20:35's opener ‘the same formula’ as 20:1's, when the two constructions differ in a way that matters for literary-form precision.

challenges.claim: The rationale calls 20:35's opener וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן ‘the same formula that opened the Moabite crisis at 20:1,’ but the two are not the same construction (tier-1 device-identification check): 20:1 reads וַיְהִי אֱַחֲרֵי כֵן בָּאוּ (a wayehi + adverbial-phrase + finite-verb narrative frame), while 20:35 reads וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן אֶתְחַבַּר (a bare vav-conjunctive directly on the adverbial phrase, with no preposed וַיְהִי). Both function as 'after this' time-transitions, but calling them 'the same formula' overstates the parallel.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise to a qualified claim (e.g., 'the same אַחֲרֵי כֵן idiom, here in a reduced construction lacking the preposed וַיְהִי') rather than asserting formula identity; the reopened-narrative-time argument itself still stands on the shared idiom regardless.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every repair here holds under independent testing. A consonantal sweep of אחרי כן over the whole book returns exactly the five hits the row names, and the typology it assigns to each is right: wayyiqtol-headed at 20:1 and 24:4, bare-waw at 20:35 and 33:14, and a prepositioned verse-final form at 32:23. The substituted death-formula comparandum is sound in a way the row does not even need to argue -- of the ten וישכב עם אבתיו verses in 2Chr, nine carry a succession clause inside the same verse, Asa's 16:13 being the lone exception, so the two-member characterisation now survives the sweep that previously embarrassed it. All twelve pointed Hebrew slices in this row collate byte-exact against the witness, the WEB excerpts are contiguous substrings of their verses, and no cited original-language reference falls inside an offset zone, so no dual-cite is owed. What remains is a single mis-glossed parenthetical on the one sweep member that carries no argumentative weight.

challenges.claim: The sweep describes 32:23's occurrence as "the unrelated verse-final idiom (a term expiring)". The verse-final placement is correct, but the gloss is not: 32:23 reads וַיִּנַּשֵּׂ֛א לְעֵינֵ֥י כָל הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מֵאַֽחֲרֵי כֵֽן, and WEB renders it "so that he was exalted in the sight of all nations from then on". The prepositioned מֵאַֽחֲרֵי כֵֽן marks a state obtaining onward from a point in time; nothing in the clause expires or reaches a terminus. The mis-gloss sits in prose added to cure OL-M8-2Chr-081-1, so it is repair-time text.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the parenthetical with an accurate one -- e.g. '(prepositioned form, "from then on")' -- or delete it; the instance count and the wayyiqtol/bare-waw typology are correct and need no other change.

primary_reviews.rationale: Confidence-high reign-closing boundary is well argued on its own terms; the reopened-time-frame case now rests on the shared idiom plus 20:34's source closure and the moral-register shift into the Tarshish venture, rather than on an overstated formula equivalence, and the death-succession comparanda are textually sound.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The outward seam holds up under independent collation: 20:34's source-citation closer and 21:1's death-plus-succession clause anchor both edges exactly as quoted. Where the row overreaches is philology, and LF and OL flag the same two spots from different angles, both confirmed against oshb. First, 20:1 opens with a wayehi-of-hayah frame (וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּ֣אוּ) while 20:35 drops the wayehi for a bare conjunctive waw directly on the adverbial (וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן אֶתְחַבַּר֙) — a real construction difference, not a stylistic quibble — so 'the same formula' overstates a shared idiom worn in two distinct syntactic dresses; OL's five-instance book sweep (20:1, 20:35, 24:4, 32:23, 33:14) independently reproduces exactly and confirms the split. Neither challenge asks the boundary to move; both ask for qualified language, which the reopened-narrative-time argument does not need to survive. All three claims verify as stated.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three slices, all exact. וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו does open 21:1 and וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו does close it, so calling the verse a paired notice describes what one verse actually contains rather than something inferred across verses; the 21:4 run reproduces that verse to its final word. The closing argument survives the sharpest test I can put to it: 21:5 begins בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה יְהוֹרָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ, a nominal clause with no narrative verb at all, which is about as clean a register break as Hebrew narrative offers after the wayyiqtol chain וַיָּ֨קָם יְהוֹרָ֜ם עַל מַמְלֶ֤כַת אָבִיו֙ ... running through v4. Two observations I record without raising them to challenges. WLC places a pe after 21:3, i.e. inside this span at the v3/v4 juncture — tier-3, single-witness, Writings, and by the contract incapable of driving a boundary on its own, so it does not disturb the row, though a future edit could disclose it. And the English given for WEB 21:4 supplies “and” where WEB has “he killed”; that reads as an elision artifact around the ellipsis rather than a gloss substituted for the translation, so I leave it below threshold.

The paired death-and-enthronement clause is quoted with the correct verb sequence (שכב/קבר/מלך), and the closing purge notice (וַיַּהֲרֹּג אֶת כָּל אֶחָיו) is the unit's own resolution rather than a borrowed comparandum; the rejected alternative correctly identifies vv5-7 as a distinct formulaic type (age-formula plus covenant clause) rather than forcing an artificial extension of this unit. I found no edge, quote, or ref problem here.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both sliced verses are byte-clean and correctly located, and the age formula at 21:5 is a real opener. What fails is the row's handling of the mark data and of its own rival reading. The pe recorded at 21:11 falls exactly where the row says no pe falls, so the row disowns weak corroboration it in fact has. Separately, the rejected alternative is built on a description of the Hebrew that does not hold: בְּיָמָיו֙ heads v8 and governs vv8-10 only, since vv5-7 begin בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה יְהוֹרָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ ..., וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ... and וְלֹא אָבָ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה ... respectively, none of which stands under a “in his days” frame; and a fronted temporal adverbial in verse-initial position is precisely the time-frame transition the contract lists as tier-1, so the assertion that no tier-1 marker intervenes is false at the very seam being dismissed. A third, smaller defect: the English attributed to WEB 21:11 is not WEB's wording. The span may yet be correct — vv8-11 do accumulate the charges Elijah's letter will name — but the defence of it has to be rebuilt.

challenges.claim: The row states that pe marks stand nearby “but none falls at this exact close”. pmarks_2Chr.json records "2Chr.21.11": "PE", and under the brief's convention a mark keyed to verse X follows verse X; this span closes at 21:11, so a pe stands exactly at the close (WLC single-witness, tier-3 in Writings, corroboration only). The nearby pe the row may have in view is at 21:3, which lies inside the preceding row's span, not at this edge. challenges.suggested_action: Rewrite the marker sentence to disclose the pe at 21:11 as weak single-witness corroboration of the close, explicitly non-driving; the topic pivot and the letter's back-reference stay the tier-1 basis, and the confidence grade need not move.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative refuses a split at v8 because the halves allegedly “share one continuous 'in his days' narrative frame ... with no tier-1 marker between them”. Neither half of that survives the Hebrew. בְּיָמָיו֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע אֱד֔וֹם opens v8; vv5-7 open בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה יְהוֹרָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ, וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל and וְלֹא אָבָ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה, so the temporal frame belongs to the second block alone and is not shared. And a verse-initial fronted temporal adverbial is a time-frame transition, tier-1 on the contract's own device list, so a tier-1 marker does stand between the halves. A book-wide sweep finds בימיו twice in 2Chr — here, and at oshb:2Chr.13.23 (MT) = web:2Chr.14.1, where it is verse-medial (בְּיָמָ֛יו שָׁקְטָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ ...) — making 21:8 the only verse-initial instance in the book, i.e. more marked than the row allows, not less.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-argue the rejected alternative on its merits (e.g. that the revolt notices of vv8-10 and the cult charge of v11 form one indictment list that the letter then recites), or split the row at 21:8; as written the dismissal rests on a false premise about the text.

challenges.claim: The English presented as WEB 21:11, “He also made high places in the mountains of Judah...”, is not the WEB text; 2Chr_web_clean.txt reads “Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and made the inhabitants of Jerusalem play the prostitute, and led Judah astray.” The substituted opening renders the Hebrew גַּם ה֥וּא directly while carrying a WEB attribution, which strategy §7 forbids (“translator glosses labeled as such, never presented as WEB text”).
challenges.suggested_action: Restore WEB's “Moreover he”, or keep the tighter rendering and label it as a gloss of גַּם ה֥וּא.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening age-formula restart at v.5 and the topical pivot to cultic apostasy at v.11 are both real and correctly quoted, and the letter's back-reference at vv12-13 does supply a legitimate forward anchor for the close. Two things weaken the row's own defense of its scope, though: it misreports the mark evidence at its own closing verse, and its rejected-alternative doesn't fully engage the strongest form of an internal split at v.8.

challenges.claim: The rationale states 'Pe marks Writings paragraph breaks nearby but none falls at this exact close,' but pmarks_2Chr.json records a PE keyed to 2Chr.21.11 (single-witness) — precisely this row's closing verse (a mark keyed to X follows verse X, per the mesh's mark convention). challenges.suggested_action: Correct the rationale to acknowledge the PE at oshb:2Chr.21.11 (single-witness) as available, if still non-driving, tier-3 corroboration for this closing edge, rather than denying its existence.

challenges.claim: V.8 opens with בְּיָמָיו פָּשַָע אֱדוֹם ('in his days Edom revolted,' WEB 21:8), introducing a wholly new subject (Edom) not present in vv5-7's covenant-promise clause; this reads as a candidate scene/participant-change seam (the device matrix's own category, cf. 10:1/19:1) inside the span this row merges. challenges.suggested_action: Either supply an explicit argument for why v.8's new-subject notice fails the participant-change category (e.g., because it stays inside one evaluative frame the letter later itemizes), or concede a live finer split at 21:5-7 | 21:8-11.

primary_reviews.rationale: The mark correction and the WEB restoration are exact, and the fronted-adverbial claim survives testing: בימיו occurs twice in 2Chr and only 21:8 is verse-initial, 13:23 being medial, with the offset zone properly dual-cited as MT 13:23 = WEB 14:1. The rejected alternative has been genuinely rewritten rather than patched. But the replacement reason it now offers -- that Elijah's letter recites the whole catalogue including the revolts -- is checkable against vv12-13 and does not hold, and since that reason is the sole thing keeping vv8-11 attached to vv5-7, the row's merger now rests on a second false premise where it previously rested on a first.

challenges.claim: The new merits argument asserts that the Edom and Libnah revolts (vv8-10) and the cult charge (v11) "build one continuous list of charges that Elijah's letter (12-13) recites as a totality". The letter recites no such thing. 21:12 charges only failure to walk in the ways of Jehoshaphat and Asa; 21:13 charges וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֨רֶךְ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, the prostitution of Judah and Jerusalem after the manner of Ahab's house, and וְגַ֨ם אֶת אַחֶ֧יךָ בֵית אָבִ֛יךָ הַטּוֹבִ֥ים מִמְּךָ֖ הָרָֽגְתָּ. Edom and Libnah are absent from both verses. Worse for the row, the one charge the letter adds beyond v.11 is the fratricide, which answers 21:4's וַיַּהֲרֹ֥ג אֶת כָּל אֶחָ֖יו בֶּחָ֑רֶב -- material outside this span, in the preceding row. So the letter's back-reference neither covers vv8-10 nor respects this row's own opening edge, and the catalogue-recital premise is false in both directions.
challenges.suggested_action: Rest the merger on something the text supports -- e.g. that vv8-11 accumulate under the evaluative verdict of vv6-7 -- or accept the split at 21:8 that the rejected alternative already concedes is live; either way, drop the claim that vv12-13 recite the revolt notices, and if the letter's back-reference is retained as an argument, disclose that it reaches v.4 as well as v.11.

primary_reviews.rationale: The revised row does more than the minimum: it concedes rather than dismisses the v.8 split candidate, correctly locates both pe marks, and the בימיו-count claim held up under an independent rerun (21:8 and 13:23 only, nowhere else). No fresh defect surfaced in this row's markup or quotations.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This row draws the heaviest challenge traffic in the cluster, and every item verifies. The mark-data error both primaries caught independently is real and singular: pmarks_2Chr.json keys a PE to 2Chr.21.11, this row's own closing verse, directly against the rationale's claim that 'none falls at this exact close.' primary_reviews.rationale: Every slice checks out, and the argument they carry is the best-evidenced in this cluster. The letter's opening frame stands where claimed (וַיָּבֹ֤א אֵלָיו֙ מִכְתָּ֔ב מֵֽאֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר), and the inset test is genuinely met rather than merely invoked: reading forward in Hebrew, v16 begins וַיָּ֨עַר יְהוָ֜ה עַל יְהוֹרָ֗ם with no resumption formula of any kind after the letter's last words, so the inset has an opening frame and no closing one and cannot be lifted out as a row. The binding the row asserts between curse and fulfilment is verifiable at the level of the lexeme, not merely of theme: וּבְבָנֶ֥יךָ וּבְנָשֶׁ֖יךָ וּבְכָל רְכוּשֶֽׁךָ in v14 recurs in v17 as כָּל הָרְכוּשׁ֙ הַנִּמְצָ֣א לְבֵית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ ... וְגַם בָּנָ֖יו וְנָשָׁ֑יו, the same three items — sons, wives, possessions — with the pronominal suffix turned from second person to third. That is the strongest single piece of internal evidence in the cluster and it holds. Minor and sub-threshold: vv15-16 carry argued content but appear in refs as web cites only, and the characterisation of v16 as a new-subject clause is asserted rather than sliced — correct as it happens, since יהוה is indeed the fresh subject there.

This is the strongest-argued row in the cluster: the letter's own frame is quoted correctly, and the lexical echo the row identifies between the curse's 'your children...your wives' (v14) and the fulfillment's 'his sons and his wives' (v17) is real and precisely located, giving the merge genuine textual teeth rather than resting on the inset rule alone. The v.18 'after all this' hand-off to the next row is exactly where the second curse (bowel disease) needs its own time-frame, so the two-curse structure is respected on both sides of this boundary.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening slice is exact, and measured against the whole book the marker is stronger than the row realises: וְאַחֲרֵ֖י כָּל זֹ֑את has exactly one counterpart in 2Chr, and that counterpart opens a major unit. The closing analysis is likewise right on the facts — 21:20 does resume the age-and-length notice of v5, and the sweep shows how unusual that is: of eighteen accession notices built on במלכו across the book, only two kings receive one twice, Jehoram here and Jotham at 27:1/27:8, and both repetitions take the same reduced shape in which הָיָה replaces the royal name (בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ; בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְחָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ). So my objection is not to the boundary, which I judge sound at both edges and honestly graded, but to the citation apparatus supporting it: the row reaches for a weaker analogue while the exact in-book parallels — permitted as literary evidence under §4 — go unnamed and unmirrored.

challenges.claim: The only comparandum offered for the opening time-marker is 8:1, וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה ..., a different construction and the sole instance of its own formula in the book, while the identical formula stands at 35:20: אַחֲרֵ֣י כָל זֹ֗את אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵכִ֤ין יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת עָלָ֞ה נְכ֧וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֛יִם ..., which opens the Necho unit the strategy's block map runs 35:20-27. The same gap affects the closing argument: 21:20 is called an age-formula repeat without reference to the one other king whose account closes the same way, Jotham at 27:8 (בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְחָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ), which shares 21:20's distinctive substitution of הָיָה for the king's name (בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ). Neither 8:1 nor 35:20 nor 27:8 appears in boundary_evidence_refs, contrary to strategy §7's requirement that argued comparanda be mirrored there.
challenges.suggested_action: Cite oshb:2Chr.35.20 as the in-book same-formula parallel for the opening and oshb:2Chr.27.8 for the repeated closing formula, and mirror every argued comparandum into boundary_evidence_refs; the high confidence grade is better supported with these than without them.

primary_reviews.rationale: The 'after all this' opener is a real, distinct time-marker separating this second curse-fulfillment from the first one closed out in the prior row, and the closing double formula (age-and-length restated, then the dishonorable-burial notice) is a clean reign-closer with its own textual weight. The rejected alternative's point — that folding vv16-17 in here would blur the very distinction v.18 draws — is correct and economically stated.

The added comparanda check out. מקץ occurs once in the book, so 8:1 is correctly called a single-instance formula; אחרי כל זאת at 35:20 does open the Necho unit and differs from 21:18 only by the conjunctive waw and the dagesh in כל, which the row honestly marks as 'near-identically' rather than identical; and the היה במלכו substitution occurs at exactly two places in 2Chr, 21:20 and 27:8, so the uniqueness claim is exhaustively true. Every argued comparandum is now mirrored into refs, and all nine pointed slices collate byte-exact. The one thing the repair states loosely is the shape of the substitution itself.

challenges.claim: The row describes 21:20 as v.5's formula "with the king's name replaced by הָיָה" and pairs it with 27:8 as sharing that same substitution. The two are not the same operation. 21:5 runs שָׁנָ֖ה יְהוֹרָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ and 21:20 runs בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ: both שָׁנָ֖ה and the royal name give way, and the preposition loses its dagesh (בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ becomes בְמָלְכ֔וֹ). 27:8's בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְחָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ keeps שָׁנָ֖ה and swaps only the name against 27:1's יוֹתָ֣ם. The row's own byte-exact slices display the difference, but the prose flattens it, so the claimed match is tighter than the forms are.
challenges.suggested_action: State the substitution precisely -- at 21:20 שָׁנָ֖ה plus the name yields הָיָה, at 27:8 the name alone does -- and note that what the two closings actually share is the הָיָה-for-name device, not an identical formula; the two-instance uniqueness result and the high confidence grade both survive the correction.

primary_reviews.rationale: High confidence is now earned rather than asserted: the opening and closing formulas each get a genuine in-book twin (35:20, 27:8) instead of a mismatched or absent comparandum, and 8:1 is retained only as an explicitly distinguished contrast rather than a false parallel.

challenges.claim: The span swallows a tier-1 seam that is never argued. (b) 22:2 opens the age-formula type, בֶּן אַרְבָּעִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ, listed in the strategy as a tier-1 regnal accession device and used as a row-opener by M8-2Chr-083 at 21:5 (בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה יְהוֹרָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ). primary_reviews.rationale: The cure is procedurally complete and unusually candid -- the row concedes the rival is the stronger one and invites the reader to weigh it -- so the disclosure obligations are discharged. The morphology is right too: וַיַּמְלִיכוּ֩ is hiphil, the following וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ is qal, both slices are byte-exact, and pmarks does key a PE to 22:1. The problem is with the substance of the new argument. The single ground it offers for treating the age formula as a completer at 22:2 but as an opener at 21:5 is a contrast that the text does not sustain, and a distance figure inside the same passage is off by more than an order of magnitude.

challenges.claim: The row declines the 22:1/22:2 split on the ground that the age formula opens a unit at 21:5 "where the preceding row had already closed a different king's account in full", implying that no such closure precedes 22:2. It does. 21:20 closes Jehoram completely -- summary age-and-length notice, the unregretted departure, and burial outside the royal tombs -- immediately before 22:1, exactly as 21:1's death, burial and succession clause closes Jehoshaphat immediately before 21:2. In both cases the previous king's account is fully shut, then new-king material intervenes (21:2-4: the brothers, the inheritance, and Jehoram's own consolidation and fratricide; 22:1: Ahaziah's installation), and only then does the age formula arrive. The stated contrast is therefore present on both sides and distinguishes nothing; if anything it cuts the other way, since three verses of new-king narrative intervene at 21:5 against one at 22:2.
challenges.suggested_action: Either find a ground that actually separates the two seams -- the most promising being that 22:1's installation clause names the agents (יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם) and supplies a causal כִּ֤י that has no counterpart at 21:1 -- or adopt the 22:1 | 22:2-9 split the row already calls the stronger rival; the present reason cannot bear the weight it is given.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative places the comparandum "four verses earlier, at 21:5". Chapter 21 has twenty verses in both witnesses and chapter 22 is unaffected by any offset zone, so 21:5 stands seventeen verses before 22:2, with sixteen verses intervening; in decision terms it is three rows earlier, not four verses.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the figure to seventeen verses (or state the distance in rows), so the reader is not told the two age formulas are near neighbours when they sit on opposite sides of a complete reign account.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both defects are cured with real argumentative work rather than cosmetic patching: the strongest rival, splitting at 22:2, is now the one actually engaged, and the row is candid that a reader could weigh the completion-relationship differently. Full-span citation also brings this row into line with its cluster-mates.

(32:5) — plus two infinitives inside speeches at 13:8 and 16:9. That is royal-installation material, formally distinct from the Baal-house demolition and priestly reorganization of vv17-19, and it is the strongest internal candidate in the span.

challenges.claim: The opening edge is carried by the claim that v.16's covenant is "distinct in party and scope from the conspirators' earlier pact ... rather than the captains' covenant of vv1/3". Verse 3 is not the captains' covenant. It reads וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת כָּל הַקָּהָ֥ל בְּרִ֛ית בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עִם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ -- the whole assembly cutting a covenant with the king in God's house -- against v.16's וַיִּכְרֹ֤ת יְהוֹיָדָע֙ בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינ֕וֹ וּבֵ֥ין כָּל הָעָ֖ם וּבֵ֣ין הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ, Jehoiada with all the people and the king. Only 23:1 is a captains' covenant. The two parties therefore overlap almost entirely (assembly/people plus king in both), and what genuinely distinguishes v.16 is not its party but its purpose clause, לִהְי֥וֹת לְעָ֖ם לַיהוָֽה, which converts a dynastic pact into a Yahweh-covenant. As written, half of the two-part ground for the opening edge is false to 23:3.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop 'party' from the distinction and rest the opening on the purpose clause plus the change of covenanting agent (Jehoiada rather than the assembly), and correct 'the captains' covenant of vv1/3' to 'the captains' covenant of v.1 and the assembly's dynastic pact of v.3'.

challenges.claim: Three quotations carrying WEB attributions in this row do not reproduce the witness. (i) v.20 is quoted as "they brought the king down from Yahweh's house"; WEB reads 'and brought the king down from Yahweh's house', governed by the singular 'He' of 'He took the captains of hundreds'. The substituted plural also misstates the Hebrew, which alternates deliberately: וַיּ֤וֹרֶד is 3ms, matching וַיִּקַּ֣ח, while וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ and וַיּוֹשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ are 3mp. That alternation is material here, because the row's rejected alternative rests on v.20 supplying 'a genuine change of location and cast'. (ii) WEB 22:10 is quoted with an inserted conjunction, 'and she arose' -- precisely the defect adjudicated at OL-M8-2Chr-087-1 and duly cured in row 087, left standing here in a row that quotes the same verse. (iii) WEB 23:21's sentence break is replaced by a semicolon ('the city was quiet; they had slain'), where the witness has 'the city was quiet. They had slain Athaliah with the sword.'
challenges.suggested_action: Quote WEB verbatim in all three places, or mark the tighter renderings as glosses; at v.20 in particular either use WEB's wording or gloss the Hebrew accurately, preserving the 3ms bringing-down against the 3mp entering and enthroning, since the participant shift is part of what the row is arguing about.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Three threads converge on one six-verse row graded high. LF is right that the 22:10/23:21 'inclusio' shares only a mot root (מֵ֣ת בְּנָ֑הּ, qal, her son's dying; הֵמִ֥יתוּ בֶחָֽרֶב, hiphil, her own killing) rather than a repeated phrase, unlike the strategy's own confirmed 1:14-17/9:25-28 or 5:13/7:3 pairs -- a motif echo, not a formal bracket. OL's second point confirms the same weakness from the other end: the 22:10 excerpt the row actually quotes stops at וַתָּ֗קָם ('she arose'), one clause short of the verse's violent act, וַתְּדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת כָּל זֶ֥רַע הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה ('she destroyed all the royal offspring'), so the claimed violence-to-violence symmetry is asserted rather than shown from what's cited. OL's first point stands apart and matters more: v20's procession-and-enthronement text (וַיִּקַּ֣ח... וַיּ֤וֹרֶד אֶת הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה... וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ... בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ... וַיּוֹשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ אֶת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א הַמַּמְלָכָֽה, byte-checked clean) moves the scene bodily out of the temple into the palace with a changed cast and a throne act -- a location/participant shift of the class the device matrix names -- and it sits unengaged between the priestly-purge material and the covenant recap, with no interior tier-3 mark to complicate the picture either way. All three claims are supported. Softening 'inclusio' doesn't touch the span, but the v20 candidate is a genuine internal rival the row doesn't meet; that confidence question belongs to the author/boss round, not to me.

primary_reviews.rationale: Four Hebrew excerpts, four clean collations; the accession formula of 24:1 runs intact to מִבְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע. I tested the device identification rather than accepting it: a book-wide sweep for verse-initial 'ben' plus the mother-name slot returns exactly five specimens (22:2, 24:1, 25:1, 26:3, 27:1), so the age-formula class is real and 24:1 belongs to it. The bracket is genuinely exclusive too — the sequence 'days of Jehoiada' occurs at 24:2 and 24:14 and nowhere else in 2Chr. PE keyed to 2Chr.24.14 is typed correctly and no mark interrupts 24:1-24:13. The v11 gloss the row quotes as WEB matches כֹּ֤ה עָשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם בְּי֔וֹם. What does not survive scrutiny is the load the inclusio is made to bear against the time-frame transition standing inside it, and the description of the bracket as a verbatim repetition.

challenges.claim: The row concedes that וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ן opens the repair narrative at 24:4 and then declines to divide, on the ground that the Jehoiada bracket makes vv2-14 one accountable unit. Time-frame transitions are a tier-1 boundary-driving class in the strategy's own device matrix, and a consonantal sweep of the whole book returns this collocation exactly twice — 24:4 and 20:1, where וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּ֣אוּ בְנֵי מוֹאָב֩ opens the Moabite invasion as a full unit-opener. An inclusio is a repetition device and is logically compatible with an internal division; bracketing vv2-14 does not by itself neutralise a tier-1 opener standing inside the bracket. The merge yields a 14-verse row against a 5.12 vv/row mean for this cluster.
challenges.suggested_action: Either divide at 24:4 (accession and evaluation 24:1-3 | temple-repair project 24:4-14), or keep the merge and meet the tier-1 opener head-on — arguing, if it can be argued, that the bracket outranks it — and drop the grade below medium if the merge is retained without that argument.

challenges.claim: 'That exact phrase recurs to close the unit at v14' misdescribes the two forms the row itself quotes. 24:2 reads כָּל יְמֵ֖י יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן; 24:14 reads תָּמִ֔יד כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹיָדָֽע. The quantifier is pointed כָּל in v2 but כֹּ֖ל in v14, and the appositional הַכֹּהֵֽן present in v2 is absent in v14. The shared consonantal skeleton is exclusive to these two verses, which is what makes the bracket real — but the recurrence is lexical, not verbatim.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword to something like 'the same phrase recurs, shorn of the appositional title', so the inclusio claim states what the two forms actually share and does not overstate the repetition it rests on.

primary_reviews.rationale: The bracket holds at both named edges – 24:1's age-formula and 24:2's closing כָּל יְמֵ֖י יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן both quote correctly, and 24:14 does echo that phrase at its close (תָּמִ֔יד כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹיָדָֽע). But the echo isn't as tight as 'exact phrase' suggests: v2 has הַכֹּהֵֽן ('the priest') where v14 doesn't, v14 adds תָּמִ֔יד ('continually') where v2 doesn't, and 'all' is spelled כָּל in v2 against כֹּ֖ל in v14. That gap matters here specifically because the row leans on this inclusio to keep v4's own opening, וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ן, from splitting off the repair narrative – and 'after this' is the same time-frame-transition class the strategy names as boundary-driving elsewhere in the book. Fourteen verses under one decision, against a ~6-7vv/decision target, is already the outlier in this cluster; a weaker inclusio makes that outlier harder to defend.

challenges.claim: The rationale states 'that exact phrase recurs to close the unit at v14,' but the Hebrew is not identical: 24:2 reads כָּל יְמֵ֖י יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן while 24:14 reads תָּמִ֔יד כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹיָדָֽע – v14 adds the adverb 'continually,' drops 'the priest,' and spells 'all' with a different vowel letter than v2. Since this overstated inclusio is the stated reason for not splitting at v4's own tier-1-eligible time-frame opener וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ן (the same device class as the 'after these things' formula named in book_strategy_draft.md §1), the case against a split is weaker than presented.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every load-bearing assertion here survives independent checking. A consonantal sweep of the whole book returns the wayehi-plus-acharei-ken collocation at precisely two addresses, 20:1 and 24:4, so 'exactly once more in the book' is correct rather than approximate; the cross-reference to M8-2Chr-076 also carries the right span, 2Chr.20.1-2Chr.20.3, which I read off the frozen row set rather than accepting on trust. The bracket the row leans on is real and narrow: the skeleton כל ימי יהוידע occurs at 24:2 and 24:14 and nowhere else in 2Chr, and the two forms differ exactly as the revised text now says. Both quoted forms and the accession formula byte-collate against the witness. The single-witness PE after 24:14 is confirmed in pmarks, and no space-mark falls anywhere inside 24:1-13, so there is no undisclosed interior marking to hold against the row. What I find most creditable is that the repair did not paper over the difficulty: the row now states plainly that the inclusio does not outrank the opener standing inside it, and pays for the retained merge with a grade drop. A 14-verse span remains an outlier, but the row no longer misrepresents its own warrant, and re-litigating a merge that was repaired along the exact path the adjudication authorised would be reopening settled ground.

The cure work here is genuine: all three original items are fixed, and the downgrade to medium_low honestly reflects that the 20:1 parallel is a live rival the row cannot defeat outright. But the repair introduces two problems of its own. First, in place of the discarded inclusio-alone defense, the rationale now leans on a new comparison -- the repair narrative's register paralleling unnamed 'construction catalogs... elsewhere in the book' -- without naming a single specimen decision or verse, and without mirroring anything into boundary_evidence_refs. That is the same uncited-comparandum defect this cluster's own LF-096-1 and OL-096-1 challenges required to be named-and-mirrored or dropped, resurfacing here as a repair-time regression in a different row. Second, both the rationale and its rejected-alternative drift into narrating their own revision rather than arguing from the text -- phrases about what 'this row does not defeat outright' and a defense being 'not as decisive as the earlier phrasing implied' only make sense to someone who has seen the prior draft. A frozen decision record has to stand on its own.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative both narrate the row's own revision rather than arguing from the text: the rationale states the row 'does not defeat outright' the 20:1 rival, and the rejected-alternative calls its own defense 'not as decisive as the earlier phrasing implied.' Both phrasings only make sense with knowledge of a prior draft state that the frozen record does not otherwise reference.
challenges.suggested_action: Rewrite these as direct claims about the text and the rival opener alone -- e.g. state that the 20:1 parallel is a live rival this argument does not defeat outright -- and remove the comparison to an 'earlier phrasing,' which is process narration that does not belong in the permanent record.

challenges.claim: The replacement argument for keeping vv1-14 whole -- that the repair sequence's register-like, procedural character parallels the treatment 'construction catalogs' receive 'elsewhere in the book' -- names no specimen verse or decision and mirrors nothing into boundary_evidence_refs, the same uncited-comparandum pattern LF-M8-2Chr-096-1 and OL-M8-2Chr-096-1 already required this cluster to fix in a sibling row.
challenges.suggested_action: Name the specific construction-catalog comparanda intended (for example, specific fortification or building-project rows elsewhere in 2Chr) and add them to boundary_evidence_refs, or drop the claim and let the conceded-weak inclusio carry the argument alone, adjusting confidence further if it cannot.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both primaries independently challenged this row and their three claims are one finding under two names, so I rule them together as instructed. First, the wording: 24:2's כָּל יְמֵ֖י יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן and 24:14's תָּמִ֔יד כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹיָדָֽע share a 'kol yemei Yehoyada' skeleton found nowhere else in the book -- I swept 2Chr_oshb.txt myself and it returns exactly these two verses -- real enough to fence the unit, but v14 adds תָּמִיד and drops הַכֹּהֵן, so 'exact phrase' overstates a side-by-side check; 'the same phrase recurs, shorn of its title' is the accurate description. Second, and more consequential: the row leans on that bracket to absorb 24:4's own opener, וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ן, without meeting it as a rival on its own footing. That specific vayehi-plus-acharei-ken collocation (distinct from the weaker ve-/me-acharei-ken forms at 20:35, 32:23, 33:14) occurs exactly twice in 2Chr: here and at 20:1 -- and the frozen record itself supplies the clincher neither primary cited: decision M8-2Chr-076 (span 2Chr.20.1-2Chr.20.3) already treats this identical formula as sufficient, alone, to open a fresh unit there ('opens a new crisis unrelated to the judicial reform just closed'). An inclusio bracketing a span does not by itself neutralize a tier-1 opener standing inside it, and the campaign's own prior ruling on the twin occurrence undercuts the case for silently absorbing it here. The 14-verse span is also this cluster's outlier against a 5.125 vv/row mean (41 verses over 8 rows, recomputed and matching OL's figure exactly). All three claims -- LF-M8-2Chr-091-1, OL-M8-2Chr-091-1, OL-M8-2Chr-091-2 -- are supported as stated. Whether 24:1-3 and 24:4-14 should separate is a genuine span/confidence question I flag rather than resolve; the row's existing medium grade already registers some doubt, but the newly-surfaced 20:1 precedent suggests the doubt runs deeper than medium concedes.
