primary_reviews.rationale: The obituary's two excerpts reproduce 24:15 and 24:16 exactly, the age notice בֶּן מֵאָ֧ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּמוֹתֽוֹ included. SAMEKH keyed to 2Chr.24.16 is typed as pmarks has it, single-witness. I did not take the burial contrast on trust: the phrase for burying in David's city occurs four times in the book (9:31, 21:20, 24:16, 24:25), and of those only 24:16 continues עִם הַמְּלָכִ֑ים with the honour rationale כִּֽי עָשָׂ֤ה טוֹבָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, while 21:20 closes וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וְלֹ֖א בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים and 24:25 closes וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וְלֹ֥א קְבָרֻ֖הוּ בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים. So the contrast is real and the hinge reading is sound — the Jehoiada bracket on one side and the death-of-Jehoiada marker on the other genuinely fence this notice off. The defect is confined to the refs array, which does not carry two of the comparanda the rationale argues from.

challenges.claim: The rationale argues two comparanda that boundary_evidence_refs does not hold. It contrasts this honourable burial with 'Joash's own (24:25)', and it identifies the notice as the pivot between 'all the days of Jehoiada' at v2/v14 and 'after the death of Jehoiada' at v17 — yet only web:2Chr.21.20, web:2Chr.24.14 and web:2Chr.24.17 are mirrored; 24:25 and 24:2 are absent. The strategy requires every argued comparandum to appear in the refs array, and a burial-formula contrast that turns on Hebrew wording cannot be audited downstream from WEB refs alone.
challenges.suggested_action: Add web:2Chr.24.25 and web:2Chr.24.2 to boundary_evidence_refs, with oshb counterparts for 21:20 and 24:25 if the burial formulae are to carry the contrast in the original. The span, the hinge argument and the high grade are all unaffected.

primary_reviews.rationale: This obituary is short and both quoted edges land where claimed: 24:15's age-and-death notice (וַיִּזְקַ֧ן יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע וַיִּשְׂבַּ֥ע יָמִ֖ים וַיָּמֹ֑ת בֶּן מֵאָ֧ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּמוֹתֽוֹ) and 24:16's burial rationale (עִם הַמְּלָכִ֑ים כִּֽי עָשָׂ֤ה טוֹבָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל) both match 2Chr_oshb.txt exactly, and the samekh after 24:16 matches pmarks_2Chr.json. The honorable-burial reading does contrast with the two dishonorable notices the rationale cites, and I checked both: 21:20's וְלֹ֖א בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים and 24:25's וְלֹ֥א קְבָרֻ֖הוּ בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים share the core 'not in the tombs of the kings' collocation, so the contrast is real, not asserted. The hinge framing (between v2/14's 'days of Jehoiada' and v17's 'after the death of Jehoiada') is exactly right and doesn't overreach.

The mirroring defect is fully repaired and the repair went further than the action required, adding oshb:2Chr.24.2 and rebuilding the contrast around the two Hebrew burial clauses. Those clauses check out: 21:20 closes וְלֹא בְּקִבְרוֹת הַמְּלָכִים, 24:25 closes וְלֹא קְבָרֻהוּ בְּקִבְרוֹת הַמְּלָכִים, both verse-final, and the resumptive קְבָרֻהוּ is indeed unattested as an independent form anywhere else in 2Chr (the nine other hits for that consonantal string are all wayyiqtol וַיִּקְבְּרֻהוּ). The hinge argument holds as well: 24:17 opens וְאַחֲרֵי מוֹת יְהוֹיָדָע, which presupposes the obituary instead of continuing it. Where the revised text slips is at its own closing edge. It reports the row as closing on the honourable-burial rationale and puts the SAMEKH immediately after that phrase, but 24:16 carries two further words past the quotation, and the mark sits after them. One further observation I record without filing: the row argues a Hebrew-level phrase pairing across v2/v14/v17 while mirroring only web:2Chr.24.14 and web:2Chr.24.17, so the original-language side of that pairing is unmirrored; and the WEB rendering given for 24:15 silently converts the translation's full stop into a semicolon and drops its opening 'But'. Neither touches the span, the hinge, or the high grade, all of which I would keep.

challenges.claim: The closing-edge sentence misplaces both the terminus and the space-mark. It reports that the row 'closes on the honorable-burial rationale עִם הַמְּלָכִ֑ים כִּֽי עָשָׂ֤ה טוֹבָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל' and that 'the lone witness sets a SAMEKH right after'. The witness reads 24:16 as וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בְעִיר דָּוִ֖יד עִם הַמְּלָכִ֑ים כִּֽי עָשָׂ֤ה טוֹבָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעִ֥ם הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבֵיתֽוֹ, so the quoted words stop two words short of the verse end; the SAMEKH recorded in pmarks_2Chr.json stands after וּבֵיתֽוֹ, not after בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל. primary_reviews.rationale: Every Hebrew form here is genuine and correctly placed. וְאַֽחֲרֵ֥י מוֹת֙ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע heads 24:17 with the plene spelling of the name that WLC actually carries, and the oracle frame of 24:20 is quoted without error. Two elements of that frame are singletons in the book, which is stronger than the row claims for itself: the Spirit-clothing form לָֽבְשָׁה֙ occurs once in 2Chr, and the messenger formula כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים likewise once — every other prophetic incipit in the book (eight of them, 11:4, 12:5, 18:10, 20:15, 21:12, 34:23, 34:24, 34:26) names Yahweh rather than God in that slot. The dying words at 24:22, יֵ֥רֶא יְהוָ֖ה וְיִדְרֹֽשׁ, are a jussive pair and the WEB rendering the row reproduces is the published one. The mark the row cites at the close matches what pmarks assigns after 2Chr.24.22, a PE on the sole witness. I pressed the rival the row rejects — isolating the oracle at 24:20 — and it fails on the stated inset test, which requires an opening frame and a resumption after it: 24:21 opens וַיִּקְשְׁר֣וּ עָלָ֔יו וַיִּרְגְּמֻ֥הוּ אֶ֖בֶן, a narrative consequence of the speech rather than any resumption formula, so the second condition is unmet and the oracle stays with its host. For completeness I disclose an interior datum the row does not mention: pmarks carries a SAMEKH keyed to 2Chr.24.19 (single-witness), aligned with the 19/20 seam. Being tier 3 it can neither drive a division nor be pressed as counterevidence, and I do not press it. Both edges rest on time-frame transitions, the strongest device available in this stretch, which is why the high grade survives despite the strategy flagging 24:17-22 as an expected low-confidence region.

The antithesis framing at v17 is textually earned: וְאַֽחֲרֵ֥י מוֹת֙ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע opens exactly as quoted, deliberately answering the 'days of Jehoiada' bracket just closed. Zechariah's oracle-frame at v20 (וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד מֵעַ֣ל לָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים) and the dying imprecation closing v22 (וּכְמוֹת֣וֹ אָמַ֔ר יֵ֥רֶא יְהוָ֖ה וְיִדְרֹֽשׁ) both quote correctly, and the pe after 24:22 matches pmarks_2Chr.json. The inset-rule application is sound: v21's stoning follows the oracle with no resumption formula between them, so keeping the oracle inside its host account rather than carving it out as its own row is the correct reading of the rule as stated in the strategy, not a stretch of it.

primary_reviews.rationale: All four excerpts collate cleanly against the witness. The opening marker is more distinctive than the row asserts: the noun לִתְקוּפַ֣ת occurs nowhere else in 2Chr, so the year-turn transition at 24:23 is unique in the book. I also tested the closing-pair identification book-wide rather than accepting the word 'fixed': the source-citation core הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים appears with eleven attestations (16:11, 20:34, 24:27, 25:26, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:19, 35:25, 35:27, 36:8) and the succession clause pattern behind וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו appears thirteen times, so the row's hedged 'nearly every reign account' is sustainable. Two observations I record without pressing them: the object מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים is unique to this verse (the noun for the source-work elsewhere only at 13:22, the book-title only at 16:11), and the incipit the strategy names for this formula class is not present at 24:27 — but the row never claims it is, and the formula core is genuinely recurrent. What does need work is an unengaged internal signal at v26 and an asserted cross-reign phrase identity that the Hebrew does not quite bear.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative disposes of a vv26-27 split by appeal to the inseparability of the v27 pair, but never touches the signal that actually opens v26: וְאֵ֖לֶּה הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִ֣ים עָלָ֑יו זָבָ֗ד בֶּן שִׁמְעָת֙ הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֔ית וִיה֣וֹזָבָ֔ד בֶּן שִׁמְרִ֖ית הַמּוֹאָבִֽית. Verse-initial waw-plus-demonstrative occurs four times in 2Chr — 3:3, 8:10, 17:14 and 24:26 — and in each of the other three it heads a list or register (foundation measurements, chief officers, the muster by fathers' houses). List and register formulas are a named tier-1 class in the device matrix, so 24:26 is the strongest internal candidate in this span, and it is the one the rebuttal does not reach.

primary_reviews.rationale: The time-marker opener at v23, וַיְהִ֣י לִתְקוּפַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה עָלָיו֮ חֵ֣יל אֲרָם֒, answers Zechariah's curse on schedule and quotes correctly, as does the conspirators' motive clause at v25 (הִתְקַשְּׁר֨וּ עָלָ֜יו עֲבָדָ֗יו בִּדְמֵי֙ בְּנֵי֙ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵ֔ן) and the source-citation/succession pair closing v27 (הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים; וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו); the pe after 24:27 matches pmarks_2Chr.json. The claim that v25's assassination notice echoes 21:20's dishonorable-burial language for Jehoram holds up: both share the same 'city of David...not in the tombs of the kings' collocation, differing only in whether the burial verb is stated or elided. Treating vv23-27 as one closing unit, rather than carving off the source-citation pair, is right – that pair is the fixed formula ending nearly every reign in this book and can't stand alone.

Both adjudicated defects were addressed substantively, not cosmetically. The arithmetic of the burial comparison is exact — the two denials differ by one inserted word and no more — and קְבָרֻהוּ really is a book-wide singleton as an independent form. The sweep behind the v26 discussion is also right: verse-initial waw-plus-demonstrative occurs at 3:3, 8:10, 17:14 and 24:26, those four and no others, and each of the first three does head a register. The closing pair is verse-final in 24:27 and the PE there is confirmed. Two problems remain, both of them created or left standing by the repair itself. First, the demonstrative at 24:26 does not do the anaphoric work the new argument assigns to it; the words that tie v26 to v25 are different ones, and one of the row's own three comparanda behaves the same way, so the contrast as drawn does not separate them. Second, the row now argues at length about the v25/v26 juncture while continuing to cite marker evidence on one side only: the witness sets a SAMEKH after 24:25, interior to this span and standing precisely at the division the adjudication told this row to test. Neither objection disturbs the span, which I would still keep whole, or the grade.

challenges.claim: The cure argument attributes the v25 dependence to the wrong element. It says that at 24:26 'its demonstrative is anaphoric to the assassination just narrated in v25, not a self-standing catalog opener'. The demonstrative אֵ֖לֶּה in וְאֵ֖לֶּה הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִ֣ים עָלָ֑יו זָבָ֗ד ... וִיה֣וֹזָבָ֔ד points forward to the two names that follow it, exactly as at 3:3 (וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה, forward to the measurements), 8:10 and 17:14. What actually reaches back to v25 is the 3ms suffix on עָלָ֑יו, whose antecedent is the Joash killed in v25, together with the participle הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִ֣ים echoing that verse's finite הִתְקַשְּׁר֨וּ עָלָ֜יו. The contrast as drawn also fails to separate 24:26 from its own third comparandum: 17:14 reads וְאֵ֥לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם, a cataphoric demonstrative carrying two anaphoric 3mp suffixes back to 17:13, i.e. the same profile the row treats as distinctive of 24:26.
challenges.suggested_action: Relocate the dependence onto עָלָ֑יו and onto the participle's repetition of v25's verb — which is what the adjudicated action asked for when it said the absorption had to be argued from the register's brevity and its dependence on v25's pronoun — and drop or qualify the demonstrative contrast, noting that 17:14 shares the cataphoric-demonstrative-plus-anaphoric-suffix pattern so the distinguishing work must be done by the verbal echo rather than by אֵלֶּה. No span change follows; the absorption of v26 remains the right call on the corrected grounds.

primary_reviews.rationale: 25:1 and 25:2 are transcribed exactly, the formula running to וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְהוֹעַדָּ֖ן מִירוּשָׁלָֽיִם without a slip and the evaluation preserving its restrictive tail רַ֕ק לֹ֖א בְּלֵבָ֥ב שָׁלֵֽם. The comparative claim I verified rather than assumed, and it is true: verse-initial 'ben' with the mother-name slot yields five book-wide specimens, and the two later ones are בֶּן שֵׁ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ at 26:3 and בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יוֹתָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ at 27:1, each carrying the full accession-age, reign-length and mother triad, and both falling inside the same writer part. primary_reviews.rationale: Both Hebrew strings check out character for character, and the PE cited after 25:16 matches pmarks. The opening device is “וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵ֨י ב֤וֹא”, wayehi with a preposition governing an infinitive construct, and the row's class claim survives a book-wide sweep: the sequence occurs three times in 2Chr, at 20:1 (“וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן”, opening the Moabite-Ammonite invasion), at 24:4 (“וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ן”, opening Joash's temple-restoration project) and here. Both comparanda do head major episodes, and 25:14's infinitive-construct variant is the only one of its kind in the book. I pressed the obvious counter — that v16 opens on the same wayehi framing, “וַיְהִ֣י בְּדַבְּר֣וֹ אֵלָ֗יו” — and it does not generate a rival seam: bet plus suffixed infinitive construct encodes simultaneity within a running scene, whereas the preposition of anteriority plus infinitive construct encodes transition between scenes, so despite the shared wayehi these are different devices doing different work. The close is verse-final and is the prophet's own utterance, “כִּֽי עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּ֔את וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ לַעֲצָתִֽי”. Edges hold on both sides; high confidence is defensible.

challenges.claim: The row makes v20 an opener, but the Hebrew reads it as retrospective comment. (i) Sweeping the negated-listening clause across 2Chr returns four instances (10:15, 25:16, 25:20, 35:22) and not one of the other three heads a narrative unit; the closest structural twin, “וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי הָיְתָ֤ה נְסִבָּה֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים”, carries the identical waw-negative-qatal-subject plus causal divine-agency shape and sits at the end of the refused-counsel exchange in ch.10, the sequel opening only at 10:16. (ii) V20's causal clause, “כִּ֣י דָֽרְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֱדֽוֹם”, answers the prophet's charge at v15, “לָ֤מָּה דָרַ֨שְׁתָּ֙ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם”; that verb-plus-noun collocation occurs five times in the book (19:3, 25:15, 25:20, 26:5, 31:21) and 25:15 with 25:20 is its only chapter-internal pair, so v20 reaches back across the taunt-exchange to the idolatry scene. The listening echo runs the same direction, v16 ending “וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ לַעֲצָתִֽי”. (iii) The feminine pronoun “הִ֔יא” has no antecedent within v20 — in the 10:15 twin the antecedent noun is present — which is what one expects of a comment clause and not of an episode head. Meanwhile v21 carries exactly the episode-opening syntax the row wants at v20: “וַיַּ֨עַל יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙”, wayyiqtol with the incoming king re-nominated under full title. All comparanda are in-book; no synoptic material is used.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-test 25:17-20 | 25:21-24 against the frozen 17-19 | 20-24. If v20 is kept as this row's opener, ground it on something other than the negated-listening clause, whose in-book distribution gives it no unit-initial use.

challenges.claim: The seam-out is misdescribed. The row says v25 opens with a fresh subject-led lifespan formula, but 25:25 begins “וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ”: apocopated wayyiqtol first, the proper-noun subject after it. Nothing is fronted, and the clause is unmarked narrative order. The label matters because this same cluster uses the same wording for “וַאֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔ק” at 25:11, where the subject does precede the verb, so two opposite word orders end up sharing one description.
challenges.suggested_action: Call 25:25 verb-initial wayyiqtol with postposed subject, and rest the seam-out on the topical shift to lifespan reckoning rather than on word order.

primary_reviews.rationale: The pivot from Joash’s quoted taunt into וְלֹא שָׁמַע אֲמַצְיָהוּ is a clean, negated disjunctive clause replacing direct speech with narratorial judgment, and the row closes on the return-to-Samaria notice right before v25’s fresh lifespan formula opens the next reign-summary.

Both original defects are genuinely repaired, and the repair is honest about what it concedes. Every Hebrew string in the row collates byte-exact against the witness at the verse the row assigns it to, including the v24 terminus וַיָּ֖שָׁב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן, which is indeed the last clause of oshb:2Chr.25.24, and the PE the row credits after v24 is present in pmarks_2Chr.json (single-witness, correctly weighted). What the repair introduced instead is an unresolved asymmetry. The row now leans hard on 10:15 as the structural twin and states in its own words that that clause looks back at the finished exchange rather than opening what starts at 10:16 -- so at ch.10 the hinge is filed with the material before it. At 25:20 the identically shaped hinge is filed with the material after it. Calling both a verdict-hinge does not by itself supply the criterion that sends one backward and the other forward, and the row's causal reading of v20 (כִּ֣י דָֽרְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֱדֽוֹם answering the prophet at v15) points backward as well. That is a defect the repair created, since the ch.10 comparandum was not in the frozen row at all. Confidence medium is appropriate and the row's flagging of v21 is good practice; the argument still needs the missing criterion. Marks: PE after 25:24 confirmed; no mark falls at 25:19/20, and I treat that absence as nothing at all, per the contract.

challenges.claim: The ch.10 comparandum the repair imported is applied in opposite directions in the same paragraph. The row asserts that וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל at 10:15 "likewise looks back at the just-finished exchange rather than opening the section that follows at 10:16" -- i.e. the hinge groups with the preceding unit there, and וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹא opens the sequel. At 25:20 the row takes the same waw-negative-qatal-plus-divine-causation shape and groups it with the following unit, letting וַיַּ֨עַל יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ at v21 be only a rival rather than the opener. No criterion is offered for the reversal, and the row's own causal analysis of v20 runs backward too: the clause answers the prophet's charge at v15 and the king's refusal at v16. As written the strongest support adduced for the boundary is evidence against it.
challenges.suggested_action: State the criterion that files the ch.10 hinge with what precedes it while filing the 25:20 hinge with what follows (for instance, that ch.10's sequel is a quoted popular response whereas 25:21 narrates the consequence the verdict predicts), or re-test 25:17-20 | 25:21-24 against the frozen 20-24 and let the comparandum decide.

challenges.claim: The English attached to the v24 terminus is not WEB and is not marked as anything else. The row writes "he returned to Samaria" in the same curly-quote form it uses for the five renderings in this row that do check out; web:2Chr.25.24 reads "and the hostages, and returned to Samaria", with no subject pronoun on that verb. book_strategy_draft.md section 7 requires translator glosses to be labelled as such and never presented as WEB text. I collated all 24 English quotations across the cluster against the WEB witness; this is the single one that fails.
challenges.suggested_action: Either quote web:2Chr.25.24 verbatim for the clause, or keep the smoother rendering and mark it as a gloss.

primary_reviews.rationale: The revision does not merely patch the wording flagged by the challenges; it reverses the underlying analysis, now treating v20 as the narrator's verdict-hinge rather than an episode head, which is the more defensible reading of the retrospective pronoun and the 10:15 parallel. The v25 relabeling removes the word-order error cleanly. No fresh defect surfaced in this row.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's two challenges both check out, one needing a small fix. 102-2 is a clean catch: the row calls v25's opening 'a fresh subject-led lifespan formula,' but וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ is apocopated wayyiqtol first, proper-noun subject after — verb-initial, not subject-led — and this same cluster uses identical wording for the genuinely subject-fronted v11 clause (וַאֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔ק), so two opposite word orders end up under one label. 102-1's substance is right too: sweeping the negated-listening clause across the book turns up 10:15, 25:20, and 35:22 as matching 3ms narratorial instances, and none of those three opens a unit; v20's causal clause (כִּ֣י דָֽרְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֱדֽוֹם) answers back to the prophet's charge at v15 (לָ֤מָּה דָרַ֨שְׁתָּ֙ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם) rather than launching anything new, and v21's re-nominated וַיַּ֨עַל יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ carries the genuine episode-opening syntax the row wants at v20. The correction: OL's sweep folds in 25:16's וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ as a fourth parallel, but that form is 2ms and sits inside the prophet's own direct speech, not the narrator's 3ms comment-clause class the other three instances share; dropping the mismatched instance from the set leaves the conclusion intact (the three genuine parallels still fail to open a unit) but the sweep as stated overclaims its count by one.

challenge_responses.response: Accepted with the peer's correction: the 3ms narratorial parallel set for the negated-listening clause is 10:15, 25:20, and 35:22 (three instances, not OL's four -- 25:16's form is 2ms direct speech and belongs to a different class). Rewrote the opening-edge argument to characterize v20 honestly as retrospective comment reaching back to v15's charge, grounded in the direct 10:15 parallel (which likewise closes a confrontation rather than opening the next section), rather than claiming v20 is a recognized book-wide opener-type. Conceded v21's re-nominated wayyiqtol as a genuine internal rival and rewrote strongest_rejected_alternative to meet it: v20 is kept because it supplies the divine rationale the following battle report depends on. Span 25:20-25:24 stays frozen; medium confidence is unchanged.

Accepted. v25 opens with “וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ”, apocopated wayyiqtol with the subject postposed, not a subject-led clause; the same correction applies at decision 103 for the identical verse. Fixed the label accordingly.

boss_ruling.reasoning: The negated-listening class is three narratorial instances, not four, and v20 reads retrospective rather than unit-opening; corrected and re-argued from v21's classic episode syntax.

post_resolution_check.notes: The parallel drawn to the Rehoboam verdict-hinge at 10:15 is apt and is checked against both Hebrew texts; the row's account of why the two hinges function oppositely (backward-closing at 10:15, forward-opening at 25:20) is coherent rather than asserted.

primary_reviews.rationale: Four strings verified; of the row's descriptive claims two stand and two fail. Standing: the conspiracy-notice label is accurate, since “וּמֵעֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁר” fronts a prepositional adjunct ahead of its verb, making v27 a genuinely marked temporal opening. Standing too, and understated by the row, is the opening form itself — “וַיְחִ֨י” is a hapax in this book, the single occurrence of the lifespan wayyiqtol anywhere in 2Chr, which is stronger evidence for the edge than the argument the row actually advances. Failing: the comparative claim about the source-citation formula is falsified by sweep, and the morphological label attached to 25:25 describes the opposite of what the form shows. Neither failure threatens the 25-28 span; both require the rationale to be rewritten, and the first correction in fact reinforces the span.

challenges.claim: The row calls the source-citation formula “unusually placed before, not after, the death narrative”. A book-wide sweep reverses that. “וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ” and its congeners occur ten times in 2Chr (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8), and in eight the formula stands before the death or burial notice — immediately at 13:22 to 13:23, 25:26 to 25:27-28, 26:22 to 26:23, 28:26 to 28:27 and 32:32 to 32:33, and with intervening material at 20:34 to 21:1, 27:7 to 27:9 and 33:18 to 33:20. Only 35:26 and 36:8 follow a death already narrated, both for local reasons. 25:26 is thus the book's regular sequence, not a deviation from it. The row also contradicts itself: its rejected alternative appeals to the formula's “usual role elsewhere in the book as a unit-closer paired with what follows it”, which is the correct account.
challenges.suggested_action: Strike the “unusually placed” characterisation, state the placement as the book's normal formula-then-death order, and mirror at least one comparandum (26:22-23 or 32:32-33) into boundary_evidence_refs as the strategy's refs rule requires.

challenges.claim: This row's opening edge rests on a word-order claim the form contradicts. It describes a subject-led lifespan notice opening the reign's close, yet “וַיְחִ֨י” is apocopated qal wayyiqtol standing first in its clause, with “אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ” following; the notice is verb-initial in the unmarked narrative order and nothing whatever is fronted. Because the stated warrant for the edge is that description, warrant and form diverge.
challenges.suggested_action: Rebuild the edge argument on grounds the Hebrew supplies — the verb is a book-hapax here, and the clause introduces a reckoning dated from another king's death that no preceding verse shares — and reserve subject-led terminology for clauses whose subject actually precedes the verb.

primary_reviews.rationale: The reign-summary grouping (age-retrospective, source citation, conspiracy, burial) is sound as a unit, and 26:1’s fresh accession formula is a clean seam-out, but the specific claim that the source-citation formula sits ‘unusually’ before rather than after the death account does not survive a check against the book's own pattern.

challenges.claim: The boundary_rationale's assertion that the source-citation formula is 'unusually placed before, not after, the death narrative' is contradicted by book-wide evidence: the identical citation-then-death order recurs at Solomon (1:29–31), Abijah (13:22–14:1), Jehoshaphat (20:34–21:1), Jotham (27:7–9), Manasseh (33:18–20), and Hezekiah (32:32–33) — six of the book's roughly thirteen source-citation instances — making this the dominant pattern rather than an exception. The rejected_alternative's supporting premise, that the formula's 'usual role elsewhere in the book' is as an absolute unit-closer with nothing narrated after it, is likewise not supported once these parallels are checked.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct or drop the 'unusually placed' framing (it describes the book's majority pattern), and re-examine on other grounds whether v27-28's substantive conspiracy-flight-killing narrative — which is more elaborate than the one-clause death formulas seen in the comparison set, and structurally closer to Joash's own assassination account at 24:25-26 — might warrant its own row rather than being folded under the v25-26 reign-summary complex.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the strongest repair in the cluster on its main axis: the false framing is replaced by the accurate one, and I could confirm each comparandum from the witness -- 9:29 citation, 9:30 reign total, 9:31 death; 13:22 citation with the death notice at MT 13:23 = WEB 14:1, correctly dual-cited both in prose and in refs. The overcorrection is the problem. In closing the door on "unusual", the row swung to a fresh exclusivity, and a book-wide sweep of the source-citation formula shows the exclusivity is false at 24:25-27, where Joash is killed and buried (וַיַּֽהַרְגֻ֥הוּ עַל מִטָּת֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר) before the citation formula arrives (הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים). That verse is not in the row's refs. The contradiction is also visible inside this cluster: M8-2Chr-109 lists 24:25-27 among the closes that invert, so two rows a few decisions apart now say incompatible things about the same passage. book_strategy_draft.md section 7 asks for exclusivity claims to be grepped book-wide at writing time, which is what would have caught this.

challenges.claim: The repair replaced a false "unusual" with a false "only". The row now states that of the citation-formula closes, "only Josiah's close (35:26) reverses it, following a death already narrated". Joash's close does the same and does it more sharply: oshb:2Chr.24.25 narrates the killing and burial -- וַיַּֽהַרְגֻ֥הוּ עַל מִטָּת֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר -- oshb:2Chr.24.26 names the conspirators, and only then does oshb:2Chr.24.27 give the citation, הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים, with the succession in the same verse. The formula at 36:8 is a further non-conforming case, carrying citation and succession together with no death notice for Jehoiakim anywhere in the book. Neither 24:27 nor 36:8 appears in this row's boundary_evidence_refs, so the sweep behind the word "only" is not visible.
challenges.suggested_action: Say "35:26 and 24:27" instead of "only Josiah's close", or drop the count entirely and keep the accurate positive statement that citation-before-death is the book's dominant order; mirror oshb:2Chr.24.25 and oshb:2Chr.24.27 into refs if the counter-instances are named. Reconciling with M8-2Chr-109, which already lists 24:25-27 as an inversion, would remove the cross-row conflict.

primary_reviews.rationale: The three original defects are genuinely cured, but the repair introduces a new inaccuracy in the same sentence that replaced them: the row now claims “only Josiah's close (35:26) reverses it, following a death already narrated,” which omits 2Chr.24.25-27, where Joash's murder and burial (v25) are likewise narrated before the citation-and-succession formula (v27). This is a fresh, repair-introduced overclaim, and it puts this row at odds with its own cluster-mate: decision M8-2Chr-109's rejected_alternative in this same cluster correctly lists “24:25-27 even inverts the order” among its exceptions. Neither 24:25 nor 24:27 appears in this row's boundary_evidence_refs.

challenges.claim: The revised rationale states “only Josiah's close (35:26) reverses it, following a death already narrated,” but 2Chr.24.25-27 reverses the same order: Joash's murder and burial are narrated at v25, “וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וְלֹ֥א קְבָרֻ֖הוּ בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים” (“they buried him in David's city, but not in the tombs of the kings”), and only afterward, at v27, does the citation-plus-succession formula follow, “הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו” (“they are written in the commentary of the book of the kings; Amaziah his son reigned in his place”). This is confirmed directly against oshb 2Chr.24.25-27, and is independently documented inside this very cluster — decision M8-2Chr-109's own revised rejected_alternative lists “24:25-27 even inverts the order” as one of its exceptions to the two-part-close pattern. The two rows in rev_cluster_10 now assert incompatible claims about the same book-wide fact, and this row cites neither 24:25 nor 24:27 in boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.suggested_action: Either drop the “only Josiah's...reverses it” clause or amend it to name both exceptions (35:26 and 24:25-27), and mirror oshb/web 2Chr.24.25 and 2Chr.24.27 into boundary_evidence_refs so this row's comparandum set matches decision 109's.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both primaries independently disprove the same sentence, and my own sweep confirms the disproof holds even more broadly than either shows. The boundary_rationale calls the source-citation formula 'unusually placed before, not after, the death narrative'; running the book's full citation set — 13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8, plus 9:29, 12:15, 16:11, and 24:27, none of which either primary swept — turns up exactly one clean reversal, Josiah at 35:26 following his battle-death already narrated at 35:20-24, against everything else standing citation-then-death or citation-then-succession (24:27 and 36:8 fold the succession clause into the very verse that carries the citation). Amaziah's placement is the book's default, not an exception. This is one finding wearing two claim_ids (LF-M8-2Chr-103-1, OL-M8-2Chr-103-1), and I rule them as a single remedy: strike 'unusually placed' and state the placement as the book's regular formula-then-death order. OL's version is the more careful of the two and needs no further fix beyond mirroring a comparandum into boundary_evidence_refs, as OL's own suggested_action already specifies. LF's needs one correction: its comparandum 'Solomon (1:29–31)' does not exist as cited — 2Chr 1 stops at v18 in oshb, and book_strategy_draft.md §1's own device list expects Solomon's citation at 9:29, where I confirmed 9:29-31 carries the identical citation-then-death shape LF is arguing for. A secondary, lower-stakes note on the same claim: LF's 'Abijah (13:22 then 14:1)' uses WEB numbering for the offset-zone specimen that book_strategy_draft.md itself lists as '14:1/MT 13:23' (§1, §3) — accurate, but per the numbering-zone dual-cite rule it should read '14:1/MT 13:23,' not a bare WEB citation that could be misread as a different chapter's event. OL's separate word-order challenge (103-2) is unrelated to the citation question and independently correct: וַיְחִ֨י is verb-initial apocopated wayyiqtol, not the subject-led clause the row calls it — the identical fix needed at 102 for this same verse from the other side of the seam.

challenge_responses.response: Accepted with a correction to LF's own comparandum: 'Solomon (1:29-31)' does not exist -- 2Chr 1 ends at v18 in oshb. Solomon's citation-then-death sequence is at 9:29-31, which I substituted. Struck 'unusually placed' and restated the placement as the book's regular formula-then-death order, citing 9:29-31 and dual-citing Abijah's case as web 14:1/MT 13:23 per the offset-zone rule, with 35:26 noted as the one true reversal per the book's binding standard on this incipit family. Added the comparanda to refs.

Accepted; same remedy as LF-103-1 above (one finding, two claim_ids, per the peer's ruling). My own sweep of the ~14 source-citation instances confirms only 35:26 reverses citation-before-death; 25:26 is the book's default, not an exception. Mirrored 9:29-31 into boundary_evidence_refs.

Accepted; the same fix as decision 102 for this identical verse: v25 opens with “וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ”, verb-initial apocopated wayyiqtol with the subject following, not a subject-led clause. Reworded the opening-edge label accordingly.

boss_ruling.reasoning: Citation-before-death is the book's norm — eight of ten instances — so the anomaly claim inverted the evidence and the Solomon comparandum was misnumbered; both corrected, and the close stands as the normal pattern instance it is.

post_resolution_check.notes: The citation-then-death ordering comparison to Solomon's close at 9:29-31 collates accurately, and the counter-examples (35:26, 24:25-27, 36:8) are correctly characterized as reversing or fusing the usual sequence.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both citations are exact and the mark type is right (PE after 26:2). The substantive claims verify, one of them more strongly than the row itself argues. Two accession notices in immediate succession is precise: “בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה” at 26:1 and “בֶּן שֵׁ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ” at 26:3 are the only two places in 2Chr where that age phrase appears. The accession type at 26:1 is indeed distinct, and it has exactly one twin in the book: “וַיִּקְח֞וּ כָּל עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙” with “וַיַּמְלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֔וֹ תַּ֖חַת אָבִ֥יו” is matched only by “וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ” with “וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ תַֽחַת אָבִ֖יו”, and each stands after a burial verse that omits the usual succession clause. That answers the rival I tested — whether 26:1 completes 25:28 rather than opening a new unit — since a detached popular-accession notice heading the successor's section is the book's own pattern. The father-and-son comparison verifies as well (“בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ מָלַ֣ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ” at 25:1, “בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יוֹתָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ” at 27:1). A precision note not worth a challenge: 26:1 does carry the age datum, but inside a circumstantial clause, “וְה֕וּא בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה”, so the contrast drawn is formal rather than informational and the row's wording survives it. The referent call in v2 follows necessarily, since “ה֚וּא בָּנָ֣ה” makes Uzziah the builder, leaving “אַחֲרֵ֥י שְׁכַֽב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם אֲבֹתָֽיו” to denote Amaziah. The defect is confined to the evidence trail.

challenges.claim: The row argues comparanda it never cites. Its opening edge turns on 26:1 being a different accession type from the age-formula used for Uzziah's father and son — the father's is “בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ מָלַ֣ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ” at 25:1 and the son's is “בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יוֹתָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ” at 27:1 — yet boundary_evidence_refs lists only 26:1, 26:2 and 26:3. The strategy requires every argued comparandum to be mirrored into the refs array, and both are missing. I verified the claim itself holds; it is the evidence trail that does not carry it.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Chr.25.1 and oshb:2Chr.27.1 with their web counterparts to boundary_evidence_refs, and consider adding 2Chr.36.1, the one structural twin of this accession type, if the distinctness is to be argued rather than asserted.

primary_reviews.rationale: Isolating vv1-2 turns on a real textual doubling — Uzziah receives both a popular-accession notice here and a standard age-formula three verses later — and the row correctly reads v2's closing clause as looking backward to Amaziah's death rather than forward to Uzziah's, a distinction easy to miss on a fast read.

The evidence trail is repaired: what the row argues, it now quotes and lists. Both formulas collate byte-exact where the row places them, and 36:1's וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ is a real structural twin of 26:1's וַיִּקְח֞וּ כָּל עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙ -- a sweep of the book finds that verb at 8:18, 23:8, 26:1 and 36:1 alone, and in the first two nobody is being enthroned at all. The trouble is the sentence the repair wrapped around that true observation. Widened to "the people rather than a formula", the class is not a pair: the book installs kings by popular subject at 22:1 and again at 33:25, both with the same hiphil and the same succession tag. Since the whole point of the row's opening edge is that Uzziah's accession is of a different type from the formula, an inaccurate count of that type is load-bearing rather than decorative. The PE after v2 is confirmed in pmarks_2Chr.json and correctly flagged single-witness, and the v2 backward-looking death clause reads as the row says.

challenges.claim: The exclusivity added at repair time does not survive a sweep. The row calls 36:1 "the only other place in the book where 'the people' rather than a formula install a king". Sweeping hiphil MLK across 2Chr returns two more popular-subject installations that use no accession formula: oshb:2Chr.22.1, וַיַּמְלִיכוּ֩ יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶת אֲחַזְיָ֨הוּ בְנ֤וֹ הַקָּטֹן֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו, and oshb:2Chr.33.25, וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו -- the latter carrying the identical subject noun to 36:1 and the identical successor tag to 26:1. What actually is confined to 26:1 and 36:1 is the narrower pairing of the taking verb with the installing verb; the verb itself occurs at 8:18, 23:8, 26:1 and 36:1, and only the last two have a people-subject take a man and make him king.
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the claim to the take-and-install pairing, which is verifiably a pair, or keep the wider class and name 22:1 and 33:25 with oshb refs alongside 36:1. While the refs are being touched, add web:2Chr.25.1 and web:2Chr.27.1 so the two age-formula comparanda carry both witnesses as 36:1 already does.

primary_reviews.rationale: The citation gap is fixed, but a fresh adversarial check of the row's own uniqueness claim turns up a problem the challenge never tested: the rationale calls 2Chr.36.1 “the only other place in the book where the people rather than a formula install a king,” overlooking 2Chr.33.25, where “the people of the land” enthrone Josiah with the identical hiphil verb used at 36:1. In fact 33:25's phrasing is a closer verbal match to 36:1 than 26:1's own wording is. The boundary determination itself (the age-formula restart at v3) is unaffected, but the comparandum set behind the “genuine structural twin” claim is incomplete.

challenges.claim: The rationale asserts 2Chr.36.1 is “the only other place in the book where 'the people' rather than a formula install a king,” but 2Chr.33.25 also has “the people of the land” enthrone a king by the same hiphil verb: “וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו” (“the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place”). That phrase is in fact closer to 36:1's own “וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ אֶת יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז...וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ” wording — both use עַם הָאָרֶץ (“people of the land”) — than 26:1's own “כָּל עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙” (“all the people of Judah”) is. Neither 33:25 nor its verbal overlap with 36:1 is cited or acknowledged.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise “the only other place” to acknowledge 2Chr.33.25 as a third instance (and note it is the closer verbal parallel to 36:1), or narrow the claim to whatever specific feature is meant to distinguish 26:1 if a narrower distinction was intended; add oshb/web 2Chr.33.25 to boundary_evidence_refs.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's single challenge is a clean evidence-trail gap, not a substantive error, and the row's underlying claim survives it fully. The citation trail needs the two verses added, exactly as OL's suggested_action specifies; no span or confidence question follows.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quoted forms collate byte-exact and sit in the verses the row assigns them to: the accession formula is a contiguous substring of oshb:2Chr.26.3 and the evaluation clause of oshb:2Chr.26.4. The fixity the row appeals to is measurable rather than impressionistic — Amaziah's formula at oshb:2Chr.25.1 and Uzziah's at 26:3 share the byte-identical run שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ, 47 codepoints of identical consonants, pointing and accents running from the reign-length clause into the mother-name notice, which is the strongest single piece of support available for the phrase standard accession formula. Mark data also checks out: pmarks_2Chr.json gives SAMEKH after 26:5, the type the row names (single-witness, corroboration only). Worth noting for the mesh, the row passes over the PE recorded after 26:2 (single-witness), which falls exactly on its own opening edge and would have corroborated it. challenges.claim: The row describes v3 as restating age and reign-length already implied in v1, but oshb:2Chr.26.1 carries the age alone — וְה֕וּא בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה — and neither 26:1 nor 26:2 contains any reign-length datum; the fifty-two-year figure enters the text for the first time at 26:3. The repetition is consonantal, not byte-level: the longest run the two verses share exactly is שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ, 10 codepoints, because v1 and v3 accent each of the three age words differently. Tier 1 (the text's own regnal-formula signal) still supports the seam; only the doublet description overshoots.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the doublet as a repetition of the age datum alone, with the reign-length figure new at v3. Span 26:3-5 is unaffected.

challenges.claim: The seam-out claim that v6 opens with a new subject-verb pair misdescribes the Hebrew. oshb:2Chr.26.6 begins וַיֵּצֵא֙ וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם: two wayyiqtol verbs with no expressed subject at all. The nearest overt subject in the running text is הִצְלִיח֖וֹ הָאֱלֹהִֽים at the close of oshb:2Chr.26.5 — God, not Uzziah — so the referent of the verbs in v6 has to be retrieved across a subject switch rather than supplied by a new nominal subject. The junction is real, but it is carried by topic and participant focus.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword the seam-out to the bare wayyiqtol chain plus the campaign topic; the neighbouring row at 26:6-8 already describes this same junction accurately and can be matched.

primary_reviews.rationale: The v3 restart of the age-formula ("בֶּן שֵׁ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ...") genuinely duplicates information already implied in v1's narrative introduction, and that duplication is the row's real warrant: the accession-formula device is listed tier-1 in the strategy's device matrix (§1), so restarting it after a narrative preface is a legitimate opening signal even though the surrounding block (26:1-15) is treated coarsely in the strategy's own block map (§5). The evaluation clause and Zechariah piety notice extend that opening unit without any competing device intervening before v6.

Both repairs land, and they land on the text rather than on a paraphrase of it. oshb:2Chr.26.1 carries the age datum only; the reign length first appears in oshb:2Chr.26.3, so the corrected description of the doublet is exact. At the far edge, oshb:2Chr.26.6 opens with two wayyiqtol verbs and no nominal subject, and the last overt subject before them is the divine name at the end of v5, which is precisely the retrieval the revised wording now describes. pmarks_2Chr.json does record a SAMEKH following v5, and the row carries it with the required single-witness flag and no evidential weight past corroboration. Every Hebrew string collates byte-exact, and each of the two translations reproduces web:2Chr.26.3 and web:2Chr.26.5 without alteration. No new original-language defect surfaced; the medium_low confidence looks honest for a three-verse formula unit whose interior is thematic rather than syntactic.

Both fixes track their originating challenges precisely rather than superficially: the age-only doublet claim is now bounded correctly against v1's actual content, and the v6 opener is described by what the clause actually contains (no subject) instead of an invented new-subject claim. Nothing further is at issue in this pair.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's pair of corrections survives independent collation. A codepoint-level alignment of the v1 and v3 age clauses returns a longest exact run of only שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ (10 codepoints, verified by direct comparison) — the two verses share the consonantal age datum but diverge in cantillation on every word, and v1 (וְה֕וּא בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה) carries no reign-length figure at all; the fifty-two-year number is new at v3. The doublet the row describes is real for age alone, not for age-and-reign-length together. Separately, oshb:2Chr.26.6's opening wayyiqtol pair has zero expressed subject — the last overt noun-subject in the running text is the divine name closing v5, not Uzziah — so calling the seam-out a new subject-verb pair overclaims what a bare verb chain supplies; the junction is real but rides on topic continuity, not a fresh nominal subject. Neither correction touches the row's core seam: the tier-1 accession-formula restart at v3 (per book_strategy_draft.md §1) still opens this unit, and the v5 SAMEKH remains correctly flagged single-witness, non-driving. medium_low confidence is unaffected by either fix.

challenge_responses.response: Accepted. v1 carries the age datum alone (וְה֕וּא בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה); the fifty-two-year reign-length is new at v3, so the doublet holds for age only, not age-and-reign-length together. Reworded accordingly; the tier-1 accession-formula restart at v3 still opens the unit.

Accepted. v6's opening wayyiqtol pair (וַיֵּצֵא֙ וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם) has zero expressed subject -- the last overt noun-subject in the running text is the divine name closing v5, not Uzziah -- so 'new subject-verb pair' overclaimed what a bare verb chain supplies. Reworded to attribute the junction to topic/participant continuity rather than a fresh nominal subject. medium_low confidence is unaffected by either fix.

boss_ruling.reasoning: 26:1 gives age only (the reign-length is new at 26:3) and v6's verbs carry no overt subject; both misstatements cured without touching the edges.

post_resolution_check.notes: The age-datum doublet between v.1 and v.3 is real on inspection of both verses, and medium_low confidence is the right call for a seam whose main support is a restart of formulaic register rather than a scene-change device.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening quote וַיֵּצֵא֙ וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם is byte-exact at oshb:2Chr.26.6 and its syntactic description is right — a bare wayyiqtol pair with no nominal subject repeated from the piety notice. The fame clause quoted from v8 also collates exactly. A sweep of ch 26 supplies corroboration the row did not use: the form שְׁמוֹ֙ occurs at 26:8 and 26:15 with byte-identical accentuation and nowhere else in the chapter, so each of the two rise subsections the draft carves out terminates in a name-goes-out notice (וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שְׁמוֹ֙ עַד לְב֣וֹא מִצְרַ֔יִם at v8, וַיֵּצֵ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ at v15). I weighed the rival reading in which those twin notices frame 26:6-15 as one inclusio-bound rise unit and did not press it, since both notices behave as summary closers rather than as an opening-and-closing frame, and the muster register at v11 pulls the other way. The defect I do press is narrower: the clause the row calls the closing is not the closing.

challenges.claim: Closing on the fame notice is inaccurate at the byte level: oshb:2Chr.26.8 runs past that clause and terminates on כִּ֥י הֶחֱזִ֖יק עַד לְמָֽעְלָה, a hiphil of the ḥ-z-q root. The omission matters past tidiness, because the same root is what carries the pivot argument at the 15/16 seam elsewhere in this cluster; leaving the v8 occurrence unquoted makes the root look scarcer in the rise section than a sweep shows it to be (26:8, 26:9, 26:15, 26:16). Tier 1 evidence, quoted from the source line.
challenges.suggested_action: Quote the actual terminal clause of v8 beside the fame notice, or call the fame notice the penultimate clause rather than the close. The 8/9 boundary itself stands.

primary_reviews.rationale: V6's asyndetic new subject-verb pair after the piety notice, and v9's equally fresh building-topic opener, bracket a self-contained military-and-fame report; nothing in vv6-8 introduces a scene-change device that would argue for splitting the Philistine campaign from the Arabian-help and Ammonite-tribute notices, since all three ride the same narrative chain rather than restarting with a fresh independent clause.

The fix does more than patch the quotation. The row now ends its v8 citation where oshb:2Chr.26.8 actually ends, and turns the recovered clause into an argument, tracing the strength root forward. I swept chs 26-27 for that root with a pattern that catches the hiphil spelling as well as the plain one: hits fall at 26:8, 26:9, 26:15, 26:16, 27:5 and 27:6, so the four the row names are all genuine and the thread it draws to the pivot is real. The pair of translations tracks web:2Chr.26.6 and web:2Chr.26.8 word for word, and the opening description of a bare verb pair with no repeated subject is right for oshb:2Chr.26.6. One phrase is loose rather than wrong: v9 is called an opener "with its own subject-verb pair", and the clause is verb-initial with the royal name following, though the neighbouring row uses the same phrase to mean an overt nominal subject rather than a fronted one, and on that reading the statement holds. I am not filing it, but a reader outside the cluster could misread it.

The fix is a direct, verbatim correction of the earlier truncation: the row no longer implies the fame clause is the verse's end, and the hazaq root's fourth occurrence (v8) is now visible alongside the three the row already tracked. Nothing else in the row calls for challenge.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The 6-8 boundary and its opening quote check out, but the clause the row calls the close is not where v8 actually ends. oshb:2Chr.26.8 runs past the fame notice to a further hiphil clause built on the ḥ-z-q root, a form the row's quotation drops entirely — thinning out what is otherwise a four-fold occurrence of that root threading 26:8, 9, 15, and 16 into the hubris pivot two rows later. This is a citation-accuracy defect, not a boundary defect: the fresh building-topic opener at v9 against the fame-and-strength close of v8 holds regardless of which clause gets labeled terminal. challenge_responses.response: Accepted. oshb:2Chr.26.8 runs past the fame clause to a further hiphil ḥ-z-q clause the row dropped; quoted the full tail (“וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שְׁמוֹ֙ עַד לְב֣וֹא מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י הֶחֱזִ֖יק עַד לְמָֽעְלָה”) so the root's fourth occurrence in this rise section (26:8, 9, 15, 16) isn't thinned out. The 8/9 boundary itself is unaffected; added oshb:2Chr.26.15, oshb:2Chr.26.16 to refs since the root-count claim now references them.

boss_ruling.reasoning: The claimed terminal clause was not terminal — a hiphil of the pivot root follows; corrected, and the root now serves the 15/16 pivot argument.

post_resolution_check.notes: The hiphil-chazaq root linking the fame notice at v.8 to the hubris pivot two rows later is present in the oshb text as claimed, and the closing seam before v.9's unrelated building topic is clean.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation passes on both quotes — וַיִּ֨בֶן עֻזִּיָּ֤הוּ מִגְדָּלִים֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם opens oshb:2Chr.26.9 and the hook חָזָֽק is the final word of oshb:2Chr.26.15 — and treating vv9-15 as register-dominant material is defensible in itself. Two parts of the supporting argument fail against the source. The span is neither marker-free nor signal-free at v11, and the lexical description of the v15/v16 link overstates what the forms show: a regex sweep of chs 26-27 returns six occurrences of the ḥ-z-q root (הֶחֱזִ֖יק at 26:8, וַֽיְחַזְּקֵֽם at 26:9, חָזָֽק at 26:15, וּכְחֶזְקָת֗וֹ at 26:16, וַיֶּחֱזַ֣ק at 27:5, וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֖ק at 27:6), so the root threads the whole rise-and-fall arc instead of belonging to one seam. Confidence medium is about right for a row with an unargued internal seam.

challenges.claim: The assertion that no competing marker breaks the list is not supported by the data, and the seam it papers over is a tier-1 candidate the row never argues. pmarks_2Chr.json records a SAMEKH after 2Chr.26.10 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only and never a driver), lying inside the span at precisely the building/army seam the rejected alternative names. Independent of the mark, v11 opens וַיְהִ֣י לְעֻזִּיָּ֡הוּ חַיִל֩ עֹשֵׂ֨ה מִלְחָמָ֜ה — a possessive-existential register frame whose closest book-wide analogue is Asa's muster at web:2Chr.14.8 = oshb:2Chr.14.7 (MT), וַיְהִ֣י לְאָסָ֗א חַיִל֮ נֹשֵׂ֣א צִנָּ֣ה וָרֹמַח֒, the same wayehi + lamed + royal name + ḥayil + participle shape — and enumeration formulas follow at once, בְּמִסְפַּר֙ פְּקֻדָּתָ֔ם in v11 and כֹּ֠ל מִסְפַּ֞ר רָאשֵׁ֤י הָאָבוֹת֙ opening v12. The same opener family recurs at oshb:2Chr.9.25, oshb:2Chr.18.1 and oshb:2Chr.32.27, each time introducing a register rather than continuing one. A seven-verse merge across that opener is exactly the granularity call the contract asks to be tested.
challenges.suggested_action: Either split 26:9-10 from 26:11-15 on the v11 register-opener, or hold the merge and argue the opener down explicitly against the 14:7 (MT) analogue; either way disclose the 26:10 SAMEKH as single-witness rather than asserting an absence.

challenges.claim: A root picked up verbatim at the start of v16 is not verbatim. v15 ends in the qal form חָזָֽק and v16 opens with וּכְחֶזְקָת֗וֹ — conjunction plus preposition plus a ḥezqāh noun plus 3ms suffix. The two share a root, not a form; and with six occurrences of that root in chs 26-27, recurrence by itself does not single out this seam.
challenges.suggested_action: Downgrade verbatim to a root-level catchword and let the adjacency (last word of v15, first word of v16) carry the argument, which it can on its own.

primary_reviews.rationale: The catalog's own outer edges are sound - v9's fresh building notice and the חזק root-hook closing into v16 both collate against the Hebrew - but the claim that vv9-15 run 'without any competing scene-change marker breaking the list' overstates the evidentiary picture: pmarks_2Chr.json records a SAMEKH after 2Chr.26.10, sitting exactly at the building (9-10) / army (11-15) seam that the row's own rejected_alternative explicitly argues against splitting on. Unlike decision 105, which discloses its SAMEKH correctly, this row's rationale is silent about a mark that sits right at the contested internal seam.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale asserts the vv9-15 catalog runs 'without any competing scene-change marker breaking the list,' but pmarks_2Chr.json lists a SAMEKH after 2Chr.26.10 (single-witness, tier-3), positioned exactly at the building/army seam (vv9-10 vs vv11-15) that the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative argues against splitting on. The mark cannot drive a split under the m8-mesh-r2 contract, but the blanket claim of an unmarked span is not accurate.
challenges.suggested_action: Amend the boundary_rationale (and boundary_evidence_refs) to disclose the SAMEKH after v10 explicitly as single-witness, non-driving corroboration, rather than asserting the span is unmarked; the 9-15 coarse grouping itself need not change, only the evidentiary claim requires precision.

primary_reviews.rationale: The disclosure repairs are clean and the row deserves credit for holding the merge openly instead of quietly. My sweep for the opener family returns exactly the inventory the row gives -- 9:25, MT 14:7, 18:1, 26:11, 32:27 -- with nothing missed, and the dual-cite in the ch.14 offset zone is correct in both directions. What will not carry weight is the reason the row gives for treating 26:11 as unlike the other four. It says the other four each head a reign-section and start a register there, whereas v11 only carries on the resource buildup of vv9-10; but the closest analogue does the same thing v11 does. MT 14:5 = WEB 14:6 has Asa building fortified cities, MT 14:6 = WEB 14:7 has him walling them with towers, gates and bars, and MT 14:7 = WEB 14:8 then musters the army -- fortification first, force second, exactly the progression from 26:9-10 into 26:11. Nor is 9:25 at the head of anything: it follows the tribute register of 9:23-24. The same holds for 32:27, which follows the illness and humbling of 32:24-26. Reign-sections in this book open with accession formulas, and none of these four does. The merge may still be right on the coarse-catalog policy; the discriminator offered for it is not.

challenges.claim: The discriminator the repair supplies is refuted by the row's own nearest comparandum. primary_reviews.rationale: Three quotes, all byte-exact and correctly attributed — citation formula at oshb:2Chr.27.7, restated statistic at oshb:2Chr.27.8, death-and-succession notice at oshb:2Chr.27.9 — and the PE after v9 matches pmarks_2Chr.json (single-witness). That framing is what I contest.

challenges.claim: The row calls the arrangement an unusual doubling and says the text offers no explanation for the citation formula standing ahead of a regnal statistic rather than after it as for Uzziah. The sequence is not unusual in this book: Solomon's close runs citation at oshb:2Chr.9.29, then וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֧ה בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה at oshb:2Chr.9.30, then the death-and-succession notice at oshb:2Chr.9.31 — the same three-part order, citation before regnal statistic before death. That is an in-book parallel, which the strategy admits as arguable literary evidence rather than cross-book metadata, and the row neither cites nor mirrors it. What is genuinely distinctive at 27:8 is not the placement but the repetition: 9:30 supplies Solomon's reign-length for the first time, whereas 27:8 restates figures already given at 27:1.
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the claim to the repetition, cite 9:29-31 as the in-book precedent for the three-part order, and mirror it into boundary_evidence_refs. Span 27:7-9 is unaffected.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row is unusually candid about a genuine crux - the source-citation formula (v7) sits ahead of a restated age/reign statistic (v8) rather than after the closing pair, unlike the clean citation-then-death sequence at 26:22-23 - and rather than inventing an explanation for the ordering, the rationale reports the anomaly and stops, which is the correct discipline under the no-fabricated-scholarship rule. That same unresolved oddity is a legitimate reason to hold confidence at medium_low rather than pushing it toward the high rating given the analogous 109 pairing, since real uncertainty remains about whether v8 truly belongs with this closing complex.

Every load-bearing assertion in the repaired row survives independent checking. The Solomonic sequence runs as described, source citation at 9:29, reign length at 9:30, death and succession at 9:31. A consonantal sweep of all 822 verses for the forty-years phrase returns 9:30 and 24:1 only, so that figure really is first supplied where the row says it is, and the contrast with 27:8 stands. Jotham's two statistics agree exactly across 27:1 and 27:8 (twenty-five at accession, sixteen years reigning), the two verses differing in a single word, so almost verbatim is fair. Uzziah's close carries no regnal figure beside its citation, as claimed. The 27:9 PE is correctly flagged single-witness, and nothing in this row touches an offset zone, so no dual-cite is owed. One bookkeeping observation too slight to file: web:2Chr.9.30 is missing from the refs though the row argues that verse's content, while its oshb counterpart is present.

The repair narrows an overclaim into a defensible, narrower one and backs it with a genuine in-book parallel instead of an assumed uniqueness. The reasoning that Jotham's v8 restates figures already on the record while Solomon's 9:30 supplies a first-time statistic is a real, checkable asymmetry rather than a rhetorical flourish, and the row is careful to use 9:29-31 only for the three-part sequencing, not for the content of the citation itself.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The row's framing of the citation-before-statistic order as unusual does not survive a look at 2Chr.9.29-31: Solomon's close runs the identical three-part sequence — citation, then a reign-length figure new to the text, then death-and-succession — an in-book parallel that book_strategy_draft.md §4 explicitly allows as arguable literary evidence, and one the row neither cites nor rules out. primary_reviews.rationale: Both Hebrew strings in this row reproduce oshb bytes without deviation (28:1 whole-verse-through-אָבִֽיו; 28:4 whole verse), and the comparative claim they carry survives a book-wide sweep rather than merely sounding plausible: the negated form וְלֹא עָשָׂ֧ה occurs once in all of 2Chr, at 28:1, so Ahaz's evaluation is not just the harshest of the four reigns in this stretch but the only negation of the הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה clause anywhere in the book (that clause otherwise stands at 14:1, 20:32, 24:2, 25:2, 26:4, 27:2, 29:2, 34:2). The agency argument for the close is true to the syntax as well: vv2-4 keep Ahaz as subject (וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ ... וְה֥וּא הִקְטִ֖יר ... וַיְזַבֵּ֧חַ), while 28:5 installs a new one, וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֜הוּ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָיו֮, with the 3ms suffix on the verb demoting Ahaz to object. The rejected alternative's grammatical point also holds — v1's evaluation clause is continued by v2's wayyiqtol וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ, so the accession pair cannot be lifted out without severing a clause chain. Numbering: ch 28 lies outside both dual-cite zones, and WEB/MT agree verse for verse across chs 28-29 (27 and 36 verses each, content anchors aligned), so the row's single-number refs need no dual cite. Checked and found non-probative: SAMEKH follows 28:5 (WLC single-witness), which would corroborate a rival close one verse later, but tier-3 spacing cannot drive a boundary and a marker-only objection is insufficient evidence.

The open and close both hold up: v1's evaluation clause and v4's high-places/green-tree line are byte-exact against 2Chr_oshb.txt, and v5's pivot to Yahweh as grammatical subject is a real tier-1 hinge, not an artifact of the row's framing. A book-wide check of the 'walked in the ways of the kings of Israel' collocation (also at 21:6 for Jehoram, fused with the evaluation clause in that verse the same way it runs on from v1 into v2 here) supports treating the evaluation and its explanatory apostasy material as one continuous unit rather than two. Two problems remain in how the row argues its edges, detailed below.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative is internally incoherent: it proposes 'reading vv1-4 as merely the fixed accession pair (as in 25:1-2 and 27:1-2) and pushing the apostasy catalog into the next row,' but vv1-4 as defined by this very row already includes the apostasy catalog (vv3-4), so nothing is left in 'vv1-4' to push anywhere. Since 25:1-2 and 27:1-2 are both two-verse comparanda, the alternative the row means to reject is presumably a vv1-2/vv3-4 split, not vv1-4 wholesale.
challenges.suggested_action: Rewrite the rejected_alternative to name the actual rival split (vv1-2 accession pair vs vv3-4 apostasy catalog) so the comparison to 25:1-2/27:1-2 makes sense.

challenges.claim: v3 opens with וְה֥וּא הִקְטִ֖יר -- waw plus independent pronoun plus QATAL (הִקְטִיר, perfect), which breaks the wayyiqtol chain running וַיֵּלֶךְ...עָשָׂה through v2. This is a recognized Hebrew disjunctive-clause shape that can flag a fresh beat, and it sits closer to a genuine internal seam candidate than anything the row's rejected_alternative actually discusses.
challenges.suggested_action: Address the וְהוּא הִקְטִיר shift directly -- either explain why it stays subordinate to the wayyiqtol-chain unit rather than opening a new one, or concede it as the strongest internal rival to the current 1-4 grouping.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both cures are present and the span itself looks sound: Ahaz stays the actor across vv1-4, and agency does pass to Yahweh at v5. The trouble lies in the two new supports the rewrite leaned on. One misreports the clause chain, since v2 does not run wayyiqtol to its end - its second half is a fronted-object qatal clause - so v3's disjunctive is the second interruption in this stretch and not the only one. The other elevates subject-change into a criterion said to be shared with neighbouring rows, and two rows in this very cluster set seams where no subject changes at all.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative describes “the wayyiqtol chain running through v2-4 (broken only by v3's non-subject-changing disjunctive)”, and the rationale has v3's pronoun-plus-qatal breaking the chain that v2's “וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ” sustains. v2 does not sustain it to its end: its second clause is “וְגַ֧ם מַסֵּכ֛וֹת עָשָׂ֖ה לַבְּעָלִֽים” - waw, gam, fronted object, qatal - already off the wayyiqtol backbone. The exclusivity in 'broken only by' is therefore false, and the row's own point, that a disjunctive inside this catalog does not open a unit, would be better served by admitting two of them rather than one.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the description so that v2 itself is shown closing with a fronted-object qatal clause and “וְה֥וּא הִקְטִ֖יר” is the second such break, then argue, as the row already does, that neither reopens the unit.

challenges.claim: The rationale asserts that “the criterion this row and its neighbors use for a hard seam is a change of grammatical subject”. Two rows in this same cluster contradict it. M8-2Chr-116 closes at the 21/22 seam where Ahaz is subject on both sides (“כִּֽי חָלַ֤ק אָחָז֙” in v21; v22's wayyosef limol, with hu hammelekh Achaz naming that same subject); M8-2Chr-120 opens at the 2/3 seam where Hezekiah is subject on both sides (29:2 wayya-as ha-yashar, 29:3 hu ... patach). Whatever criterion the part is really using, it is not subject-change, and putting it forward as the shared rule leaves this row's decisive argument resting on a generalization the cluster falsifies.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the appeal to a shared criterion and argue v3 locally - one actor, one evaluative heading, no new addressee or scene - or restate the criterion in a form that the 28:21/22 and 29:2/3 seams also satisfy.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the cleanest repair in the cluster: the rejected alternative is now internally coherent, and the grammatical-subject criterion it proposes (Ahaz as actor through v1-4, Yahweh taking over at v5) is independently confirmed by the Hebrew and dovetails with how the next decision's row opens, giving the pair real argumentative continuity instead of two isolated calls.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both LF challenges target the row's argumentative apparatus rather than its Hebrew, and both hold up. primary_reviews.rationale: Quote fidelity and mark data are clean here. The opening clause of 28:5, the closing clause of 28:8 and the v9 fragment cited in the rejected alternative all match oshb byte for byte, the WEB glosses reproduce WEB wording exactly, and pmarks keys a SAMEKH to 2Chr.28.8 — right type, right verse — which the row correctly labels single-witness and treats as corroboration only. What fails is the usage claim the rejected alternative leans on: it asserts a recurring book-level construction, and 2Chr does not have one. That is a rationale defect, not a reason to move the 8/9 edge, which the verse itself secures by introducing an unnamed-until-now participant with a name-giving clause and a verb of motion.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative rests on a book-usage claim the Hebrew does not support. A consonantal sweep of all 822 verses returns וְ֠שָׁם הָיָ֨ה exactly once — at 28:9 itself. The only other שָׁ֣ם הָיָ֗ה sequence in 2Chr is 1:3, כִּי שָׁ֣ם הָיָ֗ה אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים, a subordinate clause headed by the causal particle that supplies an object (the tent of meeting) as background at Gibeon, not a scene-opening participant introduction; the reverse order never occurs. So 'the clause the book uses elsewhere to bring on a new character at a location already named' has no second witness, and the tier-1 warrant offered for refusing the 5-15 merge is doing no work.

primary_reviews.rationale: The three quoted runs (28:9 opening, 28:13 close of the leaders' speech, 28:15 return notice) collate exactly, and pmarks does key a PE to 2Chr.28.15, so the mark cite is accurate in type, position and single-witness labelling. The row's admission that the edges are debatable is warranted: שֹׁמְרֽוֹן is the identical consonantal form at v8 and v15, so the place-name bracket the row notices is real. My objection is narrower and lies in the stated ground for rejecting the rival, which the Hebrew of v12 contradicts.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative claims that isolating 9-11 would cut 'at a point with no frame reopening the narrative in between'. 28:12 is such a frame: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרָאשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי אֶפְרַ֗יִם, followed by four men newly named (עֲזַרְיָ֤הוּ בֶן יְהֽוֹחָנָן֙ and three more). Wayyiqtol plus a newly introduced named group is the participant-change device the strategy classes tier-1, and v15 closes that same group anaphorically with the identical verb, וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֩ אֲשֶׁר נִקְּב֨וּ בְשֵׁמ֜וֹת, so 12-15 carries its own envelope. The construction is segmentation-bearing across the book (וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ stands 6x in 2Chr: 20:19, 28:12, 28:15, 29:12, 30:14, 30:27), and this cluster's own row M8-2Chr-120 treats the same construction at 29:12, וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ הַ֠לְוִיִּם plus a name list, as the subject change that closes a unit. Tier-3 SAMEKH after 28:11 (WLC single-witness) is consistent with the rival but drives nothing and is not offered as a driver.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-argue the rival on a ground the Hebrew supports — the captives chain that runs unbroken from Oded's imperative in v11 into vv13-15 is available — or, if the 'no frame' wording is retained, reconcile it explicitly with the boundary weight this same cluster gives the identical construction at 29:12. primary_reviews.rationale: Oded's introduction and the Ephraimite leaders' guilt-admission both quote byte-accurately, as does the 'returned to Samaria' close. The medium confidence is well-earned and honestly self-aware -- this is exactly the region the book strategy's own low-confidence list (28:9-15) flags, and the row's candid admission that 'Samaria' brackets both v8's arrival and v15's return matches that expectation rather than papering over it.
