boss_ruling.reasoning: The mofet anaphora binds v31 back to v24 inside the row's own span, refuting the no-continuity dismissal; the amendment concedes the tie and defends the catalog boundary on the subject-role reversal.

post_resolution_check.notes: The בימי+name construction and the מופת anaphora back to v24 both checked directly; applies row 140's own clause-final-adjunct test to itself for consistency, and the cross-reference holds up on inspection.

primary_reviews.rationale: Four runs here, each reproducing its line without deviation and each landing where the row places it. The “resumptive tag” label on וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ survives inspection and is in fact better grounded than the row argues: v29 hands the subject slot to God (כִּ֤י נָֽתַן לוֹ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים רְכ֖וּשׁ רַ֥ב מְאֹֽד), so the fronted pronoun-plus-name at v30 genuinely restores Hezekiah to it, and that same conjunction-plus-pronoun shape recurs across the book (ten consonantal hits, including 32:9 and 33:6 in this cluster's own range). The water-works link reinforces it — v30's סָתַם֙ אֶת מוֹצָ֞א מֵימֵ֤י גִיחוֹן֙ picks up the stopping verb of לִסְתּוֹם֙ at 32:3 and וַֽיִּסְתְּמוּ֙ at 32:4. The seam at v32 is a verified device and not an unchecked universal: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י returns ten hits across 2Chr, at 13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26 and 36:8. The weak point is the handling of v31.

challenges.claim: v31 is characterized as “one more catalog item”, but its syntax does not behave like the catalog. vv27-29 predicate acquisitions of the king (וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ at v27, עָֽשָׂה ל֠וֹ at v27 and again at v29) and v30 predicates a work of his; v31's main clause is עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ — a qatal whose subject is God and whose object is Hezekiah, following a fronted prepositional phrase. The row's only counterweight to isolating the verse is the connective וְכֵ֞ן, and it weighs neither that reversal of subject and object nor the anaphoric הַמּוֹפֵת֙ in the same verse, which points back to 32:24 rather than to anything in the wealth catalog — that portent noun stands at only those two places in 2Chr.
challenges.suggested_action: Let the mesh choose among detaching v31 as its own testing-notice row, attaching it to the illness-and-sign material, or keeping it here behind a rejected alternative that actually answers the God-as-subject shift and the backward reference of הַמּוֹפֵת֙ to v24. Whichever way it falls, oshb:2Chr.32.24 has to be mirrored into boundary_evidence_refs, because v31 cannot be argued without it.

primary_reviews.rationale: The catalog frame is sound: וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד opens it, וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ correctly marks the Gihon item as a resumptive addition to the same list, and the pivot to the source-citation formula at v32 is textbook. But treating v31 as merely one more catalog item via the connective וְכֵ֞ן misses a real lexical thread: v25's כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ (his heart was lifted up), v26's בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ (the pride of his heart), and v31's own closing לָדַ֖עַת כָּל בִּלְבָבֽוֹ (to know all that was in his heart) all use לב, and the sequence pride, humbling, testing reads as one thematic arc completing the illness episode rather than a fourth possession after treasuries, storehouses, and herds. The row's rejected_alternative acknowledges v31 is 'a test of character rather than an inventory item' but never engages this echo or the alternative of attaching v31 to 32:24-26 instead.

challenges.claim: The rationale doesn't address a real Hebrew lexical echo: לב (heart) recurs at 32:25 (כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ), 32:26 (בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ) and 32:31's own close (לָדַ֖עַת כָּל בִּלְבָבֽוֹ), which argues the envoys' heart-test forms one thematic arc with the illness-and-humbling unit (32:24-26) rather than simply extending the wealth catalog as one more possession.
challenges.suggested_action: Have the row, or the mesh, weigh whether 32:31 attaches to 32:24-26 as the completion of the pride/humbling/testing arc, or at minimum address the לב echo explicitly before treating v31 as a catalog item under the וְכֵ֞ן connective alone.

primary_reviews.rationale: The substantive repairs check out. מופת really does stand at exactly two places in 2Chr, so the anaphora argument is exclusive as stated; וְכֵן opens 32:31 as the row says; עֲזָבוֹ is a qatal with הָאֱלֹהִים as subject and the king as object; and 32:32 is on the book strategy's own list of expected source-citation verses (§1), which is what the row uses to close the span. One nuance the row is entitled to but should notice: v29 already contains כִּי נָתַן לוֹ אֱלֹהִים with God as subject, so God-as-agent is not itself new at v31; the row's claim survives only because it is scoped to main clauses, v29's being subordinate. Keeping v31 while conceding its content belongs elsewhere, at medium_low, is an honest reading of a span §6 of the strategy flags in advance. The defect I file is confined to citation hygiene.

challenges.claim: The v29 gloss appears in quotation marks as “for God had given him… substance,” against a row that cites web:2Chr.32.29, but the witness reads “for God had given him abundant possessions” and the word “substance” occurs nowhere in WEB 2Chr 32. The neighbouring strings for vv30-31 (“and this same Hezekiah…”, “and so… with the envoys of… Babylon,”) are likewise free renderings of the Hebrew set in the same quotation marks, so nothing in the row distinguishes witness text from the author's own translation.
challenges.suggested_action: Where quotation marks are used against a web: ref, reproduce WEB verbatim — at minimum replace “… substance” with “abundant possessions” — and present renderings of the Hebrew as glosses rather than quotations.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the most self-aware row in the cluster: it keeps its boundary but openly states that the losing alternative is textually stronger, then explains the narrow procedural reason (the ve-khen connective, v32's citation formula) for keeping v31 here anyway. That is a legitimate way to resolve a genuinely close call, not an evasion.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF and OL both challenge this row's treatment of v31, from two different lexical angles that turn out to reinforce rather than duplicate each other, and I verified both independently. LF traces לב (heart): כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ (v25), בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ (v26), and לָדַ֖עַת כָּל בִּלְבָבֽוֹ closing v31 itself — the same root marking pride, humbling, and testing across all three verses, which reads as one moral arc rather than a fourth catalog possession after treasuries, storehouses, and herds. OL traces the syntax and a second lexeme: vv27-30 predicate acquisitions or works belonging *to* Hezekiah (וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ, עָֽשָׂה ל֠וֹ, וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ סָתַם֙), while v31's main clause inverts that pattern entirely — עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ makes God the subject and Hezekiah the direct-object patient, not the catalog's beneficiary — and the same הַמּוֹפֵת֙ anaphora argued against 141 shows v31 pointing back to v24, not sideways to the treasuries. The row's only counterweight, the connective וְכֵ֞ן, is real but thin against three converging signals (a shared root, a subject/object reversal, and a definite-noun back-reference) that the boundary_rationale never engages. Both challenges are supported and are best read as one reconciled finding: v31 does not behave like 'one more catalog item,' and its correct home, folded into 141's illness-and-humbling unit, kept here behind a rewritten rejected_alternative that actually answers these three points, or split out as its own testing-notice row, is a live boundary question for the author/boss round, not something I can resolve by re-drawing the span myself.

challenge_responses.response: Confirmed: כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ (v25) and בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ (v26) mark pride and humbling, and v31 closes on לָדַ֖עַת כָּל בִּלְבָבֽוֹ, the same לב root a third time -- a moral arc rather than a fourth catalog possession. boundary_rationale now traces this echo explicitly and treats v31 as reaching back into the pride/humbling arc rather than simply extending the wealth catalog.

Confirmed: vv27-30 predicate acquisitions and works to Hezekiah (וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ, עָֽשָׂה ל֠וֹ, עָ֣שָׂה ל֔וֹ), while v31's main clause, עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ, makes God the subject and Hezekiah the object -- a reversal the row's only counterweight, וְכֵ֞ן, does not address. The definite הַמּוֹפֵת֙ anaphora to v24 is also now stated. The row keeps v31 on its own connective and on 32:32's fresh source-citation formula, while conceding its content belongs to the pride/humbling/testing arc, and oshb:2Chr.32.24 is mirrored into the refs.
Rev round: peer ruling supported; remedy applied in micro round r2 (see rev_peer.json and final_rows_edits.json entry for M8-2Chr-142).

boss_ruling.reasoning: v31 has God as subject and Hezekiah as object — not one more catalog item; the attachment question is argued openly now and the span kept with the rival recorded.

post_resolution_check.notes: Openly concedes v31 reads more naturally with the preceding illness unit and keeps it here only on the וכן connective and 32:32's source-formula -- an honest, non-strawman rejected alternative; the לב-root and מופת-anaphora claims both check out against the cited verses.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three runs, verified letter for letter against 32:32 and 32:33. Both devices the row leans on are confirmed recurrent rather than asserted: the source-citation opener returns ten hits across the book and the sleeping-with-the-fathers formula another ten, 32:33 among them, so “recognized, distinct unit-closing device” is a checked claim. The row's English for the archive name is also right where carelessness would have cost it: 32:32 reads מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל, Judah first, an order 2Chr uses at 25:26, 28:26 and 32:32 against the reverse at 27:7, 35:27 and 36:8. PE after 32:33 types correctly against pmarks (single-witness). One statement about the following seam does not hold.

challenges.claim: “The same accession hand-off formula that opens the next reign” does not describe this seam. 2Chr 33:1 opens with the age formula בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ, not with the succession formula. That succession formula occurs twelve times in 2Chr (9:31, 12:16, 13:23, 17:1, 21:1, 24:27, 26:23, 27:9, 28:27, 32:33, 33:20, 36:8) and stands verse-initial, actually opening a reign report, at 17:1 alone (וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו); everywhere else, 32:33 included, it is clause-final and closes the predecessor. If the sentence means only that the hand-off points ahead to a reign narrated beyond the part, it is ambiguously put; read as written it misdescribes 33:1.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword so the formula is said to close Hezekiah's report and pass the throne to Manasseh, whose reign opens on a different (age-formula) type; and mirror the comparandum into boundary_evidence_refs with web:2Chr.33.1 and oshb:2Chr.33.1, which the row argues from but does not cite.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both formulas are textbook and independently verified as named strategy specimens: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו opens the source-citation, and וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו through וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו completes the standard death-succession sequence exactly as the book strategy's device matrix predicts at this verse. No serious rival groups these two verses with the wealth catalog, since source-citation and death-succession are recognized, distinct unit-closing devices throughout Chronicles, not narrative continuations.

Every checkable claim in this row came back clean. A consonantal sweep for וימלך X (בנו) תחתיו returns exactly twelve hits (9:31, 12:16, 13:23, 17:1, 21:1, 24:27, 26:23, 27:9, 28:27, 32:33, 33:20, 36:8), matching the stated count, and only the 17:1 hit begins at character offset 0 of its verse, so “verse-initial and reign-opening only once” is exact. The remaining eleven, 32:33 among them, end a clause before something else begins — MT 13:23 (= WEB 14:1) continues בימיו שקטה הארץ after the construction, which is why the row's wording is clause-final rather than verse-final and is right to be. The count deliberately excludes 22:1's וַיַּמְלִיכוּ, correctly, since that is a different stem. 32:32 is on the strategy's expected source-citation list; the full v32 quotation, the v33 strings and all four English quotations collate exactly; the PE after 32:33 matches pmarks and is disclosed single-witness. The parenthetical “beyond this part's range” is accurate: the strategy's part map ends p12 at 32:33 with seam-out 33:1. One member of the twelve (MT 13:23) falls in offset zone B, but the row cites no member individually, so no dual-cite duty is triggered. Confidence high is earned by a source-citation formula, a death-and-succession sequence and a corroborating mark all landing on the same seam.

A clean, precisely-worded fix. The twelve-occurrence count and the singling out of 17:1 as the one verse-initial, reign-opening instance both check out against the text, and book_strategy_draft.md independently lists 17:1 as its succession-type specimen and 33:1 as an age-formula specimen, which is exactly the contrast the row now draws.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF supported this row without reservation; OL's challenge catches a wording slip LF's read-through did not. The row calls v33's closing וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו 'the same accession hand-off formula that opens the next reign just beyond this part's range,' but 33:1 opens with the age formula, בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ, a different device entirely. A sweep for the תחתיו succession construction returns twelve hits in 2Chr (9:31, 12:16, 13:23, 17:1, 21:1, 24:27, 26:23, 27:9, 28:27, 32:33, 33:20, 36:8), and checking each shows it stands verse-initial and actually launches a reign report at only one of them, 17:1 (וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו); at every other occurrence, 32:33 included, it is clause-final, closing the predecessor's report rather than opening the successor's. So the sentence, read as written, misdescribes what happens at 33:1: nothing there 'opens on' this formula. The challenge is supported; it targets phrasing, not the boundary itself, since no rival groups 32:32-33 with anything else and the row's underlying source-citation-plus-succession pairing is correct as a unit-closing device. The fix is textual: say the formula closes Hezekiah's report and hands the throne to Manasseh, whose own reign narrative opens on the differently-shaped age formula, and mirror web/oshb 2Chr.33.1 into boundary_evidence_refs since the row argues from that comparandum without citing it.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation is clean on all three quotes: v10, v12a and v13b are byte-identical to the OSHB lines they are attributed to, so my objection is not to the Hebrew but to how the row weighs it. Verse 12 begins with a verse-initial temporal protasis, וּכְהָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ, governing as its apodosis the very clause the row quotes, חִלָּ֕ה אֶת פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו; protasis-apodosis and time-frame transitions are tier-1 devices, so the rival split at v12 is not the paragraph-only alternative the row describes. Two further Hebrew facts pull the same way. The clause the row's English gloss carries but its Hebrew quote stops short of, וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו, together with וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֗יו and וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע תְּחִנָּת֔וֹ, reproduces the Chronicler's own programmatic sequence at 7:14 (וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י ... וְיִֽתְפַּֽלְלוּ֙ וִֽיבַקְשׁ֣וּ פָנַ֔י) — an in-book parallel and therefore arguable evidence — and it binds vv12-13 into a shaped pair; the same כנע thread then runs on to לִפְנֵ֖י הִכָּנְע֑וֹ and כְּהִכָּנַ֖ע מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו. Against my own pressure I record the counterweight honestly: the book's other distress-protases, וּבְעֵת֙ הָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ and בַּצַּר ל֔וֹ, are mid-account pivots that close nothing off, so the merge may well survive adjudication — but it has to be argued against a tier-1 rival rather than against a ¶. One further observation, offered as fact and not as a challenge: the opening edge the row does defend carries uncited tier-3 corroboration, the PE keyed to 2Chr.33.9 (single-witness), while sibling rows 147, 148, 150 and 151 all cite comparable marks.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative states that the split before v12 'has ¶ support alone'. That misstates the rival's evidence on the row's own Hebrew: v12 opens verse-initially with וּכְהָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ, a kaph-prefixed infinitive-construct temporal protasis whose apodosis is חִלָּ֕ה אֶת פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו — tier-1 (time-frame transition / protasis-apodosis), not tier-4. The same construction class is what row M8-2Chr-152 relies on for its own opening edge at וּבְהוֹצִיאָ֣ם אֶת הַכֶּ֔סֶף, so the cluster currently weighs one device class two ways. The rival is further supported in-book: vv12-13 realise the 7:14 programme lexeme by lexeme (וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י ... וְיִֽתְפַּֽלְלוּ֙ וִֽיבַקְשׁ֣וּ פָנַ֔י against וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו and וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֗יו).
challenges.suggested_action: Either restate the rejected alternative at its true tier — conceding the v12 protasis and rebutting it from the כנע/תפלל chain and the judgment-reversal arc — or split the row 33:10-11 / 33:12-13. Whichever the mesh adopts, the treatment of verse-initial infinitive-construct protases should be made uniform with row M8-2Chr-152.

challenges.claim: Two citation-accuracy defects. (a) The row says 'Two WEB paragraphs sit inside this row (before v10 and before v12)'; the ¶ before v10 stands at the row's opening edge, not inside it, so only one ¶ is internal and the other in fact corroborates the boundary the row is defending. (b) The English attached to the v12 quote runs past the Hebrew quoted: the gloss ends '...and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers', which renders וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו, a clause absent from the quoted Hebrew — and that omitted clause is the row's strongest lexical warrant for keeping vv12-13 with what precedes.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the paragraph description to one internal ¶; extend the v12 Hebrew quote to the end of the verse so quote and gloss cover the same text, and add oshb:2Chr.33.9 (PE, single-witness) to the refs as tier-3 corroboration of the opening edge.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both WEB paragraph breaks (before v10 and before v12) are real and the row's decision to override them is defensible on thematic grounds: v10's rejected-word notice, וַיְדַבֵּר יְהוָה אֶל מְנַשֶּׁה וְאֶל עַמּוֹ וְלֹא הִקְשִׁיבוּ, and v13's recognition formula, וַיֵּדַע מְנַשֶּׁה כִּי יְהוָה הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים, do bracket a single sin-to-restoration arc. But the row's rejected-alternative sentence undersells its own rival. It says the WEB ¶ before v12 'has ¶ support alone,' when v12 itself opens on וּכְהָצֵר לוֹ, a temporal/circumstantial protasis clause ('when he was in distress...') feeding the apodosis that follows — exactly the protasis-apodosis category the evidence rules name as tier-1, independent of the paragraph mark. That doesn't flip the boundary call, since the thematic unity argument is sound on its own, but the row misrepresents how thin the alternative's evidentiary base is.

challenges.claim: The rejected-alternative discussion attributes the competing v11/v12 split to WEB's paragraph mark alone ('¶ support alone'), but v12's own opening clause, וּכְהָצֵר לוֹ, is a protasis construction — a tier-1 category per the evidence rules — that exists independently of any WEB formatting. The row's framing overstates how weak the alternative is.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise the rejected-alternative sentence to acknowledge the protasis clause at v12 as a genuine (if ultimately non-decisive) text-internal consideration alongside the ¶ mark, rather than crediting the split to paragraph formatting alone.

primary_reviews.rationale: I confirmed the facts the corrections turn on. In the witness text a standalone paragraph mark precedes 33:10 and 33:12 and none precedes 33:11 or 33:13, so the corrected count of one internal break is right. The v12 quotation now matches the OSHB verse to its end and the English matches WEB word for word. 33:12 is indeed וּ + כְ + hiphil infinitive construct with חִלָּה as apodosis, so the rival really does sit at tier-1, and 7:14's וְיִכָּנְעוּ עַמִּי ... וְיִתְפַּלְלוּ וִיבַקְשׁוּ פָנַי collates exactly, so the rebuttal has real lexical purchase (33:12's חִלָּה אֶת פְּנֵי יְהוָה in fact answers the third verb too, which the row could use). Two things I would not let stand. First, fixing the count turned a description into an argument, and the argument runs on tier-4 markup. Second, and not filed, the rationale asserts that the Chronicler treats this sequence “as one theological arc elsewhere in the book” without naming a single other place; the only comparandum anywhere in the row is 7:14, and it sits in the rejected alternative. That sentence should either acquire a citation or be dropped.

challenges.claim: Correcting the paragraph count promoted a descriptive remark into an affirmative warrant drawn from tier-4 markup. The row's opening sentence now reasons that the mark before v10 “stands at the row's own opening edge, not inside it, so it corroborates rather than divides the unit” — WEB paragraphing supplying corroboration, and doing so as the first thing the rationale says. The contract classes that markup as metadata which is never evidence in either direction. Decision 148 in this same cluster was repaired by stripping the same markup out of both its positive rationale and its rejection grounds, so two standards are now running side by side within one cluster.
challenges.suggested_action: Open instead on the tier-1 material — v10's וַיְדַבֵּר יְהוָה אֶל formula and the shift of actor from Manasseh to Yahweh — and either delete the paragraph sentence or keep it flagged expressly as tier-4 non-evidence, with “corroborates” removed.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three defects in this row were argumentation-quality problems rather than boundary errors, and the revision fixes each at the level it was raised: the paragraph count is now accurate, the rival split is credited honestly, and the answer to it is textual rather than typographic. The row is stronger for having conceded ground instead of talking past the challenge.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Three challenges converge on one defect. LF-145-1 and OL-145-1 both catch that the rejected alternative brands the v11/v12 split as resting on '¶ support alone,' when v12 itself opens on וְּכְהָצֵר לוֹ, a kaph-prefixed infinitive-construct temporal protasis — confirmed against oshb:2Chr.33.12 — which is tier-1 evidence wholly independent of WEB formatting. OL's fuller version adds that this row's cluster-mate, M8-2Chr-152, credits an identically-shaped construction (וְּבְהוֹצִיאָם אֶת הַכֶסֶף) as tier-1 opening evidence for its own boundary, so the cluster currently weighs one device class two different ways; it also grounds the alternative's residual pull in the Chronicler's 7:14 כנע/תפלל program, which I verified reproduces lexeme-for-lexeme in 33:12-13 against oshb:2Chr.7.14. OL-145-2 adds two independently-verified citation-accuracy defects: the ¶ the row counts as one of 'two WEB paragraphs inside this row' actually sits at line 1023 of 2Chr_web_clean.txt, immediately before v10 — the row's own opening edge, not an internal break, so only the v12 ¶ (line 1026) is truly internal; and the v12 Hebrew quote stops at אֱלֹהָיו while the attached English gloss continues through 'humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,' rendering וַיִּכָּנַע מְאֹד מִלִּפְנֵי אֱלֹהֵי אֲבֹתָיו, a clause the quote omits though it is arguably the row's strongest lexical warrant for the merge. All three claims verified independently and ruled supported; this is one remedy split across three filings (restate the rejected alternative at its true tier, fix the ¶ count, extend the quote), not three separate defects. None of this flips the boundary — the sin-judgment-repentance arc and the PE at 33:9 (uncited tier-3 corroboration of the opening edge) still argue for the merge — but the rejected alternative needs rebuilding on accurate footing, and whether 'medium' confidence should move is a live question for the author/boss round, not something resolved here.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three quotes, all byte-exact and all sitting in the verse claimed. primary_reviews.rationale: I tested the two formulas this row rests on against the whole book rather than trusting the labels. The regesta opener וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁה֮ belongs to a set of ten (13:22; 20:34; 25:26; 26:22; 27:7; 28:26; 32:32; 33:18; 35:26; 36:8), every one of them at a reign closure. The death notice וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו belongs to a set of ten in the identical frame — including the offset-zone specimen web:2Chr.14.1 = oshb:2Chr.13.23 (MT), וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו — and its succession tail וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו to a set of twelve. The v19-as-expansion argument also holds syntactically, which is the part I could have broken and could not: v19 opens on a bare resumptive noun, וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ, repeating v18's, and lands in a verbless predication הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַ֖ל דִּבְרֵ֥י חוֹזָֽי that mirrors v18's הִנָּ֕ם עַל דִּבְרֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל with a different archive named — an expansion of the same citation, with no finite verb to start a unit on. Mark type checks out: pmarks keys PE to 2Chr.33.20 (single-witness), exactly as cited, and the WEB footnote at v19 offering 'the seers' is tier-4 and plays no part in either edge.

The register shift from reform narrative (v17) into archival citation (v18) is unambiguous, and v20's death-and-succession pair is one of the book's most frequent closing devices — a book-wide sweep for שכב + עם אבתיו found ten other instances (9:31, 12:16, 13:23, 16:13, 21:1, 26:2, 26:23, 27:9, 28:27, 32:33) and the succession half (וימלך...תחתיו) recurs even more broadly, so the row's implicit claim that this formula 'recurs closing reigns elsewhere in this book' is solidly true. The rejected alternative (treating v20 as Amon's opening rather than Manasseh's close) is correctly dismissed: the verb subjects throughout v20 stay with Manasseh, and Amon's own formula doesn't start until the age-clause at v21.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative rejects a v24 split because 'no formula break, dating clause, or ¶ marks it'. The first term is false. וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ עֲבָדָ֔יו is the regicide-conspiracy formula in its fullest 2Chr form, matched almost word for word by הִתְקַשְּׁר֨וּ עָלָ֜יו עֲבָדָ֗יו (Joash) and by וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר (Amaziah). Verse 25 then supplies a second formula-class signal, the people-of-the-land enthronement notice וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, whose only other instance in the book is וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ ... וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ תַֽחַת אָבִ֖יו. So the discarded split has two tier-1 formula signals, not none.

The father-comparison clauses in vv22-23 (כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה מְנַשֶּׁה אָבִיו / כְּהִכָּנַע מְנַשֶּׁה אָבִיו) are real and verbatim, giving the evaluation its own internal coherence distinct from a generic 'did evil' notice. The row is unusually honest about its own strongest rival: it names the v24 conspiracy-report shift as a genuine device change and then correctly notes that nothing — no dating clause, no formula break, no ¶ — actually marks it, which is exactly the kind of admission the medium confidence should reflect.

The concessions asked for were made properly and the Hebrew behind them collates: וַיִּקְשְׁרוּ עָלָיו עֲבָדָיו at 33:24 against הִתְקַשְּׁרוּ עָלָיו עֲבָדָיו at 24:25 and וַיִּקְשְׁרוּ עָלָיו קֶשֶׁר at 25:27, and 36:1's וַיַּמְלִיכֻהוּ תַחַת אָבִיו is where the row says it is and does concern Jehoahaz. Confidence medium remains right for a merge that now depends entirely on a distributional test about what opens reign-units.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's two challenges are both verified, and the first matters more than its severity label suggests because it exposes a place where LF's own 'supports' rationale is wrong on the facts, not just under-argued. LF's rationale praises the row for 'correctly' noting that 'nothing — no dating clause, no formula break, no ¶ — actually marks' the v24 conspiracy shift. That is false: v24's וַיִּקְשְׁרוּ עָלָיו עֲבָדָיו is the book's regicide-conspiracy formula, matched almost word for word by 24:25's הִתְקַשְּרוּ עָלָיו עֲבָדָיו (Joash) and 25:27's וַיִּקְשְׁרוּ עָלָיו קֶש׆ֶר (Amaziah) — both confirmed by direct collation — and v25's וַיַּמְלִיכוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ אֶת יֹאשִּיָּהוּ בְנוֹ תַּחְתָּיו matches 36:1's עַם הָאָרֶץ enthronement formula for Jehoahaz, also confirmed. Where LF took the row's claim at face value, OL tested it against the book's own conspiracy-and-succession pattern and falsified it; OL's evidence wins this disagreement outright. OL-148-2 is a separate, narrower point, also confirmed: the boundary_rationale's 'WEB keeps the whole account in one paragraph...with no internal ¶' functions as a supporting plank in the positive case (it appears immediately after the age-formula claim, not as a trailing aside), and the rejected alternative repeats ¶-absence as one of three grounds for dismissal — both uses are tier-4 material doing tier-1 work, contrary to the evidence-tier contract. Both challenges are ruled supported. Neither primary argues the merge itself is wrong — the reign-report's compactness and the unbroken Amon subject may still carry vv21-25 as one unit — but the rejected alternative needs to be rebuilt on the real (and now shown to be nontrivial) קשר/עם הארץ evidence rather than a false absence-of-formula claim, and that reopens whether 'medium' confidence is still the right call; that determination belongs to the author/boss round.

challenges.claim: The row calls וְלֹא סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול 'a self-contained evaluative formula that appears elsewhere in the book for other favorably-judged kings'. A book-wide sweep of the OSHB text falsifies the recurrence: ימין and שמאול co-occur in 2Chr only at 3:17, 4:6, 4:7, 4:8, 18:18, 23:10 and 34:2, and every instance but 34:2 is a spatial notice about temple furnishings, the heavenly court, or the positioning of guards — the idiom is a hapax as a royal evaluation in this book. The nearest evaluative סור-analogue for a favorably judged king is a different idiom, וְלֹא סָ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נָּה (Jehoshaphat). What does recur is the clause immediately before it, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה, one of five (25:2; 26:4; 27:2; 29:2; 34:2) — but that is the row's opening evaluation, not the closer it argues from.

primary_reviews.rationale: The core boundary logic is sound: v1's age-formula (בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנִים יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ בְמָלְכוֹ) is the same device class as Manasseh's and Amon's openings, and v3's double-dated clause is a genuinely different device (synchronism-style dating) from v1-2's undated evaluation — I independently confirmed Manasseh's own v3 (וַיָּשָׁב וַיִּבֶן אֶת הַבָּמוֹת) carries no dating clause at all, which is the real textual basis for treating Josiah's case differently, so that part of the analogy holds. A full sweep of 2Chr_oshb.txt for the root סר co-occurring with ימין returns exactly one hit in the entire book: 34:2 itself. The idiom is not a demonstrated recurring in-book formula-type; asserting that it recurs 'elsewhere in the book' is an overclaim the primary text doesn't support (a Deuteronomistic cross-book echo, e.g. 2Kgs 22:2, would be synoptic metadata under strategy §4, not valid in-book evidence anyway).

The criterion also needs stating because it is what excludes 24:2, וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יוֹאָ֛שׁ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה, the same evaluative clause with the royal subject interposed for another favorably-judged king.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF-149-1 and OL-149-1 converge on the same finding via independent sweep methods, and I ran a third, independent check to adjudicate: a consonantal scan of 2Chr_oshb.txt for bare ימין co-occurring with שמאול (after correcting for medial-vs-final nun forms, which silently broke a naive substring match on the first pass) returns exactly five hits — 3:17, 4:6, 4:7, 4:8, 34:2 — and every one but 34:2 is a spatial notice (temple pillars, lavers, menorahs). primary_reviews.rationale: Collation passes on each of this row's three citations, and both edges survive pressure from the Hebrew side. The opener וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ is a full dating formula of the same year-count class as v3's, and the SAMEKH the row cites for the preceding verse is correctly typed against pmarks (2Chr.34.7, single-witness). The one seam I probed inside the span is v12, where the syntax shifts from that wayyiqtol chain to a participial register clause, וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֩ עֹשִׂ֨ים בֶּאֱמוּנָ֜ה בַּמְּלָאכָ֗ה; but no dating clause, formula, mark or paragraph stands there, and splitting a five-verse funding notice from a two-verse overseer list would cut finer still in a draft already running below the strategy's verses-per-decision estimate, so the merge is right. Two OSHB orthographic notes that touch nothing structural: v9 carries the ketiv-qere pair וישבי וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרֽוּשָׁלִָֽם, where WEB renders the ketiv ('the inhabitants of Jerusalem') while the qere reads 'and they returned to Jerusalem', and v5 the pair מזבחותים מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֑ם. Neither bears on an edge.

The eighteenth-year dating formula at v8 (וּבִשְׁנַת שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לְמָלְכוֹ) is a fresh, unambiguous synchronism opener following directly on v7's SAMEKH-marked return, and the funding chain in vv9-12 (Levite gatekeepers to overseeing workmen to carpenters/builders) is narrated as one continuous hand-off exactly as described. The closing personnel list at v13 (וּמֵהַלְוִיִּם סוֹפְרִים וְשֹׁטְרִים וְשׁוֹעֲרִים) does read as a register-closing formula rather than a transitional aside, and v14's pivot to the law-book discovery is a real topic change with no verbal bridge back to the money thread. I don't find a stronger unargued seam inside vv8-13; the administrative content resists further splitting without breaking the funding chain's own internal logic.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quotes collate byte-exact, and the edges survive the harder test I could put to them. Coming in, וּבְהוֹצִיאָ֣ם אֶת הַכֶּ֔סֶף is a verse-initial beth-prefixed infinitive-construct temporal protasis — the same device class I am pressing row M8-2Chr-145 to concede at 33:12 — and here it is used consistently, as a unit opener. Going out, v19's וַיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ is one of only three ויהי כשמע pivots in the book (10:2; 16:5; 34:19), each of them turning the narrative onto a new actor's reaction, so the seam at v18/v19 is as clean as the row claims. On the contested ¶ before v16 I looked for what the row's negative formulation passes over: vv15, 16 and 18 each carry a speech or report frame — וַיַּ֣עַן חִלְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל שָׁפָ֣ן הַסּוֹפֵ֔ר, וַיָּ֨שֶׁב ע֧וֹד אֶת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר, וַיַּגֵּ֞ד שָׁפָ֤ן הַסּוֹפֵר֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֔ר — and speech frames are tier-1. That is a stronger rival than 'no dating clause or archival formula' concedes; but none of the three is paired with a resumption formula afterwards, so under the campaign's inset rule they stay inside their host narrative, and the row's own rejected alternative does name the real device at v16 (the scene change to the king) rather than hiding behind the ¶ — which is exactly the honesty I found missing at 33:12. Medium confidence is if anything conservative given the strength of the v19 opener.

This row does the honest thing with a genuinely live paragraph tension rather than ignoring it: WEB's ¶ before v16 marks a real scene shift (temple precinct to throne room), and the row names that directly as its strongest rejected alternative before explaining why the found-told-carried-reported-read chain across vv14-18 is a tighter causal unit than the formatting break. That's a defensible judgment call, not an overreach, and the medium confidence is an honest reflection of the tension rather than a hedge against a weak case.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three quotations, three exact hits at 35:7, 35:8 and 35:9; the SAMEKH cite matches pmarks at 2Chr.35.7 and is disclosed as cutting against the row's own span, which is the honest way to handle it. The triadic-form argument is far better evidenced in the Hebrew than the row shows. All three tiers are built on the same hiphil of רום — וַיָּ֣רֶם (v7), הֵרִ֑ימוּ (v8), הֵרִ֨ימוּ (v9) — and each tally terminates in an identical cattle-clause shape: וּבָקָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֑ים at v7's atnach, וּבָקָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת verse-final at v8, and וּבָקָ֖ר חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת verse-final at v9. A book-wide sweep of הרימו / וירם over 2Chr returns only 30:24 and this trio, and 30:24 is itself a two-tier version of the same donor form (Hezekiah with הֵרִ֨ים, then וְהַשָּׂרִ֞ים הֵרִ֤ימוּ) — an in-book parallel, which strategy §4 admits as literary evidence, and it independently supports reading 7-9 as one donor set that a tier-3 mark should not sever. The row's arithmetic also checks out against the text (30,000 flock and 3,000 cattle; 2,600 and 300; 5,000 and 500). My two objections concern quotation precision only.

The cluster's other quotes avoid the issue by slicing clear of the K/Q pairs at 34:22, 34:25 and 35:3.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three donor tiers share the donor-then-livestock-count shape and a repeated רום root across finite verbs (וַיָּ֣רֶם / הֵרִ֑ימוּ / הֵרִ֨ימוּ), so reading vv7-9 as one triadic tally is grounded in the verb pattern itself, not just asserted; letting the matched form outweigh the trailing SAMEKH tracks the marker policy's stated weighting rather than overriding it.

The tally logic is sound and the numbers behind it check out. WEB 35:7 does give thirty thousand from the flock and three thousand bulls, matching למספר שלשים אלף ובקר שלשת אלפים in the Hebrew, and the same donor-then-count shape recurs at v8 (2,600 and 300) and v9 (5,000 and 500), so the threefold pattern the row weighs against the mark is really there. The SAMEKH after 35:7 is correctly located and correctly subordinated: letting a tier-3 mark sever the king's gift from two tiers built on its own template would invert the evidence order the contract sets. Declining to treat v10's completion register as part of the tally is likewise right. My challenge concerns only the precision of the ketiv/qere disclosure that the repair added.

challenges.claim: The disclosure added to cure the round-one item overstates what the qere covers. The row says v9 ‘opens with the ketiv וכונניהו, pointed as the qere וְ֠כָֽנַנְיָהוּ וּשְׁמַֽעְיָ֨הוּ’. primary_reviews.rationale: The bracket quotations collate exactly and are verse-initial at both 35:10 and 35:16, and the morphological claim is correct: וַתִּכּ֖וֹן and וַ֠תִּכּוֹן are both niphal wayyiqtol 3fs of כון. A sweep of the consonantal string ותכון over 2Chr returns exactly three verses — 29:35, 35:10, 35:16 — so this pair is the only adjacent occurrence in the book, real support for reading them as a matched frame. The shared royal-command tag is likewise verifiable rather than impressionistic: v10 closes כְּמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ and v16 closes כְּמִצְוַ֖ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ, consonantally the same phrase with a name appended and differing accentuation, and כמצות המלך occurs only four times in 2Chr (29:15, 30:6, 35:10, 35:16). One asymmetry the row should own rather than a defect: the third instance, 29:35 וַתִּכּ֖וֹן עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית יְהוָֽה, stands unit-final at the close of the Hezekiah cleansing, so the in-book pattern shows this formula behaving as a terminal summary — which corroborates v16 as a closer while making v10 the less typical of the two legs. My substantive objection lies at an internal seam the row passes over.

challenges.claim: vv14-15 are syntactically a different kind of text from the rest of the span, and the row does not argue them. Verses 10-13 and 16 are wayyiqtol-driven (וַתִּכּ֖וֹן, וַיַּֽעַמְד֨וּ, וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ, וַיִּזְרְק֤וּ, וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ, וַֽיְבַשְּׁל֥וּ, וַיָּרִ֖יצוּ, וַ֠תִּכּוֹן), whereas vv14-15 contain no wayyiqtol at all: v14 opens וְאַחַ֗ר הֵכִ֤ינוּ with qatal, repeats הֵכִ֣ינוּ at v14b, and v15 opens with a verbless clause, וְהַמְשֹֽׁרֲרִ֨ים בְּנֵי אָסָ֜ף עַל מַעֲמָדָ֗ם. וְאַחַ֗ר is the only standalone token of that form in 2Chr, and a temporal transition heading a chain-break is tier-1 in the device matrix. This is an unargued internal seam at 13/14 inside a seven-verse, medium-confidence span, and strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only the closing edge, leaving both the opening edge and this seam untested.

The span may stand; the argument as written does not cover it.

challenges.claim: The load-bearing lexical tie is asserted in English and never quoted, and the English used is not WEB's. 'so the service was made ready', 'so all the service of Yahweh was made ready' and 'the children of Israel who were present did...' are glosses; WEB reads 'So the service was prepared', 'So all the service of Yahweh was prepared the same day' and 'The children of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time'. Likewise 'commandment of the king' matches neither verse in WEB (35:10 'according to the king's commandment'; 35:16 'according to the commandment of King Josiah'), while the Hebrew that would prove the point, כְּמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ against כְּמִצְוַ֖ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ, is never quoted. I verified the claim is true; it is the demonstration that is missing, contrary to the rule that original-language claims quote the form.

primary_reviews.rationale: The תכן root genuinely brackets this unit — וַתִּכּ֖וֹן הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה in v10 and וַ֠תִּכּוֹן כָּל עֲבוֹדַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה in v16 are the same verb scaled from 'the service' to 'all the service of Yahweh' — and the row is candid rather than evasive about its one real complication, since WEB's own paragraph break falls between v15 and v16, not between v16 and v17 as a forward reading would require.

The inclusio the row is built on is genuine and now properly demonstrated: ותכון העבודה with כמצות המלך at v10 and ותכון כל עבודת יהוה with כמצות המלך יאשיהו at v16 both slice byte-exact, and the widening from bare king to named king is visible in the Hebrew rather than inferred from the English. Handling the WEB paragraph before v16 as a rival's ground and then defeating it on lexical grounds keeps the tier-4 material in its place; I confirmed that break does fall where the row says. Medium confidence is right for a seven-verse span with a live internal question. But the parenthesis argument, which is the whole cure here, rests on a claim about vv11-13 that the text does not support.

challenges.claim: The parenthetical ‘vv11-13, all wayyiqtol’ is false on two counts, and it is the premise the vv14-15 parenthesis is argued from. v11 ends on a subject-plus-participle clause, וְהַלְוִיִּ֖ם מַפְשִׁיטִֽים, with no finite verb; v13 ends its middle clause on a fronted object with a plain qatal, וְהַקֳּדָשִׁ֣ים בִּשְּׁל֗וּ, before ויריצו resumes. The two clause types the row treats as diagnostic of vv14-15 — qatal and verbless — are therefore already present inside the block it calls uniformly wayyiqtol, so the register contrast as stated does not hold. The round-one item said vv10-13 and 16 were wayyiqtol-driven; the repair hardened that into an absolute, which the text falsifies.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate as wayyiqtol-driven rather than uniformly wayyiqtol, and turn the correction to the row's advantage: because the execution report demonstrably tolerates a participial clause at v11b and a fronted-object qatal at v13b, vv14-15 extend a pattern already attested inside the span rather than breaking its register, which strengthens the parenthesis reading against a 10-13 / 14-15 division. Span stays; medium confidence stays.

Because the load-bearing statement here is an exclusivity one, I ran it rather than trusting it: inside chapter 36 the citation head occurs at v8 only, and the dynastic replacement tag תַּחְתָּֽיו likewise at v8 only (16 occurrences book-wide, none of the rest falling in this chapter). Restricting the full citation-plus-succession pairing to Jehoiakim alone is therefore true as written, and the contrast drawn with v10's bare appointment clause does sharpen this unit's far edge. Both PE cites, after v4 and after v8, agree with pmarks (single-witness), and neither is a double-mark verse. Two phrasings are loose without being wrong: an atnach separates the citation from וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו inside v8, so 'running straight into' is generous, and the tier-1 element at v4 is the appointment clause in that verse's first half rather than the deportation clause it ends on. Neither touches the boundary.

The comparison this row draws between Jehoiakim's full citation-plus-succession close and Jehoiachin's bare deportation notice just below is exactly the kind of local, checkable literary claim that should anchor a boundary call, and it holds when read against the actual text of vv9-10.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Unchallenged by both primaries, and rightly so on my own check. The exclusivity claims are the part most worth re-running rather than trusting, and they hold: the citation head and the dynastic tag תַּחְתָּּיו both land at v8 only within chapter 36, and no citation formula appears anywhere in vv9-10, so the Jehoiakim/Jehoiachin contrast the row draws is real. Spot-checked and confirmed; no action needed.

post_resolution_check.notes: The double citation-plus-succession formula at v8 checked directly and correctly contrasted with v10's bare deportation-and-succession close; PE marks at 36:4 and 36:8 both match pmarks.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quotations check out letter for letter, and the two PE cites (after v8, after v10) match the mark data with the right type. I think the edges themselves are right: v9 opens on the chapter's third age-formula, v11 on its fourth. But three statements inside the rationale fail against the Hebrew. The closing device is misidentified, the reign-length comparison is inverted and collides with a sibling row in this same cluster, and a chapter-wide generalization breaks at its fourth member. None of the three moves the span; all three should be corrected before this text is published as reasoning.

challenges.claim: Calling v10's close the very device that ends v8 merges two different tier-1 formulas. v8 has the qal succession shape וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, where the incoming king is the subject and the final word תַּחְתָּֽיו marks dynastic replacement; v10 has the causative וַיַּמְלֵךְ֙ אֶת צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָחִ֔יו עַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם, where the appointee is an accusative object and no replacement tag appears at all. v10's real twin is v4, וַיַּמְלֵ֨ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֜יִם אֶת אֶלְיָקִ֣ים אָחִ֗יו עַל יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם: same stem, same object-plus-brother-plus-over-Judah frame, same foreign agent.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the closing device as the imperial-appointment clause paired with v4 rather than the dynastic succession formula of v8, and carry oshb:2Chr.36.4 into the refs as that comparandum.

challenges.claim: 'the shortest reign in the chapter' is false on the numerals the text gives: Jehoiachin reigned וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (v9) while Jehoahaz reigned וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם (36:2), which is ten days less. M8-2Chr-164 asserts the opposite about the same two reigns, so as frozen the two rows contradict each other.
challenges.suggested_action: Strike or reverse the superlative in this row; the version in 164 is the one the Hebrew supports.

challenges.claim: Generalizing an opening age-formula plus a closing succession clause to all four reign-units of the chapter fails at the last of them. Zedekiah opens with the age-formula at v11, but nothing closes his reign that way: a sweep of chapter 36 puts תַּחְתָּֽיו at v8 alone and the causative installation verb at vv1, 4, 8 and 10, every one of them before v11.
challenges.suggested_action: Scope the claim to the chapter's first three reigns, or drop the universal and let the edge rest on the v11 age-formula by itself.

primary_reviews.rationale: The two-verse span itself is well anchored by the recurring age-formula and by the observation that this reign alone lacks any citation notice, but the row's descriptive claim about reign length collides head-on with a sibling row in this same cluster, and the rejected alternative on offer doesn't put up the strongest available fight.

challenges.claim: This row calls Jehoiachin's reign of 'three months and ten days' (oshb:2Chr.36.9, וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֔ים) 'the shortest reign in the chapter,' but M8-2Chr-164 in this same cluster calls Jehoahaz's 'three months' (oshb:2Chr.36.2, וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים) 'the shortest recorded here.' Three months is strictly shorter than three months and ten days, so the two claims cannot both be true -- Jehoahaz's reign is the shorter one, and this row's superlative is arithmetically wrong.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop or correct the 'shortest reign in the chapter' claim in M8-2Chr-166; Jehoahaz's three-month reign (v2) already holds that distinction per M8-2Chr-164.

challenges.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative ('Reading v10 as an appendix tacked onto Jehoiakim's block (vv5-8)...') misstates which verse carries the age-formula (it is v9, not v10) and does not engage the toughest rival reading. Jehoiachin's notice is the thinnest reign-report in the chapter -- two verses, no citation formula at all, per this row's own observation -- which makes a forward merge with Zedekiah's notice (treating vv9-14 as the two citation-less closing reigns) the more serious alternative to dispose of, rather than an appendix-to-Jehoiakim reading the age-formula argument already defeats easily elsewhere in this cluster.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the rejected alternative with the forward-merge-into-Zedekiah reading and explain why the recurring age-formula still wins against it.

primary_reviews.rationale: Five Hebrew strings collate byte-exact, the two PE disclosures match pmarks at 2Chr.36.8 and 2Chr.36.10, and the arithmetic repair is sound. The v4/v10 pairing is the strongest thing in the revised row: both clauses run causative verb, object marker plus appointee, אָחִ֗יו apposition, and the territorial phrase, with no replacement tag in either, so the distinction drawn against v8's תַּחְתָּֽיו is exactly right. The trouble lies in what the scoping edit put where the old universal stood. Rewritten to cover the chapter's first three reign-units, the generalisation is falsified by this row's own neighbouring sentence and by two of the three units it names. A second, smaller slip in the same sentence calls the agent behind v10's appointment unnamed when the verse names him. Both arrived with the repair, both are checkable inside one chapter, and both are filed. The boundary at 36:9-10 is untouched by either and stays well founded on the age-formula opening.

challenges.claim: The scoped replacement reads “the age-formula opening this reign and the causative-installation clause closing it are the devices marking the chapter's first three reign-units (vv1-10)”. Neither half survives a sweep of those units. On the closing side, vv5-8 ends on וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (oshb:2Chr.36.8), the qal succession formula this very row separates from the causative two clauses earlier; and vv1-4 ends on וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה (oshb:2Chr.36.4), the causative appointment standing mid-verse rather than at the close, as M8-2Chr-164 states in this same cluster. On the opening side, unit one begins at וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ (oshb:2Chr.36.1), the age-formula arriving only at v2 — again as M8-2Chr-164 states. The pairing therefore holds in full for vv9-10 alone, one unit rather than three. This is second-generation: the first-round item asked for scoping, and the scoping edit substituted a claim the chapter contradicts.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the three-unit generalisation and rest on what is demonstrable — that this reign opens on the recurring age-formula and closes on a causative appointment clause whose only true parallel in the chapter is v4 — or restate it as a device inventory across vv1-10 without asserting each unit opens and closes on the pair.

challenges.claim: The row describes v10's appointment as one “where the appointee is an accusative object under an unnamed foreign agent”. That agent is named in the same verse: oshb:2Chr.36.10 opens וְלִתְשׁוּבַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֗ה שָׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֔ר, and that subject carries through to וַיַּמְלֵךְ֙. M8-2Chr-169 in this cluster counts 36:10 among the four namings of Nebuchadnezzar in the chapter, so two frozen rows now disagree about one verse. The defensible statement is narrower: the causative verb leaves its subject unexpressed in its own clause, unlike v4 where מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֜יִם stands inside it.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace “unnamed” with a note that the causative clause leaves its subject unexpressed although the verse has already named Nebuchadnezzar, which strengthens rather than weakens the parallel with v4's named foreign appointer.

primary_reviews.rationale: All five original items are cured, but the OL-166-3 fix creates a fresh internal contradiction. Two sentences earlier the row correctly separates v8's closing device (Qal, where the new king is himself the grammatical subject) from v10's construction (appointee as accusative object under a foreign agent); the very next sentence then generalizes that same causative label across the whole opening stretch of the chapter, which requires v8 -- closing the second of those three units, Jehoiakim's -- to fit the causative pattern too. It does not: 2Chr_oshb.txt shows v1 and v4 and v10 all Hiphil causative (וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ, וַיַּמְלֵ֨ךְ, וַיַּמְלֵךְ֙) against v8's Qal וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ. The row's own two sentences now describe incompatible patterns for the same verse. Filed as one new item.

challenges.claim: The row's fix for OL-166-3 introduces a self-contradiction rather than resolving one. It first distinguishes v8's closing device -- the Qal succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, incoming king as subject -- from v10's causative installation clause, then two sentences later asserts 'the age-formula opening this reign and the causative-installation clause closing it are the devices marking the chapter's first three reign-units (vv1-10),' which requires v8 to be causative as well. A direct pull of the four מלך forms in ch36 (v1 וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ, v4 וַיַּמְלֵ֨ךְ, v8 וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ, v10 וַיַּמְלֵךְ֙) confirms v8 alone is Qal, not causative -- exactly the verse the row itself just set apart.
challenges.suggested_action: Either drop 'the causative-installation clause' from the generalized closing description and use a label that actually fits v8 too (an installation-type closer, causative in two of the three cases), or keep the causative claim scoped to v1/v4/v10 alone and state plainly that v8 closes its own reign-unit on the different, Qal self-succession device.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This row draws the heaviest challenge traffic in the cluster, and the results split three ways. First, the reign-length collision is real and both sides caught it independently: Jehoiachin's וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֔ים (v9) is ten days longer than Jehoahaz's וּשְלֹשָה חֳדָשִים (36:2), so 'the shortest reign in the chapter' belongs to M8-2Chr-164, not here. LF-M8-2Chr-166-1 and OL-M8-2Chr-166-2 are the same finding approached from two directions and both are supported outright; one remedy covers both -- drop or reverse the superlative in this row. Second, OL-M8-2Chr-166-1 correctly separates two formulas the row conflates: v8's qal וַיִּמְלֹךְ יְהוֹיָכִין בְּנו תַּחְתָּּיו (the incoming king himself as subject) is not the same construction as v10's causative וַיַּמְלֵךְ אֶת צִדְקִּיָהו אָחִיו (the appointee as accusative object under a foreign agent's verb) -- v10's actual formal twin is v4's וַיַּמְלֵךְ מֶּלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם אֶת אֶלְיָקִים אָחִיו, matched stem for stem. Third, OL-M8-2Chr-166-3's core point also holds: nothing closes Zedekiah's reign the way this row's 'every reign-unit' claim requires, since a chapter sweep puts the causative installation verb at vv1, 4, and 10 and the distinct qal-plus-תַּחְתָּּיו pairing at v8 alone, none of it recurring at or after v11 -- though the sweep as phrased folds v8 into the 'causative' count when v8 is actually the qal form OL's own preceding challenge isolates, so I log the conclusion as supported but the tally as needing that one-word fix. LF-M8-2Chr-166-2 does not clear the bar: the row already attributes the age-formula to v9, not v10 ('v9 opens with the identical age-formula'), so the 'misstates which verse' objection targets a misstatement the text does not contain, and its proposed rival grouping (Jehoiachin-plus-Zedekiah as 'the two citation-less closing reigns') rests on a premise that a citation-less report is unusual here, when in fact three of this chapter's four reigns lack one -- only Jehoiakim's has it -- so the alternative is not obviously the stronger reading the challenge claims. None of this moves the v9/v10 span itself, which two independent age-formula walks confirm; what needs revision is the descriptive prose layered on top of it.

boss_ruling.reasoning: Three of five items held: v10's true twin is v4's causative frame, the shortest-reign superlative belongs to Jehoahaz, and the every-reign universal fails at Zedekiah. The age-formula verse claim was wrong and is rejected with the peer. Rebuilt on the installation-verb taxonomy, the row stands.

post_resolution_check.notes: The v4/v10 causative-installation 'stem for stem' comparison verified directly -- the same hiphil frame installs a brother king in both -- and the self-falsifying sweep of the chapter's first three reign-units' formula pairing checked against those verses and holds.

primary_reviews.rationale: The two citations are exact and rightly placed, and the mark cited at 36:10 is a PE as labelled (single-witness); nothing between v11 and v14 carries a mark, and the row does not pretend otherwise. The narrative substance of vv12-13 answers to the Hebrew (לֹ֣א נִכְנַ֗ע מִלִּפְנֵ֛י יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא and מָרָ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבִּיע֖וֹ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֑ים), and the fork the row flags at v14 is a real one. What I cannot verify is the reason it gives for resolving that fork, which describes a participant continuity the chapter does not have. The span can survive on better evidence sitting a clause away.

challenges.claim: v14 does not keep naming actors already introduced in Zedekiah's regnal notice. vv11-13 name only the king, the prophet and Nebuchadnezzar; the priestly chiefs and the people enter for the first time at v14, and they enter as an addition: גַּ֠ם כָּל שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהָעָם֙. The tie the Hebrew does supply is the additive chain running from v13's own head, וְ֠גַם בַּמֶּ֤לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּר֙ מָרָ֔ד, into v14, and a sweep finds that particle at only three points in the chapter (וְ֠גַם v13, גַּ֠ם v14, and once more at v22), so the pair is tight rather than incidental.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the actor-continuity claim with the additive chain across vv13-14, which supports the same span on evidence that holds, and leave 36:11-14 as drawn.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row is admirably honest about the v14/v15 fork rather than papering over it, but the tie-breaker it offers doesn't survive its own logic once the device doing the work -- a shift of grammatical subject -- is checked against how the very next row in this cluster uses that identical device to open its own span.

challenges.claim: The row concedes the vv14-16 guilt-then-response grouping is 'defensible' and resolves the fork by noting v14 'still nam[es] the human wrongdoers inside Zedekiah's own reign-report.' But v14 opens with גַּ֠ם כָּל שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהָעָם֙ הִרְבּ֣וּ (oshb:2Chr.36.14) -- an extension-particle-marked shift from Zedekiah's exclusively singular subject in vv11-13 (3ms verbs) to a new plural corporate subject. That is the same class of device -- a grammatical-subject change -- that M8-2Chr-168 relies on to justify its own opening edge at v15 ('its edges rest on a shift of grammatical subject rather than any recurring formula'). The criterion is applied inconsistently: subject-change counts as boundary-relevant at v14/v15 but not at the comparable v13/v14 shift.
challenges.suggested_action: Either state explicitly why a human-to-human subject shift (v13/14) is weaker boundary evidence than a human-to-divine shift (v14/15), or concede v14's attachment is genuinely contested between this row and M8-2Chr-168.

primary_reviews.rationale: The substituted evidence is good and it verifies: allowing a prefixed waw, גם occurs in chapter 36 at exactly three points, two of them adjacent, so the pairing across vv13-14 is as tight as claimed. All four Hebrew strings collate byte-exact, and the PE disclosed at 2Chr.36.10 matches pmarks, correctly corroborating the opening seam at v11. One error entered with the rewrite, and it concerns the very clause that now carries the argument. The row places the additive clause at the end of v13, then three sentences later calls the same clause v13's head. The Hebrew settles it against the first description, and the disagreement is visible without leaving the row. The fix is local and the span survives it, since the chain argument works from that clause's initial position rather than a final one.

challenges.claim: The rationale says the reign narrative is “closing v13 on וְ֠גַם בַּמֶּ֤לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּר֙ מָרָ֔ד”. That clause opens the verse rather than closing it: oshb:2Chr.36.13 runs וְ֠גַם בַּמֶּ֤לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּר֙ מָרָ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבִּיע֖וֹ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֑ים וַיֶּ֤קֶשׁ אֶת עָרְפּוֹ֙ וַיְאַמֵּ֣ץ אֶת לְבָב֔וֹ מִשּׁ֕וּב אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, whose terminal words are מִשּׁ֕וּב אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל. The row contradicts itself shortly afterwards with “the additive particle chain running from v13's own head into v14”, which is both the correct placement and the one the chain argument needs — an adjacent pair of verse-initial particles, not a verse-final one answered by a verse-initial one.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace “closing v13 on” with a statement that the rebellion clause heads v13, so the two additive particles stand at the head of consecutive verses; the vv12-13 reference and everything downstream need no change.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both items are cured on the same move: the row stops claiming v14 shares vv11-13's subject and instead grounds the tie in the גם/וגם chain, which a chapter-wide sweep confirms occurs exactly three times (v13, v14, v22). The rejected-alternative now names the fork with M8-2Chr-168 honestly rather than asserting a settled answer. No fresh defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both challenges here converge on the same seam and both are right about it. The row keeps v14 inside Zedekiah's unit by claiming it 'still names the same corporate actors ... introduced within Zedekiah's own regnal notice,' but that is not what vv11-13 contain -- they name only the king, Jeremiah, and Nebuchadnezzar, and כָּל שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהָעָם֙ enters for the first time at v14, not as a repeat of anyone already on stage. LF-M8-2Chr-167-1 is supported for noticing that the row leans on a subject-change of exactly this kind while denying that subject-change is doing any boundary work here, a standard the very next row (M8-2Chr-168) applies in the opposite direction for its own edge. OL-M8-2Chr-167-1 is supported for supplying the tie that actually holds: the additive particle chain running וְגַם (v13) into גַּם (v14), which a chapter-36 sweep finds recurring only once more, at v22 -- three hits total, tight enough to anchor the join on cohesion the Hebrew actually offers instead of a false claim of shared participants. Neither correction disturbs the span; both improve the case for keeping it exactly where it is, and the same גַּם-chain evidence is what resolves the parallel tension flagged under M8-2Chr-168 below.

primary_reviews.rationale: Quotations at v15 and v16 are exact, the glosses are fair, and no mark is claimed anywhere in this row, which is right since pmarks records none between 36:10 and 36:19. The near edge is sound: v15 does front Yahweh as a new explicit subject. The far edge is not, and the failure is syntactic rather than interpretive, because the agent said to arrive in v17 arrives there as a grammatical object. Running the compassion vocabulary book-wide then turned up a lexical tie across the very seam being claimed. Given that the row's own confidence is already medium_low and the exile stretch is flagged in the strategy as thin ground, the far edge needs rebuilding before this span is adjudicated.

challenges.claim: The far edge rests entirely on a 'wholly new named agent' entering at v17, but the Chaldean king enters as an object, not an agent: וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים, where the object marker standing in אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ makes that noun phrase accusative, so the verb is causative and its unexpressed subject is still Yahweh from vv15-16 (WEB reads it the same way, 'Therefore he brought on them the king of the Chaldeans'), and the verse ends with Yahweh still acting, הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ. The ketiv/qere at that word is orthographic and does not touch the syntax. No agent change happens at this seam, so the row's sole stated warrant for the closing edge is not in the text.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-argue the v16/v17 edge from something the Hebrew carries, for instance the shift from the iterative sending-and-scoffing summary of vv15-16 to punctual narrative action in v17, or reopen the rejected alternative and grade the row down to low.

challenges.claim: The compassion verb occurs exactly twice in the whole of 2Chr, and both occurrences straddle the proposed seam: כִּֽי חָמַ֥ל עַל עַמּ֖וֹ וְעַל מְעוֹנֽוֹ (v15) and וְלֹ֥א חָמַ֛ל עַל בָּח֥וּר וּבְתוּלָ֖ה (v17). A book-exclusive positive/negative pair of this kind is in-book lexical evidence for the alternative the row set aside, vv15 onward as a single movement. I log it as counterweight rather than proof, since an antithesis can also be composed across a boundary.
challenges.suggested_action: Answer this pair explicitly in the rejected-alternative sentence, whichever way the mesh finally settles the seam; oshb:2Chr.36.17 is already in the row's refs and can carry it.

primary_reviews.rationale: Read alone this row's logic is tidy -- Yahweh's initiative differs in kind from the corporate-guilt subject that precedes it, and the new-agent entrance at v17 is a legitimate scene-break -- but the same subject-change reasoning this row leans on for its opening edge is available a verse earlier too, and the row doesn't rule that reading out.

But oshb:2Chr.36.14 (גַּ֠ם כָּל שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהָעָם֙ הִרְבּ֣וּ) already marks a subject shift of its own, from Zedekiah (vv11-13) to the priests-and-people, using the identical device class this row invokes. primary_reviews.rationale: This is the most thoroughly reworked row in the cluster and the heavy lifting is sound. Eight quotes collate byte-exact. Two book-level claims verify on sweep: חמל appears twice in 2Chr, at 36:15 and 36:17, and מרפא appears twice, at 21:18 and 36:16, so both the parallel and the positive-negative pairing hold exactly as stated. The syntactic correction is right — אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ is accusative and no fresh agent takes the stage at v17 — and the refusal to claim any tier-3 corroboration is also right, since pmarks keys no mark to 36:14 through 36:17. Two low-grade items remain. The replacement register argument characterises v17 as a dated invasion, and the verse carries no date. Separately, the row runs an orthographic pair together inline without saying so, on the same word its cluster-mate discloses after an upheld first-round item. Neither disturbs the low-confidence call, which I consider appropriately graded for this stretch.

challenges.claim: The rebuilt far-edge warrant contrasts vv15-16's iterative register with “v17's punctual narrative action (a single dated invasion, executed and complete)”. No date appears in v17. oshb:2Chr.36.17 reads וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים ... הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ, with no year, month or day element anywhere in it; the chapter's dating elements sit at 36:9-11 and 36:22, not here. Because this sentence is the entire replacement warrant for an edge whose original ground was struck down at high severity, an inaccurate descriptor inside it matters more than it otherwise would.
challenges.suggested_action: Delete “dated” and let the contrast rest on what the verbs carry: iterative infinitive-absolute sending set against a chain of punctual wayyiqtol actions completed inside the verse.

challenges.claim: The row quotes וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים with the unpointed and pointed forms run together and nothing to signal that these are a ketiv/qere pair rather than two words of running text. M8-2Chr-169 in this same cluster quotes the identical stretch and does disclose it, that disclosure having been required by an upheld first-round item on this very word. A reader collating this row alone would take כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים for a construct sequence.
challenges.suggested_action: Add the parenthetical the neighbouring row carries — ketiv כשדיים, qere כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים — noting the variation is orthographic and leaves untouched the accusative syntax the argument depends on.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three items land where requested: the false 'new agent' claim at v17 is gone, the edge rests on register (iterative sending-and-scoffing versus punctual invasion) rather than a nonexistent subject change, confidence drops to low to match the thinner tier-1 warrant, and the compassion-verb antithesis is now weighed explicitly rather than ignored. Cross-checked against the revised M8-2Chr-167 row for the shared v14/v15 tension and found the two now cohere. No fresh issue found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This is the row carrying the cluster's sharpest finding. The near edge holds -- v15 does front Yahweh as a fresh explicit subject against v14's corporate human actors -- and LF-M8-2Chr-168-1 is supported for tracing the resulting inconsistency back to M8-2Chr-167's treatment of that same device one verse earlier, a tension resolved for both rows under M8-2Chr-167 above via the גַּם-chain, without moving either span. The far edge does not hold as argued, and OL-M8-2Chr-168-1 is supported at the severity it was flagged: the row's sole warrant for the v16/v17 seam is 'a wholly new named agent,' but מֶ֣לֶךְ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים enters v17 under אֶת, the accusative object marker, not as a grammatical subject -- the Hiphil וַיַּעַל that introduces him carries no expressed subject of its own, and the verse's own close, הַכֹּל נָתַן בְּיָדוֹ, still requires an antecedent giver, which nothing in v17 supplies except Yahweh continuing from vv15-16. No new agent takes the grammatical subject slot anywhere in this verse; the claimed break is not in the text as the row states it. Given the row's own confidence is already medium_low and it sits inside the exile stretch the strategy independently flags as thin ground, this finding bears directly on that confidence, though the call on lowering it belongs to the author/boss round, not to me. OL-M8-2Chr-168-2 is supported as a secondary, lower-weight observation: חָמַל occurs exactly twice in the whole of 2 Chronicles, at v15 and again at v17 (a full-book sweep confirms no third instance), forming a positive-then-negative pair straddling the very seam in question -- offered rightly as counterweight to consider rather than as proof, since the same pairing could just as easily be composed across a genuine boundary.
