boss_ruling.reasoning: Yahweh remains the operative subject at 36:17 (the king is the et-marked object of the causative), so the new-agent warrant was false — twice found independently. The replacement register-shift warrant is honest but thin, inside a strategy-flagged stretch; low ratified, span kept, and the chamal catchword pair recorded as a relation for convergence.

post_resolution_check.notes: Honestly grades down to low given that the register shift (iterative to punctual) isn't one of the book's named tier-1 formula types; the 21:18 'no remedy' comparandum checked and matches.

primary_reviews.rationale: All five Hebrew citations in this row slice clean: each is a byte-exact substring of the verse it is assigned to, and each string occurs in exactly one verse of the whole book, so nothing is misattributed. The two mark cites agree with pmarks (SAMEKH after 36:19 and PE after 36:21, both single-witness, neither one a double-mark verse). Chapter 36 lies outside both dual-cite zones, and MT and WEB both run 23 verses with content aligned at every edge I sampled, so the row's bare oshb refs are numerically right and no dual-cite is owed. What does not survive inspection is the morphology behind the opening warrant. וַיַּ֨עַל is Hiphil 3ms and its subject is still YHWH, carried from וַיִּשְׁלַ֡ח יְהוָה֩ in v15; the Chaldean king enters as the object marked by את (אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים), and YHWH is subject again at the verse's close, הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ. The king becomes subject only later in the verse, at וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג. Two root echoes bind v17 backwards over the seam instead of breaking at it: חמל surfaces book-wide in just two verses, v15's כִּֽי חָמַ֥ל עַל עַמּ֖וֹ answered by v17's וְלֹ֥א חָמַ֛ל; עלה likewise carries v16's עַ֠ד עֲל֧וֹת חֲמַת יְהוָ֛ה into v17's wayyiqtol. A tier-1 opener of better quality sits unused one clause earlier, in v16's terminal עַד לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא. Internally the row waves off the 19/20 split on the ground that one Chaldean agent governs both halves, but the finite verbs change number at exactly that point, and the closural superlative is asserted rather than tested. The span may well be right; the reasons given for it are not the reasons the Hebrew supplies.

challenges.claim: The opening warrant states that ‘a previously unnamed agent enters’ at v17, but the verse's first finite verb וַיַּ֨עַל is Hiphil 3ms continuing YHWH as subject from v15 (וַיִּשְׁלַ֡ח יְהוָה֩); the Chaldean king is the את-marked object אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים, and YHWH resumes as subject at הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ — tier-1, the text's own participant syntax. The Babylonian king is moreover named four times earlier in this same chapter (נבוכדנאצר at 36:6, 36:7, 36:10, 36:13; consonantal sweep of 2Chr_oshb.txt), so only the gentilic designation is new here, and it stands at 36:17 as ketiv כשדיים / qere כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים, which the row does not disclose. Two catchwords cross the seam rather than mark it: חמל occurs in all of 2Chr only at 36:15 (כִּֽי חָמַ֥ל עַל עַמּ֖וֹ) and 36:17 (וְלֹ֥א חָמַ֛ל), and עלה links v16's עַ֠ד עֲל֧וֹת חֲמַת יְהוָ֛ה to v17's וַיַּ֨עַל.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-ground the opening on v16's terminal tier-1 clause עַד לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא (in 2Chr only here and at 21:18, לָחֳלִ֖י לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא, both at points of irreversible ruin) together with the shift from prophetic-messenger action to military execution; restate or drop the ‘previously unnamed agent’ sentence so that it describes an object-position introduction of a new gentilic, and disclose the ketiv/qere.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative dismisses a vv17-19 / vv20-21 split because ‘the same Chaldean agent still governs both halves.’ The Hebrew contradicts that at the proposed seam: v19's destruction verbs are 3mp (וַֽיִּשְׂרְפוּ֙ ... וַֽיְנַתְּצ֔וּ ... שָׂרְפ֣וּ) while v20 opens 3ms with וַיֶּ֛גֶל, whose singular referent is confirmed by וַֽיִּהְיוּ ל֤וֹ וּלְבָנָיו֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים. A change of subject number is a tier-1 participant signal and it falls precisely where the rival boundary is drawn, independent of the tier-3 SAMEKH keyed to 36:19 (single-witness). The rival is therefore stronger than the row concedes.
challenges.suggested_action: Rewrite the rejected alternative so it engages the 3mp→3ms shift, and reject the split on a ground the Hebrew does supply — that v21 is an infinitive-construct continuation of v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל and cannot be detached from it — or else re-open 19/20 as a live option.

challenges.claim: ‘The fulfillment clause is the strongest formal closer anywhere in this exile-compression stretch’ is a scoped universal the row never tests, and a programmatic sweep tells against it on formal grounds: למלאות occurs in 2Chr only inside 36:21 itself (both tokens, לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ and לְמַלֹּ֖אות שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה), so it is not a recurring closural device at all, whereas the same stretch contains 36:8, וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהֽוֹיָקִ֜ים ... הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים, the tenth and final member of the ויתר דברי source-citation series (13:22, 20:34, 25:26, 26:22, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:18, 35:26, 36:8) that book_strategy_draft.md section 1 classes as a strong unit-closer, doubled there by the succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו.
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the superlative to what is demonstrable — that v21 is the strongest closer still available at this point, the source-citation series having already terminated at 36:8 — and mirror oshb:2Chr.36.8 into boundary_evidence_refs as the compared specimen.

challenges.claim: v20's Hebrew is argued in the rationale (עַד מְלֹ֖ךְ מַלְכ֥וּת פָּרָֽס, byte-exact and unique to oshb:2Chr.36.20), yet oshb:2Chr.36.20 is missing from boundary_evidence_refs; oshb:2Chr.36.18 is likewise absent although v18's treasury inventory is described as a movement of the unit. Both WEB counterparts are present, so the omission is one-sided, and book_strategy_draft.md section 7 requires every argued comparandum mirrored into the refs array.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Chr.36.20 and oshb:2Chr.36.18 to boundary_evidence_refs.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both edges hold up on inspection: v16 closes the messengers-scorned scene on its own tier-1 completion note (עַד לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא, 'until there was no remedy'), and v17's naming of 'the king of the Chaldeans' is a genuine first-mention participant entry, not a mid-scene continuation, matching the device matrix's scene/participant-change category cleanly. The v21 close is the strongest available stop: the purpose-clause fulfillment formula has no rival closer downstream before v22's fresh dating formula, and the row is honest that this stretch sits in the strategy's flagged 36:11-21 low-confidence zone rather than overclaiming certainty. Where the row falls short is bookkeeping rather than boundary logic: it quotes Hebrew from v20 to carry part of the argument but never cites that verse as evidence.

challenges.claim: The rationale quotes v20's Hebrew clause עַד מְלֹ֖ךְ מַלְכ֥וּת פָּרָֽס ('until the reign of the kingdom of Persia') as part of the boundary argument, but boundary_evidence_refs contains no oshb:2Chr.36.20 entry — only .16, .17, .19 (samekh), .21 (pe), and .22 are listed, so the quoted form is left uncited even though it is doing evidentiary work in the prose.
challenges.suggested_action: Add 'oshb:2Chr.36.20' to boundary_evidence_refs to back the quoted Hebrew form already used in the rationale.

primary_reviews.rationale: Twenty-two Hebrew strings collate byte-exact, the largest quote load in this cluster, and the row's checkable book-level claims all hold: מרפא twice in 2Chr, Nebuchadnezzar four times in chapter 36 before v17, the citation series ten members long and closing at 36:8. Both the SAMEKH and PE disclosures match pmarks at 36:19 and 36:21. The number shift the rewritten alternative concedes is genuine — v19's three destruction verbs are plural, v20 opens singular, and וַֽיִּהְיוּ ל֤וֹ וּלְבָנָיו֙ confirms the referent. What fails is the ground chosen to defeat that rival. The row asserts a dependency for the wrong one of v21's two infinitives, then denies the verse any independent clause, a denial its own cluster-mate contradicts on the same verse. That, plus the still-missing original-language ref and a line of drafting history left sitting inside the rationale, is what I file. The span 36:17-21 remains defensible; the reasoning holding vv20-21 to it needs re-anchoring.

challenges.claim: The rewritten dependency argument attaches the wrong infinitive and then overstates. oshb:2Chr.36.21 runs לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ עַד רָצְתָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתֶ֑יהָ כָּל יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙ שָׁבָ֔תָה לְמַלֹּ֖אות שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה — two occurrences of למלאות, not one. The row quotes the verse-final לְמַלֹּ֖אות שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה and says it depends on v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל, but that token stands immediately after שָׁבָ֔תָה and completes it; the infinitive reaching back to v20 is the verse-initial לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ. The rejected alternative compounds this by saying v21 “supplies no independent clause of its own”, which is false: שָׁבָ֔תָה is a finite qal perfect governed by the subject כָּל יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙, and M8-2Chr-170 in this cluster identifies כָּל יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙ שָׁבָ֔תָה as v21's one truly independent clause. Since the dependency is this row's sole stated ground for holding vv20-21 together against the 19/20 rival, two frozen rows now contradict each other precisely where the argument bears weight.
challenges.suggested_action: Quote לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ as the token riding v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל, and drop the claim that v21 has no independent clause — concede שָׁבָ֔תָה and argue instead that a verse opening on a bare purpose infinitive cannot head a unit, which defeats the 19/20 split without colliding with M8-2Chr-170.

primary_reviews.rationale: Four of five items are fully cured on the exact Hebrew requested, and I independently re-ran the underlying sweeps (חמל, למלאות, four Nebuchadnezzar citations, both marks) and they all check out. Two things still need attention: OL-169-4's citation fix is incomplete (oshb:36.18 never made it into the refs despite v18 being argued in the text), and a claim added to reinforce the v19/v20 number-shift argument -- that וַֽיִּהְיוּ 'confirms' a singular subject at v20 -- is itself grammatically backward, since that verb is 3mp throughout the book and the row's own English gloss even reads it as 'they.' challenges.claim: OL-M8-2Chr-169-4 asked for both oshb:2Chr.36.20 and oshb:2Chr.36.18 to be added to boundary_evidence_refs. Only oshb:2Chr.36.20 was added; oshb:2Chr.36.18 is still absent, even though the row's own prose still treats v18 ('the seizure of every treasury') as part of the unit's movement, and web:2Chr.36.18 is present in the refs while its oshb counterpart is not.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Chr.36.18 to boundary_evidence_refs to complete the fix already begun for oshb:2Chr.36.20.

challenges.claim: The row states the pivot to a singular subject at v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל is 'confirmed singular by וַֽיִּהְיוּ ל֤וֹ וּלְבָנָיו֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים, "they were servants to him and his sons"'. וַֽיִּהְיוּ is itself 3mp -- 'and they were' -- not singular, and the row's own gloss translates it as plural. A sweep of the same wayyiqtol form elsewhere in the book (2Chr.5.8, 13.13, 20.25, 24.12, 24.14) shows it is always plural, and WEB's own translation of v20 keeps the same split ('he carried... away... and they were servants'). A plural verb describing the deported remnant cannot confirm the number of the earlier, grammatically unrelated 3ms וַיֶּ֛גֶל.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the 'confirmed singular by וַֽיִּהְיוּ' clause, or redirect the point to the singular pronominal suffix in ל֤וֹ ('to him'), which is the element that actually continues a singular referent into the clause.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The citation-hygiene items converge into one fix: LF's flag that עַד מְלֹ֖ךְ מַלְכ֥וּת פָּרָֽס, ‘until the reign of the kingdom of Persia’, is quoted mid-rationale with no matching oshb:2Chr.36.20 ref is confirmed byte-exact against the source line, and it is the same gap OL's fourth item names. One remedy covers both — add oshb:2Chr.36.20. OL's companion ask for oshb:2Chr.36.18 does not clear the same bar: no Hebrew from v18 is quoted or compared anywhere in the rationale (only an English gloss of the treasury inventory is used), and web:2Chr.36.18 is already present in the refs array, so that half is a correction rather than a clean support. The three grammar-level items are the substantial ones and all confirm under my own slicing. וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים opens as Hiphil, not with the king as a new grammatical subject: וַיִּשְׁלַ֡ח יְהוָה֩ supplies the last overt subject before the seam, the king sits in the את-marked object slot, and הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ returns to that same subject at the verse's close — so 'a previously unnamed agent enters' overstates what the syntax shows, and the row's own English rendering ('he brought up against them the king') already concedes as much without the prose noticing the tension. Two catchwords do cross the seam rather than mark it: the root חמל surfaces in 2Chr only at כִּֽי חָמַ֥ל עַל עַמּ֖וֹ and וְלֹ֥א חָמַ֛ל, and עלה links עַ֠ד עֲל֧וֹת חֲמַת יְהוָ֛ה to the seam's own וַיַּ֨עַל. Neither the ketiv/qere pair underlying כשדיים (ketiv, bare) / כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים (qere, pointed) at v17, nor any of this, is disclosed in the row. Separately, v19's destruction verbs (וַֽיִּשְׂרְפוּ֙, וַֽיְנַתְּצ֔וּ, שָׂרְפ֣וּ) are all 3mp while v20 opens 3ms with וַיֶּ֛גֶל, confirmed singular by וַֽיִּהְיוּ ל֤וֹ וּלְבָנָיו֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים — a real participant-number shift sitting exactly where the row dismisses a 19/20 split on the ground that 'the same Chaldean agent still governs both halves.' And the claim that v21's fulfillment clause is 'the strongest formal closer anywhere in this exile-compression stretch' does not survive a sweep: למלאות occurs only inside v21 itself (לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ and לְמַלֹּ֖אות שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה), while the ויתר דברי source-citation formula — which book_strategy_draft.md §1 itself names among the strong unit-closers — already terminated the same 36:1-21 stretch at 36:8, its tenth attestation in the book. None of this overturns the v17-21 span by itself: v16's own terminal עַד לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא (paralleled in 2Chr only at 21:18's לָחֳלִ֖י לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא) is a real alternative anchor for the same opening edge, and the syntactic dependency surfaced under decision 170 (v21's purpose clause rides on v20's finite verb) is in fact a cleaner reason to reject the 19/20 split than the 'same agent' line the row gives. This is a confidence question, not a span override: the row's own medium rating already carries the strategy's 36:11-21 low-confidence flag, and these findings show the stated grounds for that medium call are weaker than the boundary they defend, worth a second look at the author round.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both Hebrew citations here collate byte-exact and each is unique in the book. Most of the device claims hold: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס does open v22, and בשנת with or without prefixed waw heads a dated notice in eight verses of 2Chr (3:2, 13:1, 16:1, 16:12, 16:13, 17:7, 34:8, 36:22, consonantal sweep), the last of them here — though not every instance is unit-initial (16:12 and 17:7 date events inside a reign), so the formula corroborates this seam rather than settling it alone. The third-person to first-person pivot is exactly as described: כֹּה אָמַ֞ר כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ introduces the edict, after which the speaker says נָ֣תַן לִ֗י and פָקַ֤ד עָלַי֙. Mark cites match pmarks (PE keyed to 36:21, SAMEKH keyed to 36:22, single-witness, neither doubled), and no dual-cite is owed in this chapter. Two statements about the Hebrew nonetheless fail. The closing form וְיָֽעַל is not an imperative: it is third masculine singular and apocopated — waw plus shewa, qamets under the yod in pause, no final ה, against the long imperfect יעלה — hence a jussive, which the row's own gloss ‘let him go up’ in fact renders correctly. And the rejected alternative leans on v21's fulfillment clause being ‘already a complete sentence,’ which it is not. The 21/22 boundary is sound and the closing edge is the end of the book; the corrections run to the reasoning, not to the span.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative asserts that ‘v21's own fulfillment clause is already a complete sentence without it.’ It is not: the fulfillment clause is לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ, the preposition lamed plus the Piel infinitive construct למלאות, which carries no finite verb and depends on v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל. The only independent finite clause anywhere in v21 is כָּל יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙ שָׁבָ֔תָה, and that is not the fulfillment clause; the other perfect, רצתה, sits inside an עד clause. Tier-1, read off the verse's own syntax. The error runs against the row's own interest, since v21's dependence on v20 is itself a reason v22 has to begin fresh.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate the rejected alternative on the syntax the verse actually has: v21 is an infinitival continuation of v20 and cannot host a regnal dating formula, so folding v22 backwards would attach an independent dated notice to a dependent purpose clause.

challenges.claim: ‘Closing on its final imperative’ misclassifies וְיָֽעַל. A Hebrew imperative is second person; this form is third masculine singular and apocopated — codepoints vav, shewa, yod, qamets, meteg, ayin, patah, lamed — that is, the short jussive יעל in pause, not the long imperfect יעלה, and it carries conjunctive waw rather than the waw-patah plus doubling of a wayyiqtol (contrast וַיַּ֨עַל at 36:17 in this same cluster). The clause is a protasis-apodosis close, מִֽי בָכֶ֣ם מִכָּל עַמּ֗וֹ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהָ֛יו עִמּ֖וֹ וְיָֽעַל, which is itself a listed tier-1 device.
challenges.suggested_action: Relabel the closing device as a third-person jussive inside a protasis-apodosis frame rather than an imperative; the English gloss already in the row needs no change.

A span-internal tier-3 mark cannot corroborate the unit it sits inside; the most it could do, if it drove anything, is exert weak pressure toward separating the quoted edict, a tension the row does not disclose. The mark that genuinely bears on the opening edge is the PE keyed to 36:21 (single-witness), already carried in the refs.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the SAMEKH sentence as an internal narration-to-speech hinge observation, with an explicit note that it does not corroborate the unit's boundaries, and let the 36:21 PE carry the tier-3 corroboration for the 21/22 seam.

The strongest_rejected_alternative, though, only tests the merge-with-v21 option on syntactic grounds ('v21's own fulfillment clause is already a complete sentence without it') and never engages the strongest textual reason someone might actually propose that merge: v22 carries its own fulfillment-of-Jeremiah clause that is a near-verbatim echo of v21's. primary_reviews.rationale: The cleanest row in the cluster after revision, and every correction it was asked to make survives independent checking. Eleven Hebrew strings collate byte-exact. Both mark disclosures match pmarks — PE keyed to 36:21, SAMEKH keyed to 36:22 — and the row places each correctly relative to the span, which is what the third first-round item turned on. The jussive analysis is confirmed at codepoint level, including apocopation and the absent doubling that separates וְיָֽעַל from the wayyiqtol it is contrasted with. Its reading of v21 is correct on inspection and, notably, is the reading this cluster's M8-2Chr-169 fails to reproduce; where the two rows disagree about that verse, this one has the text on its side. The lexical echo between the two fulfillment clauses is real, four words shared, and the answer given to it — that v22 anchors on its own finite הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה while v21's rides a verb in the preceding verse — is accurate and sufficient. peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both mark cites and both Hebrew citations here collate clean, and the challenge set converges on one real problem in the rejected_alternative's single sentence rather than on the boundary itself. LF is right that the row asserts v22's Jeremiah-fulfillment framing without ever quoting its own clause, לִכְל֥וֹת דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ, leaving the near-verbatim echo with v21's לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ untested against the merge case it exists to rebut. OL is separately right that the row's actual sentence — 'v21's own fulfillment clause is already a complete sentence without it' — is not merely under-argued but false: לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ is a bare Piel infinitive construct carrying no finite verb of its own, and the one truly independent clause anywhere in v21, כָּל יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙ שָׁבָ֔תָה, is not the fulfillment clause at all (the other perfect, inside עַד רָצְתָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתֶ֑יהָ, sits in its own עד-clause). These two findings reconcile into a single fix rather than two: the fulfillment clause in v21 rides as a purpose-infinitive on v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל, and v22's own near-identical clause rides the same way on its own later finite verb, הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה — two parallel but syntactically independent frames bracketing the exile's start and the return's start respectively. That is why the echo reads as deliberate bracketing rather than grounds for folding v22 backward, and it is this syntax, not the sentence-completeness claim as written, that should carry the rejected_alternative once revised. Separately, 'closing on its final imperative' misnames וְיָֽעַל: the form is a third-person apocopated jussive carrying simple conjunctive waw, contrasting with the wayyiqtol doubling pattern the same root shows at v17's וַיַּ֨עַל in the sibling decision, and Hebrew imperatives are second person only in any case — the row's own gloss 'let him go up' already reads it correctly even though the label does not. And the SAMEKH the row features trails v22 — by the same trailing-mark convention the row itself applies to 169's SAMEKH-after-19 and PE-after-21 — so it falls between v22 and v23, inside this span rather than at either outer edge; the PE keyed to v21, already carried in the refs, is what actually corroborates the opening seam, and the row does not disclose that the mark it foregrounds is span-internal. Taken together, three of the row's four supporting claims about its own Hebrew need correction even though the span itself — a fresh dating formula, the person-pivot into direct speech, the literal end of the book — still reads soundly. That is a confidence question for the author round: 'high' rests partly on grounds that do not hold as written, even though nothing here argues for a different span.
